News.title: England cruise to victory led by ‘absolute freak’ Brook
News.content:
As Brendon McCullum watched from the England balcony with the newest member of his think tank, Kevin Pietersen, their captain Harry Brook put on a brutal display that married the best of those two great T20 batsmen. To McCullum’s pure aggression and power, Brook added Pietersen’s flair and sheer range of strokes.

Brook made 114 from 49 balls, his second ton in T20 internationals and his first in any format this summer, as his team continues to take shape. They smashed 254 for four from their 20 overs, setting up a win by 119 runs. Under Brook, England have now won 19 of their 22 completed T20s.

Brook said he and Pietersen have had a “couple of conversations”. But in the idle hours before this match, “I was actually watching his highlights earlier on my phone”. He added that Pietersen “was a phenomenal player”; his influence on his batting is clear, and will only grow now they are working together.

It proved the perfect warm-up. This was the second time he and his predecessor Jos Buttler have wrought utter carnage on this ground this summer. Against India in July, they racked up 257 for three, with that pair sharing 233. Then, Buttler made a big hundred, with Brook finishing 95 not out, having been starved of the strike. This time, Buttler made 80 as they put on only 128 from 60 balls, and they fell just short of the team score from July, but it was still their fourth highest ever. Brook, meanwhile, made sure he got to three figures, reflecting ruefully afterwards that he had “let myself down a couple of times” this summer, letting opportunities for big scores go.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit 19-year high as global bond rout intensifies
News.content:
The cost of UK government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007 in a fresh global debt sell-off.

The yield on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, rose from 5.37pc to a fresh 19-year high of 5.41pc on Tuesday as rising oil prices risk reigniting inflation.

Mortgage experts have warned that residential and buy-to-let mortgage rates are set to climb towards 5pc, as market turmoil threatens to filter through to household finances.

Short-term debt costs have also jumped, with the yield on two-year UK bonds surpassing 4.9pc for the first time in three years.

The bond chaos came as Andy Haldane, a former Bank of England chief economist, warned that Labour risked becoming “just a traditional tax and spend socialist government with better TikTok videos”.

He told LBC that John Healey’s original plan for a “low drama budget” had been “torpedoed” by higher borrowing costs and “events over the last couple of weeks”.

He said: “I think that [the bond market turmoil] will mean some hard choices next month at the Budget.”

“Few hard choices so far, but one is looming on the horizon, how any hole to the budget headroom is made good on. Is that a question of tax rises, or is it a question of taking the knife to public spending.”

Mr Haldane has been advising Labour since Andy Burnham took power.

It comes as the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England face pressure to raise interest rates this week to combat rising prices.

Anthony Brinkman, a portfolio manager at Principal Asset Management, said: “The recent gilt market movements seem to be intent on showing central banks they are out of time – the market is expecting action.”

Borrowing costs around the world are rising after a 20pc surge in oil prices so far this month.

Brent crude tipped above $109 a barrel this week after Houthi rebels in Yemen, considered a proxy for Iran’s forces, seized control of a key port in the Red Sea, threatening shipping.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates on Wednesday in the face of the inflation threat.

As a result, the yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds has surged above 5pc for the first time since 2007.

News.title: AI could transform global inequalities or ‘widen the gap’, warns Bill Gates
News.content:
“AI could be a great equaliser, or [it could] widen the gap”, says Mr Gates. “This is not a long-range prediction. It’s a present-tense choice”.

“We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident. After all, the market is an extraordinary engine of innovation, but a terrible guarantor of equal opportunity.

“With AI, the gap could grow even faster … That is what makes this moment so urgent. Things are changing rapidly, and the window to shape who benefits from AI, and how soon, is short”.

The key issue holding back the deployment of AI in the developing world revolves around the availability of local data and, in turn, the ability for the technology to scale in environments very different from where it is currently being created.

An app that is trained on billions of hours of American English, will struggle at first with British English (see your spell check) but is next to useless if your local language is Swahili or Chichewa.

More profoundly, an AI tool that allows a farmer in Hampshire to control his combine harvester remotely, will offer little to a smallholder in South Sudan who works the land by hand and faces a completely different array of pests, weather conditions and costs.

The same is true for health. “A community health worker in Rwanda examining a baby with a fever faces different questions than a clinician in a well-resourced hospital - and the AI supporting her needs to reflect that”, says Mr Gates.

He adds: “Most of the world is invisible to today’s AI models. These AI systems were trained primarily on what exists on the internet – and the internet reflects a deeply unequal world. More than 90 percent of the data used to train early, large language models came from English-language sources. The communities that stand the most to gain from AI are largely absent from the knowledge base these tools are built on. They are not just underserved. They are not in the picture at all”.

The new investment aims to help correct that. Mark Suzman, CEO of the Gates Foundation, says investments are already being made with companies including Microsoft and Google to build databases of a much wider range of languages, for instance.

Africa alone has more than 2,000 languages, and for AI’s to be effective there they have to understand what and how people actually speak - “their dialects, accents, and slang, too”.

The investments, he says, are being made on the condition that the intelligence and knowledge they accumulate are made freely available for others to use.

Languages for AI “are true public goods, almost definitional public goods. They need to be freely available to everybody. Once they’re created, they are public goods that can be uploaded onto any AI,” said Mr Suzman.

News.title: Reynolds refuses four times to rule out tax raid on state pensioners
News.content:
The Business Secretary refused four times to rule out retirees paying tax on the state pension from next year.

Jonathan Reynolds declined to reassure pensioners that they would not pay income tax on the benefit for the first time, saying it was a question for the Chancellor.

The comments on Tuesday raised concern for millions of retired people expecting to see their state pension surpass £13,000 from April, forcing them to pay income tax.

However, pensions minister Torsten Bell later insisted Labour would not put up taxes on people who rely on the state pension.

It is still unclear how this will be implemented given the complexity of separating the tax arrangements of different groups of pensioners.

The rise under the triple lock guarantee would drag many pensioners into paying income tax for the first time because their state income would surpass the personal allowance of £12,570.

Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, said last year that people solely reliant on the state pension would not have to pay the tax.

However, Mr Reynolds was repeatedly asked on BBC Breakfast whether Labour would honour this commitment after the next increase in the state pension in April. He declined to answer four times.

He said: “I’m sorry, that is for the Chancellor and for a Budget.

“The majority of pensioners in this country don’t just rely on the state pensions. Some do, I accept that, but the majority don’t.

“Sometimes when this is looked at, we’re focusing just on the state pension side of this. You’ve got to consider the full range of income retired people in the UK have.”

However Mr Bell, the pensions minister, walked back from Mr Reynolds comments.

He said: “In line with the commitment made at Budget 2025, pensioners who only just exceed the personal allowance will not have the administrative burden of paying small amounts of tax in this Parliament.

“The Chancellor will set out further details on how that commitment will be delivered at the Budget.”

Former pensions minister Sir Steve Webb said only one in 16 pensioners would benefit from this policy.

He said: “Those on the new state pension can expect to see an increase of nearly £500 per year next April.

“But the sting in the tail is that this will take the standard rate of the new state pension above the tax threshold.”

The comments came after official figures on Tuesday indicated the triple lock will rise by 3.9pc from April.

Under the triple lock, the state pension rises each April in line with inflation, average wages or 2.5pc, whichever is highest.

Total pay, including bonuses, rose by 3.9pc in the three months to July, down from 4.2pc in the three months to June.

Pensioners may yet receive a bigger increase if September’s inflation figure is higher than 3.9pc. That will be revealed next month but a higher figure is thought to be unlikely.

News.title: Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon
News.content:
The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Sports.title: Pioneer behind Sunderland’s Stadium of Light in ‘fantasy land’ after booking Europa League trip to Milan
Sports.content:
SIR BOB MURRAY built the ground fit to stage European football.

The 80-year-old, however, admits he never envisioned his beloved Black Cats playing in Europe there.



Murray, the son of a Sunderland coal miner, began his love affair with the club “from birth” and it blossomed with every visit to Roker Park.

Like every boy, he grew up hoping to one day play there while watching on from the Fulwell End. Instead, he went on to OWN them.



Before replacing Tom Cowie as chairman in 1986, the lifelong fan had watched his team win the 1973 FA Cup but missed out on the resulting European campaign.

Attempting to cash in on the excitement of a first foray in the European Cup Winner’s Cup, the club controversially doubled the usual £1 a seat and 50p standing tickets for the visit of Hungarian side Vasas Budapest.

A backlash led to a disappointing turnout of just 22,762 fans to see their side win the second leg 2-0 and advance in their first European game.

A price reduction for the next round worked. And 31,568 watched Sunderland beat Sporting Lisbon at Roker Park, though they were eventually eliminated after losing 2-0 in the return leg.

Murray, an accountant by trade but who made his fortune in kitchen manufacturing, may not have witnessed his heroes in Europe. But upon taking charge, he set out to get them back to the big time.

They came close on a hat-trick of occasions during his 20-year tenure. The first losing the 1992 FA Cup Final before back-to-back seventh place finishes at the turn of the century under Peter Reid’s legendary side.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Finally, this week he gets his wish. And the waterworks began when he spotted the current French-Swiss owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus at the Arsenal game.

Murray said: “I just walked up to the owners on Saturday and gave them a big hug and said, ‘Thank you.’ Simple as that. I’m in awe of them.

“My dad was a Sunderland coal miner. I used to come to the game with him. I’d get the service bus and Jackie White’s Market and get a saveloy. That’s what we did.

“Now I’ve booked tickets for Milan! Unbelievable, really. A few years ago, you’d never have seen this, would you?



“This is a one-off at the moment. I pinch myself about the whole thing, the profile for the city, everything.”

Murray has seen numerous owners come-and go since he sold up in 2006. As the club began to slide, he was even banned from attending games at one point by American Ellis Short after hitting out at the mis-management.

But even in those dark days his love for Sunderland never swayed. Murray founded the Foundation of Light and its award-winning home, the Beacon of Light, in the city. The award-winning community, education, and sports hub that provides local services and funds the Foundation of Light charity is about to celebrate its 25th anniversary.



And it was here that Murray remains hard at work trying to change the lives of others in the North East.

SUNDERLAND EURO MESSAGE Club statement Wednesday’s UEFA Europa League fixture against AZ Alkmaar will be a historic occasion for Sunderland AFC, marking the Club’s first European home fixture in 53 years. With supporters travelling from the Netherlands to experience the occasion, we are looking forward to welcoming AZ Alkmaar, its players and supporters to Sunderland and the Stadium of Light.

As part of their visit, a number of AZ Alkmaar supporters will take part in a planned march to the Stadium of Light. The march, which will commence at 5.30pm approximately, will use the Keel Crossing as supporters make their way towards the stadium. As a result, the Keel Crossing may be temporarily closed for a short period to allow the march to pass safely. Supporters and members of the public are asked to be aware of a potential brief delay when using the crossing. It will reopen as soon as it is safe to do so. After 53 years without European football at the Stadium of Light, Wednesday represents an important moment in the Club’s history and an opportunity for Sunderland to showcase itself on the European stage. We want the occasion to be remembered for the right reasons and ask all supporters to welcome our visitors and enjoy the occasion responsibly.

He says: “That’s been my privilege. I’ve done that through choice. I got out of bed and came here for a 12-hour day, and I want to do that. I don’t get money out of it. I’m very lucky and fortunate in life. Some people around here, not so fortunate.”

The Beacon of Light sits next to his other pride and joy – the Stadium of Light. He paid £25m, “not even enough to buy a full-back these days,” to build the ground in 1997.

He spared no cost in getting it up to Uefa four-star level. That was in order to achieve his ambition of hosting the England national team rather than thinking about the Black Cats making a European return.

He added: “That’s beyond living in fantasyland. Kyril and the guys have taken the club with no raw material, nothing in the academy. They bought the club at the lowest point of its history and within a very short time they’ve had tremendous success.”



Five years ago Sunderland were hosting Accrington Stanley in League One. Now, after two promotions in three years and finishing seventh on their return to the top-flight, there will be a full house to see AZ Alkmaar tonight.

Kevin Phillips won the European Golden Shoe during Murray’s reign as part of those consecutive top seven finishes.

That team is still considered by many to be the best of Sunderland’s modern-era. But the former striker says Regis Le Bris’ men have undoubtedly taken that crown.



Speaking to Sun Sport via BestBettingSites.co.uk, he said: “They’ll be talked about now for the rest of Sunderland’s history for having secured European football at the Stadium of Light.

“We got very close but didn’t quite get there. But these boys have done it.

“They deserve all the credit that comes their way and will become legends of the football club without a shadow of a doubt. And they could go even further if they were to go on and have a decent run in the Europa and stay in the Premier League again.”

Sports.title: Chelsea star goes from World Cup to EFL Trophy humiliation within weeks after summer from hell
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S kids fell to an EFL Cup defeat to League One Wycombe.

A much-changed academy side, with a number of big names missing, competed well at Adams Park, having won their opening group game on penalties against Bristol Rovers.



But the Blues faded after the break and conceded twice to Mohamed Keita and then late with Caolan Boyd-Munce finding the back of the net.

Harrison Bettoni grabbed a Chelsea goal during injury time but the visitors lacked attacking threat for the most part. SunSport runs you through three things we learned…



IN MORE ways than one, Chelsea’s kids were mirroring Xabi Alonso‘s first team.

The shape here at Adams Park was very similar to that which the Spaniard has been using since arriving at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea’s back four quickly became a five when they were out of possession, with winger Sol Gordon playing the Pedro Neto role of tucking in at wing-back before having to dash forwards when on the ball.

There was a reflection of the first team too in that they could not match up defending and attacking.

Despite conceding twice, they looked rather more stable at the back, a goalkeeping blunder aside, especially compared to Alonso’s men, with Justin Osagie standing out and his partner Dante Waite not afraid of a challenge.

But going forwards they lacked a cutting edge, very much in contrast to the seniors.

Sports.title: Premier League cult hero, 47, reveals he helped rescue Wrexham from oblivion before Ryan Reynolds takeover
Sports.content:
CRAIG BELLAMY has revealed how he once donated money to Wrexham to help save the Welsh club from dropping out of the Football League.

The Wales boss was defending his commitment to his country after revealing he rejected the chance to become Burnley manager this summer.



Bellamy said in a Wales press conference ahead of the upcoming Nations League matches: “I donated money to Wrexham (in 2007).

“They stayed in the league. So my commitment with Wales, I don’t believe I have to ever try and win anyone over with that. It’s there.”



Bellamy’s intervention came in March 2007, when Wrexham were second-bottom of League Two and fighting desperately to preserve their Football League status.

The then-Liverpool striker made what the club described as a “very generous donation,” with the exact sum never publicly disclosed.



The cash allowed Wrexham to bring in THREE loan players before the transfer deadline, and they stayed up.

Bellamy said at the time that, as a “proud Welshman and supporter of Welsh football”, it was important to him that Wrexham retained their Football League place.

His intervention helped them do exactly that, with the Red Dragons eventually surviving on the final day of the 2006-07 season.

But their reprieve proved temporary and Wrexham were relegated to non-league the following year.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

They spent a painful 15 YEARS outside the EFL before their fortunes were transformed by two unlikely figures from Hollywood.

Deadpool star Ryan Reynolds and It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia creator Rob McElhenney completed their takeover in February 2021, buying the club from the Wrexham Supporters Trust and initially investing £2million.

Their extraordinary project – chronicled around the world through hit documentary Welcome to Wrexham – eventually produced one of English football’s most remarkable rises.

Under boss Phil Parkinson, Wrexham won the National League with 111 points in 2023 to finally return to the Football League.

They did not stop there, earning promotion from League Two at the first attempt before finishing second in League One in 2024-25.



Wrexham narrowly missed out on the Championship play-offs in their first season back in the second tier and remain there this season.

Sports.title: DAZN host Diletta Leotta shows off curves in translucent top as fans say ‘what a lucky man Karius is’
Sports.content:
DILETTA LEOTTA delighted fans with her latest social media snaps.

And followers joked her goalkeeper husband Loris Karius is a very lucky man indeed.



The glamorous Italian DAZN presenter, 35, took to Instagram on Tuesday with a life update.

She posted 14 pictures and one video to her 9.4million followers.



And that included various revealing outfits.

The collection of snaps featured a mix of selfies, at work on and off screen, enjoying family time and even her collection of heels.

Diletta captioned the post: “A little bit of everything I love.”

And as well as racking up nearly 100,000 likes within 11 hours, more than 350 fans flooded the comments section.



One gushed: “Stunning as always.”

Another beamed: “Absolutely stunning, out of this world.”



A third typed: “You are so beautiful.”

A fourth declared: “Diletta Leotta you are perfect.”



And a final user quipped: “@loriskarius YOU ARE THE LUCKIEST MAN IN THE WORLD.”

Diletta, who has worked as a Serie A broadcaster with DAZN since 2018, married Karius in 2024 in Italy.

The ex-Liverpool stopper has two children with Diletta – daughter Aria and son Leonardo.

Sports.title: West Ham 2 Fulham 3: Oscar Bobb takes advantage of Kante error to hand Arbeloa’s strugglers morale-boosting win
Sports.content:
OSCAR BOBB burst West Ham’s bubbles as his 78th-minute winner sent Fulham through.

The second-half sub cashed in after Mo Kante lost possession on the edge of his box to fire past Finlay Herrick.



It was a boost for boss Alvaro Arbeloa on the back of Fulham’s first point of the season — in their fourth league game — at Liverpool.

Championship leaders West Ham twice pegged Fulham back in a thrilling first half.



The visitors took a 13th-minute lead when Rodrigo Muniz planted a header home after Cesar Palacios pulled the ball back.

But West Ham — fresh from beating Wrexham 6-0 on Friday — took just three minutes to level the tie.



Arne Engels’ deep cross was headed back into the danger zone by Konstantinos Mavropanos for Morato to head his first Hammers goal.

Rookie keeper Herrick, 20, then got down well to push a Palacios shot around the post.

But Fulham went route one to restore their lead in the 37th minute.

Joachim Andersen raked a ball forward for Palacios to run on to before shooting past Herrick.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Max Dowman, 16, draws Messi comparisons as Merino shows why Gyokeres has been frozen out
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’s B-team cruised into the fourth round of the League Cup as they brushed Ipswich Town aside in a 4-2 win.

Mikel Arteta made nine changes to his side that beat Sunderland at the weekend, but his heavily-rotated squad still looked like the business at Portman Road.



The Gunners were in control from the off as teen sensation Max Dowman opened the scoring after seven minutes with a terrific solo goal.

The teen sensation bagged a second later in the game alongside goals from Mikel Merino and Noni Madueke.



Arteta will have been chuffed with his team’s showing as they barely had to get out of second gear to find the result.

Here SunSport Arsenal reporter Joshua Hall rates each individual Arsenal performance…

KEPA ARRIZABALAGA – 6

The backup goalkeeper had little to do and will be disappointed not to have kept a clean sheet given Arsenal’s dominance.

MARLI SALMON – 7

A fifth senior appearance for the teenager, who signed his first professional deal last month on his 17th birthday.

Faced a serious battle against Zian Flemming, one that saw him struggle at times, but ultimately came out of it as the winner on the night.

He is so comfortable with the ball at his feet and even when he was almost caught in possession by Marcelino Nunez he had the confidence to get out of trouble and drive into midfield.

GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 8

Made a crucial last-ditch tackle to deny a certain goal from Jaden Philogene.

The Brazilian acted as Salmon’s big brother for most of the game, guiding the teen through the game and sweeping up any little errors he made.

Subbed off at half-time to save his legs after a professional performance.



MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 7

Pushed back into the left-back position despite a great start to the season in midfield.

The 19-year-old slotted straight back into the role with ease and put in another confident performance.

MARTIN ZUBIMENDI – 7

Deployed as a makeshift right-back due to the absences of Ben White and Jurrien Timber.

The biggest compliment would be that it was hard to even tell he was playing in that position as he went about his night with minimal fuss. Assured performance.

BRUNO GUIMARAES – 8

A first start since the Community Shield for the Brazilian, off the back of his stunner off the bench against Sunderland.



His role in Arsenal’s second goal was superb, chasing down the back line like a man possessed to win the ball back high up the pitch.

He and Mikel Merino bossed the midfield behind Dowman to allow the teen to shine.

MIKEL MERINO – 8

The Spaniard was wearing the captain’s armband and put in a performance to match.



He was all over the pitch in his midfield role, dictating play and allowing the players around him to find space off the ball.

His delightful dinked ball into the path of Noni Madueke set up Arsenal’s second goal of the night, while his finish to find the bottom corner for the fourth was brilliant.

MAX DOWMAN – 9

Arteta warned Dowman that he must “earn” his minutes this week, after the 16-year-old was left out of the matchday squad for Sunderland at the weekend.

It took the teenager less than seven minutes to show the Arsenal boss exactly what he can do.

His opening goal was a moment of magic, leaving Cedric Kipre for dead with a cheeky shimmy and sending the keeper the wrong way with a tide finish too.



And he played a crucial role in the second goal too, pressing the goalkeeper to force the loose pass and allow Guimaraes to win the ball back.

His second goal was another example of how composed he is for his age, calmly tucking it into the bottom corner, while his dummy ‘assist’ for Merino’s fourth was another sparkling moment.

Arteta has previously compared Dowman to a young Lionel Messi, and it is genuinely not insane to do so when you see just how talented he is.



NONI MADUEKE – 7

It is fair to say Madueke has faced some criticism for his end product since joining Arsenal last summer, but his finish for the second goal was top tier.

If Madueke can make those moments a more regular feature of his game then his reputation in North London will improve tenfold.

EBERECHI EZE – 6

Back on the left wing, where he will likely play most of his football this season given Arsenal’s lack of depth in that position.

It wasn’t exactly an inspiring performance from the England international, who will have been hoping to bag a goal to show he can do it from out wide.

VIKTOR GYOKERES – 5

The Swede has scarcely been given a chance up top so far this season, with Arteta preferring Kai Havertz to lead his line in every Premier League game.



This performance did little to change that as Gyokeres struggled to be involved in a match that Arsenal dominated once again.

Sports.title: Liverpool told they already have £100m transfer solution as Andoni Iraola message sent
Sports.content:
Liverpool told they already have £100m transfer solution as Andoni Iraola message sent

Trey Nyoni was one of the standout performers for Liverpool in their 3-1 Carabao Cup win over Tottenham, with pundits Jamie Redknapp and Conor Coady tipping the 19-year-old as a potential alternative to £100m-rated Alex Scott

View Image Trey Nyoni has been tipped for a bright future at Liverpool (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

Liverpool have been told why 19-year-old Trey Nyoni could be the long-term solution to the club’s midfield dilemmas. The Reds were heavily linked with signing a new midfielder in the summer transfer window, but chose not to strengthen that area of the squad.

‌



Nyoni was in action for Liverpool on Tuesday night as the Merseyside outfit claimed a 3-1 win over Tottenham Hotspur in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

‌



Andoni Iraola’s side secured the win thanks to goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, with Nyoni also earning plenty of praise for his performance.

‌



Iraola named Nyoni in the starting line-up to face Spurs, and went on to play a key role in the midfield alongside Mac Allister and James McConnell before being substituted around the hour mark.

Liverpool beat Tottenham after stunning Dominik Szoboszlai strike - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Ex-Liverpool star Jamie Redknapp has lauded Nyoni's display for the Reds against Tottenham and explained why he believes the 19-year-old has a promising future ahead in a deeper midfield position.

"I thought he [Nyoni] was excellent in that first half, but he's got a lot to learn in that area, it's a specialised position," Redknapp told Sky Sports.

‌



"He did himself no harm whatsoever. Playing forward, getting the ball into good areas, comfortable on the ball. He's just a really good footballer who just sees the picture.

"He's been a No.10 as a kid, so now he's got to play in that slightly different role where he's got to back people up.

"And he's got to always think that the worst is going to happen on a football field. If he does that, he's going to go a long way."

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool were linked with a number of midfielders throughout the summer transfer window, amongst them Bournemouth star Alex Scott, whom Iraola managed during his tenure with the Cherries.

Reports in recent weeks have suggested that Scott is valued by Bournemouth at approximately £100million, and was linked with Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester United over the summer.

‌



Liverpool academy product and former Everton defender Conor Coady appeared alongside Redknapp for Sky Sports' coverage, and believes Nyoni could emulate Scott's trajectory under Iraola's guidance.

"We see someone like a Trey Nyoni, I'm hoping he goes on and has an incredible Liverpool career, because I really rate him that highly," Coady said.

"He could become that [next Alex Scott], rather than going out and buy someone, he could become that if he learns and takes on everything that Andoni Iraola is trying to do."

Sports.title: Man Utd vs Brighton injury news as 15 players could miss Carabao Cup tie
Sports.content:
Man Utd vs Brighton injury news as 15 players could miss Carabao Cup tie

Manchester United and Brighton both face lengthy injury lists ahead of their Carabao Cup clash at Old Trafford on Wednesday night

View Image Luke Shaw remains an injury doubt for Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United and Brighton will go head-to-head in the Carabao Cup this week, but both teams will have to deal with several injury concerns. The Red Devils will host the Seagulls at Old Trafford in the third round of the League Cup, with a place in the next round up for grabs for both teams.

‌



United were on the receiving end of a 1-0 defeat to Manchester City in the Premier League at the weekend, with Erling Haaland scoring a controversial goal in the Manchester derby.

‌



Michael Carrick will now be focused on the Carabao Cup after spending the last few weeks prioritising the Premier League and Champions League, with both United and Brighton dealing with injury concerns.

‌



United were missing Luke Shaw for the City defeat on Sunday, with the left-back now having sat out the previous two fixtures due to injury.

JJ Gabriel asks to QUIT Man Utd immediately as club left completely stunned READ MORE :

Carrick indicated that he is hopeful Shaw will be fit to take on Brighton, though he stopped short of confirming it.

"He could possibly be fit for Brighton, but it's not clear-cut," Carrick told reporters on Tuesday. "But it's a matter of a few days rather than anything else."

‌



Carlos Baleba has also been absent throughout the campaign so far, having joined United from Brighton earlier in the summer.

Baleba remains out with an ankle problem sustained during his spell with the Seagulls, and while he is edging towards fitness, he will be unavailable to feature against his previous employers.

"He'll be back in and around the group at some point over the next week or so," Carrick said. "So that means, after the internationals, he should be in good shape."

‌



United will also be without Amad Diallo and Matthijs de Ligt, with both players on the road to recovery.

Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel's six next club options as Man Utd forced into losing 'Kid Messi' for free

Manchester United academy prospect JJ Gabriel has told the club he wants to leave with immediate effect and could become a free agent

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel wishes to leave Man United

JJ Gabriel could soon trigger a bidding war after informing Manchester United that he wants to leave the club immediately. The 15‑year‑old is widely regarded as one of the most gifted young players in world football.

‌



He had been due to make his first‑team debut in United's Carabao Cup tie against Brighton on Wednesday, but the escalating situation has cast major doubt over that plan. Gabriel has now asked United to cancel his registration in a shock move that could make him a free agent.

‌



United, who have had him in their system since he was 11, have yet to accept the request. Under current regulations, the 15-year-old remains registered with United until the end of the season.

‌



Premier League rules surrounding players under 17 prevent them from signing professional contracts, and players must also be 16 before they can sign scholarship agreements. Gabriel does not turn 16 until next month.

Should all parties reach an agreement, registrations can be cancelled. The rules state: "If the parties don't agree, then any person involved can also ask the Premier League to provide a binding decision on a termination request."

‌



Should the forward's registration with United be terminated, he would be free to move to another club. Manchester City previously attempted to prise him away from their city rivals and could well revive their interest if the opportunity presents itself.

Several young players have switched between the two Manchester clubs in recent seasons. Most notably, David Eze and Karim Cassim have both made the move to Manchester United from City.

Barcelona and Real Madrid have also been credited with an interest in the youngster and are expected to monitor developments closely. Liverpool could equally look to capitalise on the situation.

Sports.title: Liverpool beat Tottenham after stunning Dominik Szoboszlai strike - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Liverpool booked their place in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup as they survived a late onslaught to beat Tottenham 3-1 and pile more misery on the visitors at Anfield.

Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo had Liverpool in complete control, before Conor Gallagher had Spurs back in the game in the latter stages. But with seconds left, Dominik Szoboszlai scored one of the goals of the season to put them out of sight.

Spurs and Liverpool both had early chances, but Lucas Bergvall was denied by Giorgi Mamardashvili, shortly before Martin Dubravka stopped Lewis Koumas’ efforts. But Mac Allister gave Dubravka no chance in the 21st minute when he fired into the top corner to open the scoring in brilliant fashion.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Roberto De Zerbi's side were made to pay the price for missed chances in the second half when Gakpo lashed in a second shortly after the break. It then looked as if it would be a procession for Liverpool, but Gallagher's header shortly before the 70th minute set up a grandstand finish.

Spurs pushed and pushed for equaliser and were only denied by a stunning Mamardashvili save as the clock ticked down. But any hopes of forcing a penalty shootout were extinguished when Szoboszlai unleashed a ferocious volley from 30 yards to settle the point.

Here are the talking points from Anfield...

‌



WALKING THE WALK

After going public with his ‘sadness’ about not being offered a new contract, Mac Allister knew his performances would immediately be under scrutiny.

Just a day after that very open press conference, the Argentine scored against Atletico Madrid. And as one of the experienced members of a much-changed XI, he provided a moment of real quality to break the deadlock.

View 5 Images Alexis Mac Allister celebrates after opening the scoring for Liverpool vs Tottenham

His season won’t be judged on performances in the early round of the Carabao Cup, but after a difficult 25/26, the early signs are that under Iraola, Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover his form.

‌



Gakpo in the groove

Make that two goals and three assists in five games this season for Gakpo. The fact that just two weeks ago, there was a chance the Dutchman was leaving Anfield now seems difficult to imagine.

Virgil van Dijk made it clear how important his compatriot was to the squad and Anfield bosses should be thanking their lucky stars a deal didn't materialise.

But if transfer speculation was needed to take his game up to the next level, then in the long term it's good news for everyone concerned. He has been one of the standout performers of the early weeks of the season.

View 5 Images Cody Gakpo scored his second goal of the season in the win over Spurs

‌



ALL CHANGE

We all know the Carabao Cup is bottom of Liverpool and Tottenham’s list of priorities this season. But that didn’t make the team selections any less disappointing.

Liverpool need to build some momentum under new boss Iraola, after winning just one of their four league games under the Spaniard. But he decided to make 10 changes to his line-up, despite having until Sunday afternoon to prepare for Bournemouth.

It was a similar story for Tottenham, who made eight changes. If Liverpool wanted to build some momentum, Tottenham just needed a result of any type. And Spurs don’t have European football to contend with.

View 5 Images Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi opted to make eight changes

‌



I’m aware this is all a bit ‘old man shouting at clouds’ and it did give a chance for some very talented youngsters to get minutes, but with a three-week international break on the way, could we have not seen slightly stronger XIs?

Had Tottenham gone stronger from the off, there's a fairly good chance they'd be in the hat for the next round.

NO ROOM FOR RICH!

While De Zerbi was happy to make a host of changes, one he wasn’t willing to make was bringing Richarlison in from the cold.

The Italian has made it clear that he will not play for the club again after turning down a new contract offer in the summer.

‌



View 5 Images Richarlison will not play for Tottenham again according to De Zerbi (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

Richarlison was close to leaving in the summer, but is now set to be a glorified spectator until January.

De Zerbi stuck to his word, but there must have been a slight temptation. In six games against Liverpool as a Tottenham player, he has four goals. That kind of firepower would have been handy tonight at Anfield.

Encouraging signs

I know. Spurs fans won't want to hear this. And at the end of the day, this is another defeat - their third in six games, but in the first half particularly, there were reasons for optimism.

‌



On another day Tottenham went in at the break leading, but Bergvall and Kudus both failed to take excellent chances. Scoring a goal - their first against Premier League opposition all season is another huge positive that De Zerbi has to build on quickly.

On Saturday, they host struggling Aston Villa, where they will hope another positive performance can get their first win of the top-flight campaign.

Sports.title: Max Dowman dazzles for Arsenal in rampant win over Ipswich - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Max Dowman scored twice as Arsenal cruised through to the fourth round of the Carabao Cup with a comfortable 4-2 victory over Ipswich.

The Gunners wonderkid produced two classy goals to sandwich Noni Madueke's strike before Mikel Merino put the icing on the cake prior to a couple of consolation goals from the hosts. It's now seven wins from seven games in all competitions for Arsenal, who are enjoying best start to a season under Mikel Arteta.

Both managers showed where their priorities are with their team selections, as Gary O'Neil made 10 changes to the side who impressively beat Crystal Palace 3-2 away from home on Saturday. Meanwhile, Arteta made nine changes after their hard-fought 2-0 win at Sunderland over the weekend.

Here are five talking points from Portman Road.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. Teenage kicks

On night when one of Arsenal's rivals were faced with losing their teenage sensation, Max Dowman showed why he's got a bright future with the Gunners. His goal to break the deadlock oozed confidence, taking the ball from the toe of Viktor Gyokeres and gliding into the empty space.

Dowman sent Cedric Kipre for a hot dog with a lovely shuffle of his feet before rifling the ball into the back of the Ipswich net. His second goal came just two minutes after the restart and was a more cultured finish.

‌



The 16-year-old stroked the ball home after good work from Martin Zubimendi and put the game to bed. Pre-match, Arteta warned Dowman that he'll need to earn his minutes in the first-team, and he did exactly that with a man-of-the-match performance that boosted his stock.

Should Max Dowman get an England call-up? Have your say in the comments section.

View 5 Images Max Dowman was simply outstanding (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

2. Madueke sends timely reminder

It's been slim pickings for Noni Madueke since he started the Community Shield clash with Manchester City last month. The winger only played 40 minutes of football in Arsenal's next five games, with Bukayo Saka firmly ahead of him in the pecking order.

‌



And while there was a hint of fortune about his goal, Madueke made no mistake to double the Gunners' lead on 16 minutes with an emphatic finish across Christian Walton after a defensive mix-up. Given his lack of game time, the ex-Chelsea star isn't a lock to be named in England squad which will be announced on Friday, but that strike will certainly help his case.

View 5 Images Noni Madueke made it 2-0 (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

3. Zubimendi's new role

First there was Thomas Partey, then Declan Rice and now Martin Zubimendi is Arsenal's next midfielder-turned-right-back. The Spaniard was deployed in a new-look back four after finding minutes hard to come by in his regular position so far this campaign.

With an assist to his name for Dowman's second, the experiment was looking like a success. But Jack Clarke's introduction caused problems for Zubimendi, as he skipped past him to set up Anis Mehmeti for a consolation goal.

‌



View 5 Images Martin Zubimendi started at right-back (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

4. Gyokeres continues goal drought

When Arsenal paid £64million for Viktor Gyokeres little over a year ago, these were the sort of games you'd expect him to sit out. Instead, the striker finds himself playing second fiddle to Kai Havertz and having to feed off scraps.

Gyokeres only managed one shot against a porous Ipswich defence, so no wonder he's still without a goal this season. Unlikely to start against former club Brighton on Saturday, he'll be hoping to find his shooting boots during the international break.

View 5 Images Viktor Gyokeres hasn't scored this season (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

‌



5. Cup wait goes on for Ipswich

Only making it beyond the third round once in the last 15 seasons, the Carabao Cup isn't often a source of joy for Ipswich supporters. And their wait to make another deep run akin to their semi-final exit to Arsenal in 2011 goes on after this comprehensive defeat.

The top priority for O'Neil's side is and always will be survival, of course, but a cup run could've helped inspire a more memorable campaign than when they were last in the top flight. Until they enter the FA Cup in January, it's all on the Premier League.

Sports.title: Chelsea's Cole Palmer banned from Twitch after EA FC 27 stream goes wrong
Sports.content:
Chelsea's Cole Palmer banned from Twitch after EA FC 27 stream goes wrong

Twitch banned Cole Palmer and removed content from his channel at the request of EA Sports as the copyright holder after live streaming FC 27 on Tuesday afternoon

View Image Cole Palmer's Twitch account has been banned for streaming EA FC 27 (Image: Getty Images)

Cole Palmer has called on Twitch to unban his account after streaming EA Sports FC 27 ahead of the game's early access period. Chelsea's number ten broadcast footage of himself opening Ultimate Team packs

‌



Palmer, 24, was live for over an hour, with thousands of viewers watching, before the stream abruptly ended. This year's game does not launch globally until next Friday (September 25), but early access begins at midnight this Friday (September 18), two days after the Web App.

‌



However, anyone watching Palmer play got an even earlier look. EA Sports FC were even watching along at one point.

‌



Man Utd handed new Bruno Fernandes punishment verdict after Man City controversy READ MORE :

Premier League rules clear as JJ Gabriel tells Man Utd he wants to leave immediately READ MORE :

Their official account said in the stream's chat: "Errr Cole, weren't we going to do this a bit later? We'll be live at 6pm UK!" That is when they started their first gameplay livestream.

Palmer has responded with an Instagram story, saying: "I was only giving the people what they wanted... unban me pls," before tagging EA Sports FC and Twitch.

FC 27 news page Fut Sheriff posted about him being banned on the same social media platform, a post that Palmer liked and commented: "We back soon". Several clips and screenshots from his cut-short stream are being shared online.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

At one point during the live stream, Palmer complained that his overall rating had been downgraded this year. He has gone from an 87 to an 85, with the passing and dribbling on his Ultimate Team card dropping by the same amount.

The player also described himself as having "one leg" last season. Palmer missed two months with a groin injury before also fracturing the small toe on his left foot after stubbing it on a door at home.

‌



He missed all but three of the first dozen Premier League matches with his various fitness issues. He returned in December.

Speaking about his injuries during pre-season, Palmer said in Sydney during Chelsea's pre-season tour: "The first few months, with me being injured, I just wanted to go out and play, which I probably shouldn't have done.

"Obviously, I couldn't play how I wanted to play. It was a bad season, personally, with injuries and stuff, but I feel good now. The seven weeks obviously helped. I'm ready to go again.

"I went to Sweden or Denmark, one of those countries, to see a doctor. We did speak about (surgery), but I didn't end up getting it."

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel quit threat is a blow to Man Utd but NOT a seismic setback for Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel quit threat is a blow to Man Utd but NOT a seismic setback for Michael Carrick

The prodigiously talented 15-year-old has shocked the club by asking for his Old Trafford agreement to be cancelled but his request is not overly unusual and will happen more often

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel has asked for his Manchester United registration to be cancelled

The talk about JJ Gabriel’s prodigious talent has been loud for a long time and everything he has done in Manchester United’s youth ranks has suggested the hype could well be justified. Which is why the news he wants to leave United has caused quite a stir.

‌



For every well-publicised prodigy that actually goes on to enjoy a successful professional career at an elite level, there is a well-publicised prodigy who does not make it at an elite level. Always remember that.

‌



A scarily good 15-year-old does not necessarily turn into a scarily good 25-year-old. Freddy Adu was billed as the next Pele when playing in Major League Soccer at the age of 15. At the age of 25, he was having an unsuccessful trial at Blackpool.

‌



But in the case of Gabriel’s future, it is hard to find anyone with any serious doubt over whether he will make it or not. He is, by common consent, the brightest prospect in the land.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He is an even brighter prospect, some say, than Max Dowman, who made his Premier League debut for Arsenal at 15 years and 235 days old. So, yes, it will be a blow for United if he does walk away, which certainly seems to be his intention.

The competition for marquee youngsters is intense. Rio Ngumoha was one of the most talked-about academy players in the Premier League but left Chelsea for Liverpool around his 16th birthday.

Gabriel turns 16 in three weeks’ time. Youngsters moving between powerhouse clubs is nothing new.

‌



View 3 Images JJ Gabriel was the youngest winner of the Manchester United Academy Player of the Year award (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Cesc Fabregas was a jewel of Barcelona’s fabled academy, La Masia, but walked away when he was 16 and joined Arsenal. It happens.

That is not to say Gabriel’s request will not concern United and their fans. This is Manchester United we are talking about. It should be a club that is the ultimate dream for any young player.

‌



But times have changed. For Gabriel’s generation - and probably his family’s generation - United is just another big club. They have not won a Premier League in 13 years and have not won a Champions League in 18 years.

Gabriel might look at Marcus Rashford - a predecessor as a prodigy - and wonder why the England attacker would have preferred to be at Barcelona this season. The reasons behind the decision of Gabriel and his family and his advisers are not yet crystal clear.

View 3 Images Rio Ngumoha left Chelsea for Liverpool at the age of 16 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



There is a suggestion that they thought he should be in United’s Champions League squad, in the same way Dowman was in Arsenal’s at a similar age. Whatever the reasons, they should be respected.

But it should be remembered that the old mantra about no one player being bigger than the club is still true. And especially when that player is not yet 16 years old and especially when that club is Manchester United.

Yes, it will be extremely annoying for United’s coaching staff, executives, and, indeed, fans. But of the issues Michael Carrick and the rest of those in charge of the footballing operation have, it is not a seismic setback.

Sports.title: Howard Webb points blame for Manchester derby offside controversy as Pro Ref take action
Sports.content:
Refereeing chief Howard Webb has claimed that VAR officials in Stockley Park had 'tunnel vision' before the decision to allow Erling Haaland's controversial winner in the Manchester derby.

Video assistant referee Matt Donohue and his assistant, Blake Antrobus, have both been stood down for this weekend's Premier League fixtures after wrongly letting Haaland's goal stand.

Initially flagged for offside due to Enzo Fernandez's attempt to play the ball in build-up, the decision was overturned following VAR check. Webb, as head of Pro Ref, wrote to Manchester United officials within hours of full-time to apologise for the error that played a decisive part in their 1-0 defeat to leave Michael Carrick's side on four points after four games.

Haaland's goal wasn't the only moment of drama at Old Trafford either. City star Phil Foden was sent off after kicking out at United captain Bruno Fernandes, a decision which Webb insists was correct.

‌



Appearing on Match Officials Mic'd Up, the former referee admitted: "We felt it was important that we acknowledged an error in this situation. We know that Erling Haaland, who was penalised on field for offside, wasn't in an offside position.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"But we also know that Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, almost certainly interfered with the Manchester United defence and probably the goalkeeper as well.

‌



"I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are. None more so than the officials themselves. They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation. They'll not be officiating again until after the international break. We've reached out to Manchester United and acknowledged the error, as we do when these things happen.

"They don't happen that often, but we want to ensure that we are transparent and open, and we've played the audio and the footage to the football club to let them know what happened, and we're going to review this situation to understand what elements of process fell down in this situation which meant we didn't get to the right outcome."

Should Phil Foden have been sent off? Have your say in the comments section.

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez dived for the ball from an offside position (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Webb added that the officials back in Stockley Park got 'tunnel vision' in focusing on Haaland's part in the goal, with colleagues unable to pull him back out to look at the wider picture.

He added: "And when the VAR starts their check, they see through the use of the semi-automated offside technology, that Haaland, when he's played, is actually onside by three centimetres, played on by [Patrick] Dorgu on the far side, and the VAR gets super focused on Haaland. He establishes he's onside, he thinks that's a good goal, Haaland's not offside, as was thought initially.

"But of course, when he then runs it back through the full APP, he doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez's position. He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score. He doesn't touch the ball, but he doesn't truly evaluate other elements of offside. In that moment, he gets tunnel vision. He gets focused on Haaland, and it's down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn't happen on this occasion."

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez's role was incorrectly overlooked in the process of allowing the goal, according to Webb

‌



Webb then emphasised: "We'll review it, reflect upon it, and try to take the learning forward to prevent this unusual type of error from happening again."

City took the lead in the derby after they were reduced to 10 men. Tempers flared in the 23rd minute, as Foden reacted to a kick from Fernandes by lashing out himself.

On-field referee Michael Oliver quickly made up his mind and it was the City player who was punished. "I agree with the red card for Phil Foden for violent conduct," Webb concurred. "He kicks out with force into the upper body of Bruno Fernandes.

"We saw a player sent off for Aston Villa earlier in the season. [Joao] Gomes was sent off for a very similar thing, kicking with the studs into the body. And that's seen by the referee on the field, and that's the on-field call, a red card for Foden.

‌



"Now, when you look at the footage, there is that petulant kick by Bruno Fernandes into the backside of Foden. It is more petulant than violent.

"To be violent conduct, it has to have excessive force or brutality, and when you look at that, particularly in full speed, it doesn't have those elements. So therefore, this would be a yellow card offence. And the VAR can't step in to recommend the referee looks at the screen to give a yellow card.

"Of course, if all of this is missed and nothing is given against Foden, then the VAR could step in so the referee could see Foden's actions for a possible red card, and they would capture Fernandes' yellow card action. But because the referee gave the red card on the field, that option is not open to the VAR."

‌

Sports.title: Fairy Glen well fancied in John Musker feature at Yarmouth
Sports.content:
The Listed John Musker Fillies’ Stakes takes centre stage on day two of Yarmouth’s Eastern Festival on Wednesday, all live on Sky Sports Racing.

3.41 Yarmouth - Fairy Glen, Seet & Rhapsody clash

The EBF Stallions John Musker Fillies' Stakes is the feature on an excellent midweek card at Yarmouth.

Simon & Ed Crisford-trained filly Fairy Glen tops the ratings with a mark of 112, and this Group Two winner could prove hard to beat in this lesser grade. She was only narrowly beaten when fifth in the Group One Prix Vicomtesse Vigier back in May and has obvious claims if fit enough on her return.

Rhapsody is a key player for William Haggas and Tom Marquand. A dual winner, she has filled the runner-up spot on her last two outings, and a similar effort would see her in the mix.

Seet is lightly-raced and should have more to offer, while Sky Safari has not been seen since finished third in the Group Three Hoppings Stakes at Newcastle and looks an each-way player on the switch to the turf.

4.12 Yarmouth - Unbeaten Enoch makes handicap debut

Ryan Moore has a 24 per cent strike-rate from over 100 rides at Yarmouth and heads to Norfolk to ride Enoch, who bids to remain unbeaten in a strong edition of the Goffs Two Million Series Handicap.

John & Thady Gosden's charge made it two from two when defying a penalty at Lingfield last month and, given his pedigree, he rates an exciting addition to handicap company.

Image: Ryan Moore heads to Yarmouth for two rides

Round The Table built on his debut to land a maiden and a novice before racing too keenly when beaten on handicap debut last time. He is given another chance with the tongue-tie removed.

Plenty have chances including the consistent El Matador, while Point Of Contact was beaten favourite at Salisbury and has a bit to prove.

3.06 Yarmouth - Liberty's Hall looks to go one better

Liberty's Hall hopes to build on an encouraging debut in the EBF Future Stayers Maiden Stakes.

James Owen's son of Nathaniel showed inexperience when chasing home Sonic Angel on his first start at Kempton last month and given natural progression he should hit the frame.

Nostalgic Warrior is a brother to the useful Star Performer and Divine Rhythm must be monitored in the betting on his debut for William Haggas.

Richard Hughes' Daddy Star is worth a mention, while Chapel Stream was only seventh on his debut and his trainer reaches for the cheekpieces.

Sports.title: Inside Europe's early Ryder Cup team trip to 'immaculate' Adare Manor
Sports.content:
It may still be a year to go until Team Europe's bid for a historic Ryder Cup threepeat, but Luke Donald has already had many of his prospective line-up together at Adare Manor.

Although not quite a full scouting mission like Donald provided ahead of previous Ryder Cup wins at Marco Simone GC and Bethpage Black, it gave many of his potential players an early experience of tackling next year's Ryder Cup venue in Ireland.

A mix of established Ryder Cup members and likely rookie contenders made the trip after the Amgen Irish Open, with a team dinner followed by 18 holes on Monday

Sixteen players joined Donald and his vice-captains for the team session ahead of travelling onto the DP World Tour's BMW PGA Championship - 10 of last year's line-up, two more with past Ryder Cup pedigree and four potential debutants.

Sports.title: Tipped to be the best ever - but is Herbert the NFL's best underachiever?
Sports.content:
The kids call it glazing. NFL folk might call it Jim Harbaughing. Either way, gushing praise of Justin Herbert is generating heightened and unavoidable attention around one of football's most gifted but divisive stars.

Herbert stepped out at SoFi Stadium as the best player on the field last weekend. He stepped off it having been out-duelled and outplayed by, with the greatest respect to him, everybody's favourite bridge quarterback in veteran Jacoby Brissett and a transitioning Arizona Cardinals team adrift of postseason discussion.

Brissett and a valiant defensive display had guided the Cardinals to a 26-14 opening weekend victory over Herbert's Los Angeles Chargers to pierce, but by no means burst (yet), the bubble of a team billed among the most exciting playoff contenders coming into Week One. Over-billed? Over-hyped? Time will tell.

It was the quintessential Chargers Chargering exhibition based on the discourse of recent years, a disjointed performance of mistakes and miscues negating the influence of superior individual talent. An all too familiar theme to this team.

Now, were you to drop somebody on earth for a day, ask them to watch a showreel of the NFL's starting quarterbacks and point out which they believed might be considered the best, the most feared, the most dangerous, you would bank on an initial eye test leading many to Justin Herbert. He remains something of a dream prototype blessed with the ludicrous arm talent, the marauding ground presence, the dwarfing stature, the fizzing needle-threading velocity and deep ball fireworks - as much, though, fuels most of the frustration surrounding his career thus far.

In his most successful moments, he has been spectacular, a match for any defense in the league and one of the most box office showcases in football. There has rarely been a flicker of doubt over his skillset, but noise-meets-uncertainty over both his killer instinct and credentials among the elite play-callers in the NFL is as loud as ever, you feel.

Herbert finished Sunday's loss 17 of 27 for 209 yards, one touchdown and an ill-informed interception while attacking double coverage downfield with 10 minutes to play and the Chargers trailing by nine. His day had started hot when he led an eight-play, 77-yard scoring drive including three passes for 60 yards to Ladd McConkey, whose exit with a chest injury after his touchdown catch before the end of the third quarter left Herbert and his offense short of answers.

In fact, the Chargers proceeded to go punt, turnover on downs, interception, turnover on downs, turnover on downs on the five possessions spent without McConkey, their offense failing to reach opposition territory in four fourth-quarter drives, while also collecting six of their team's total penalties including five in the second half and three straight on their penultimate series.

Image: Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert shakes hands with Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett

The performance came just days after head coach Jim Harbaugh forecast Herbert going down as the best to play his position.

"Allow me to call my shot, like Babe Ruth pointing his bat over to centerfield: Justin Herbert, when it's all said and done, when his career comes to an end, I predict he will be known as the greatest, best ever to play the position of quarterback," Harbaugh said. "When it's all said and done, and his career is finished, we're going to look back and say, 'Yep, that's the best that ever did it.'"

Harbaugh will not and should not change who he is, having become Herbert's most vocal and persistent cheerleader since taking over as head coach in 2024. He has repeatedly hailed his quarterback's potential for greatness and sought to speak Herbert's explosion into existence almost, but with it has come enlarged expectations and a Hollywood fishbowl feel. Is there such a thing as too much hype?

We might add that it is merely Week One, a prime window for premature panic. The Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots both lost in the first week of last season before going on to reach the Super Bowl, while the widely favoured Los Angeles Rams were just beaten by the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne; nobody wrote them off, nor is anybody writing them off. Seasons aren't defined in Week One, but an unwelcome start has only prompted further question marks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Elsewhere in the AFC West, the Chargers' rival Kansas City Chiefs stormed to victory over the Denver Broncos

Part of the intrigue around Herbert this season comes from the hiring of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, whose wizardry fell flat in a disappointing end to his Miami Dolphins head coaching tenure but has seen his arrival tipped to unlock the best of his quarterback's alien arm. The best of McDaniel's offense in Miami relied on Tua Tagovailoa's quick-release passing concepts, heavy pre-snap motion and a dynamic rushing attack off which his quarterback could tee, so Herbert will be asked to stray from his comfort zone a little. Every quarterback-coordinator marriage needs time to flourish, McDaniel similarly seeking to justify his own advertising as one of the most influential offensive figureheads in modern football.

McDaniel failed to get his running game going at all through second-year back Omarion Hampton, who managed just 43 yards from 12 carries and averaged only 1.5 yards before contact behind an offensive line that surrendered three sacks. It had been an area the Chargers appeared to address efficiently over the last two seasons under Greg Roman, whose run-heavy offense restored some long-lost stability to their attack. No balance, no party.

Herbert was sacked 54 times last season, the second-most in the league, as the Chargers went without two-time Pro Bowl left tackle Rashawn Slater for the entire campaign while losing Pro Bowl right tackle Joe Alt for 11 games through injury. His 225 sacks and 615 hits entering the season marked the most on any quarterback since Herbert was drafted with the sixth overall pick in 2020. Both Slater and Alt returned this weekend, but weaknesses continued to show on the interior of the Chargers' offensive line.

The numbers have often spoken to his ability to join the NFL's premier quarterbacks at the table. Herbert's 24,820 passing yards through his first six seasons are the second most in NFL history behind only Peyton Manning, whom he surpassed for the most completions by a quarterback in his first six seasons.

He also previously began his NFL career by setting the record for most consecutive 4,000-yard passing seasons with three in a row from 2020 to 2022 behind his best offensive arsenal featuring Keenan Allen, Mike Williams and Austin Ekeler. The gradual departure of the aforementioned trio hasn't helped; McConkey, Quentin Johnston and tight end David Njoku are now his most recognised pass-catching targets.

But for all his stats through the air, the one number Chargers fans care about is playoff wins, which currently stands at zero from three postseason appearances. Herbert has fallen in the Wild Card round in three of the last four years, witnessing the Chargers blow a 27-0 lead against the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2022 playoffs, producing a career-worst 43.8 completion percentage and four interceptions against the Houston Texans in the 2024 playoffs and throwing for just 159 yards and no touchdowns while being sacked six times against the Patriots last season.

There is something to be admired about the ability for Herbert to become one of the prized faces of the league without quite yet managing to break through the glass ceiling. For the purposes of further fuelling an AFC arm's race brimming with quarterback talent, football is urging and willing him on to thrust himself among the perennial frontrunners, and football knows he is capable of doing so.

But games like that of Sunday should not be happening. Year seven is up and running and the Justin Herbert story remains both captivating and impossible to forecast.

Sports.title: What next for Arsenal prodigy Dowman after latest statement display?
Sports.content:
Max Dowman has waited patiently for opportunities in Arsenal's first team, but when he gets them, he delivers.

Mikel Arteta has managed the prodigy carefully since his big moment last season, when he became the Premier League's youngest scorer in a vital 2-0 home win over Everton on their title charge.

Dowman has played six times since then, mostly in cameos, and has been an unused substitute on four occasions this season. Last Saturday, he played an hour for the U21s in their 4-1 defeat to Chelsea while the first team won at Sunderland. Arteta warned Dowman afterwards that he must earn his minutes this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Carabao Cup round three clash between Ipswich and Arsenal

But Dowman did not have to wait long for his chance. While £63.5m striker Viktor Gyokeres failed to take his opportunity during Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night, Dowman excelled, and the ease with which he scored twice was frightening.

His first, in just the seventh minute, came after he stole possession in midfield, burst onto the ball before Gyokeres, shimmyed past Cedric Kipre to leave the defender on the ground, before sending goalkeeper Christian Walton the wrong way with his weaker right foot.

"That's something very natural for him," said Arteta. "He can deliver those actions effortlessly. I would say that's his biggest quality."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dowman scores his second of the night to put Arsenal three up against Ipswich

Dowman had to be more precise for his second. Martin Zubimendi's pass deflected off Jacob Greaves's left arm, and Dowman, with little space inside the penalty area, adjusted to the ricochet with two quick touches to set up an accurate, composed shot on his left foot that almost trickled over the line, such was the perfectly measured weight of the effort.

Dowman's performance will only increase the hype around him. How will Arteta manage that?

"Well, it depends. If he does what he does on the pitch, it's not easy, I understand," said Arteta. "But what we have to do is look after him. He's 16 years old. You don't see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that's a totally different context.

"But in this league, with the demands that the league [has], the players and everything put on you, we really need to make sure every time we throw him in, he's in the right context with the right preparation. That's what we are trying to do."

It wasn't all about the goals at Portman Road. Dowman, who only completed his GCSEs in August, also showed his work rate off the ball, pressing Ipswich into a mistake for Noni Madueke's goal.

"Defensively, his application, his capacity as well to sustain the actions, is not easy," added Arteta.

"He's 16 years old, and he can create moments, but to consistently go through the game, every phase, with the demands that we put on them, to be able to do that is extremely difficult. And he's coping better and better and better.

"He did the action where he regained the ball and won it. In the first goal, he loses his man. And that's the thing that we need to continue to reiterate with him because he's an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play at the biggest stage and still handle the situation with such naturality."

The evening wasn't even all about Dowman. Marli Salmon, 17, made only his second start for the first team and impressed at centre-back with an assured performance.

"Just having two 16-year-olds playing for Arsenal at this level against a Premier League team is so fulfilling," said Arteta. "Because I've been there and just to be able to contribute in somebody's career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight is just phenomenal.

"Medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we're going to have two tremendous footballers for the future."

Dowman has benefited from Arsenal's stability under Arteta. The club has been able to nurture and develop him, without the distraction of cycling through managers. On the same day 15-year-old JJ Gabriel asked to leave Manchester United, Dowman made his latest statement on the pitch.

Arsenal fans will be desperate to see more of him. Arteta has warned it's not so easy to play him regularly.

"Everything is possible. The probability [of playing regularly] is probably extremely low because you don't see the players with the capacity to handle just the physicality of the game," he said.

"Not only that, but the demands that you have to put your body through in the week to be able to be in good condition to compete, the amount of information, the challenges that you have to face. But he's doing it and he's doing it really well every time there's a chance."
