Sports.title: Jamie O’Hara wishes Tottenham got relegated and storms out of studio after argument with Jason Cundy boils over
Sports.content:
Jamie O’Hara wishes Tottenham got relegated and storms out of studio after argument with Jason Cundy boils over

Jamie O’Hara took his Tottenham frustration to new heights by claiming the club should have been relegated last season.

The Sports Bar host endured yet another sombre start to the show on Tuesday night following his beloved Spurs’ Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool.

7 It was another match without victory for Roberto De Zerbi's Spurs Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

7 O'Hara cut a dejected figure on Tuesday's Sports Bar

Roberto De Zerbi’s side were beaten 3-1 at a rain-soaked Anfield to bring about an early end to any hopes of winning the competition.

Goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai were enough to sweep Spurs aside who had pulled one back late on through Conor Gallagher.

The midfielder’s close range finish was Tottenham’s first goal anywhere this season after drawing blanks in their opening four league games.

And with a season that is already mirroring those of the previous two campaigns, O’Hara, who later in the show stormed out of the talkSPORT studio, appeared to have already reached his limit.

O'Hara's passionate tirade

“Seriously, what is going on?,” O’Hara said opening up Tuesday’s show.

“I feel like everyday I wake up and it’s the same thing.

“Every single time Spurs play, I look at the fixtures and I'm like, ‘Spurs are playing tonight, alright, here we go, get beat.’

“I don’t know what to say. It’s groundhog day.

Things were made doubly worse for the ex-Spurs midfielder with partner-in-crime Jason Cundy lapping up every second of his co-host’s misery.

“This is the perfect night again for Cundy. When is my night?” O’Hara ranted.

7 Dominik Szoboszlai's superb effort from range was the pick of the goals at Anfield Credit: Getty

“I’ve been here for five years and I’ve had one good night. One. The Europa League final, that was it.

“It’s absolute guff, it really is and I’m sick and tired of it. I know it’s all great and everyone enjoys it but this is actually getting ridiculous.

“Where do Spurs go from here? We have got a disease. We don’t know how to win. Even when we score we get beat,

“Every single game no matter what, Spurs get beat. Spend £400million – get beat.

“Score – get beat. New manager – get beat.

“We’ve got a disease."

7 Cundy did his best to further wind up his co-host - and succeeded

Cundy then hilariously chimed in describing the disease as an incurable one.

Just when listeners thought O’Hara had got everything off his chest, he made the bold suggestion that Tottenham should have been relegated last season.

Championship level

“You know what should have happened, we should have gone down. We are so bad,” he added.

“We’re shocking. The only reason we stayed up is because Aston Villa guffed it and Everton jacked it in at the end of the season.

“I thought, we might start the new season and see something different, something positive.

“No, absolute guff again. We don’t deserve to be playing Premier League teams. We are absolutely useless.”

7 Conor Gallagher's late goal, which reduced Spurs' deficit from 2-0 to 2-1, was the only highlight of the night for Spurs Credit: Getty

O’Hara then bravely asked his co-host to provide him with one positive from Tuesday’s cup tie to which Cundy cheekily replied: “You scored tonight at a Premier League ground. First time that’s happened this season.”

And that set O’Hara off on yet another rant.

“The problem is we don’t take our chances and are soft,” he said. “Ice creams. We’re like a flake in 30 degree heat.

“And why is [Mathys] Tel still playing? I'd rather Richarlison played.

“He’s guff, he’s terrible, he’s got trampoline feet. He’s everything that’s bad about Tottenham. We signed him for £50m.”

O'Hara storms out of studio

After over an hour of being tormented by talkSPORT's chief wind-up merchant Cundy, it all got a bit much for O'Hara.

7 O'Hara simply couldn't take Cundy's ribbing any longer

7 O'Hara needed some air for a few minutes before returning to hosting duties for the second half of the show

The 39-year-old made for a sharp exit mid-show after arguing with Cundy about Mathys Tel's use to the Spurs team.

O'Hara questioned why De Zerbi continues to select the French winger, even suggesting replacing Tel with the exiled Richarlison would be a better option for Spurs.

Cundy launched a defence, albeit a sarcastic one, of Tel's value to the team - and O'Hara decided enough was enough.

After the break, O'Hara returned to his hosting duties for more ribbing by his mate.

Sports.title: Why Lionel Messi is in Argentina squad weeks after announcing retirement
Sports.content:
Why Lionel Messi is in Argentina squad weeks after announcing retirement

Lionel Messi will say goodbye to the Argentina national team during a friendly match next month.

Messi announced at the end of August that he is retiring from international football, ending a glittering 21-year spell for his country.



3 Messi will officially call time on his Argentina career next month Credit: Getty

His news came just weeks after Argentina lost 1-0 against Spain in the 2026 World Cup final.

Club football pauses for the first international break of the 2026/27 season, which will last three weeks, towards the end of this month.

Argentina have three fixtures lined up and, despite his decision to call time with his nation, Messi will feature in the coming weeks.



Why is Messi in the Argentina squad?

The Argentina squad for the friendlies was revealed on Tuesday, and Messi is among the 28 players to be called up.

Argentina have said that he will join the team for their third and final friendly against Benin on October 3.



And their president Claudio Tapia has confirmed that the match will be Messi's farewell at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.

Speaking via ESPN, he said: "After a chat with Lionel Scaloni, we made the decision to invite the best player in the world, the emblem of our national team, our captain Lionel Andres Messi, so that he can have the farewell he truly deserves, on October 6th, in Argentina."



The occasion will be even more special for Messi as he made his home debut for Argentina at Estadio Monumental in October 2005.

He assisted Juan Roman Riquelme for the opener in a 2-0 win against Peru during their 2006 World Cup qualifying run.

It's not yet clear if Messi will play against Benin, but the fact that he has announced retirement would suggest that he won't.

3 Messi is set for a special and emotional send-off Credit: AFP



Tapia is also said to have extended the invitation for the farewell to the players who are not in the latest squad, but were part of their 2022 World Cup win.

Victory in Qatar was the cherry on the icing on the cake for Messi and his Argentina career as he finally won football's biggest prize.

A second World Cup title in the summer just gone would have added to his endless achievements, but the defeat to Spain ended in tears.

Messi has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina, with each metric the all-time highest for the South American nation.



Alongside his World Cup triumph, the 39-year-old is a two-time Copa America winner and Finalissima champion.

He scored 21 goals across six World Cups, the second-most in history, and his 34 matches played is the tournament record.

3 All good things must come to an end - and Messi is primed to get his final farewell Credit: Getty

Messi, who will begin playing under his new Inter Miami head coach Kily Gonzalez on Wednesday, has recently been nominated for the Ballon d'Or.



The forward is one of 30 names in contention for the award, and is set to be present at the ceremony as the record eight-time winner.

Sports.title: Max Dowman joins exclusive club with Wayne Rooney as Mikel Arteta purrs over Arsenal star’s ‘silk’
Sports.content:
Max Dowman became just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side across all competitions.

The Arsenal academy graduate netted twice in his side’s 4-2 win over Ipswich in Tuesday’s Carabao Cup clash at Portman Road.

3 Max Dowman was mobbed by his Arsenal teammates after brilliantly opening the scoring at Portman Road Credit: Getty

Dowman’s heroics sees him join Wayne Rooney on the exclusive list following his League Cup double for Everton against Wrexham in October 2002.

The teenager registered his second and third goals for the Gunners at senior level with fans left purring by his opener on the night.

After just six minutes, Dowman collected the ball midway into the Ipswich half before cantering his way towards goal.

Appearing as though he was shaping up to play Eberechi Eze in on goal, he cut inside instead with a superb dummy to deceive Ipswich’s Cedric Kipre.

He then topped it off with a cool finish in the bottom corner to hand his side the lead.

It set the tone for another fine result for Mikel Arteta's side, with the Gunners boss opting to field a host of fringe players for the cup tie.

Noni Madueke doubled Arsenal's advantage before Dowman netted his second of the night shortly after the interval.

Mikel Merino made it 4-0 to Arsenal before the Tractor Boys made a fist of it with two late goals to make the scoreline look somewhat respectable.

The win hands Arsenal safe passage into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

But the night belonged to Dowman who wrote yet another piece of footballing history.

3 Dowman has three goals in 14 appearances for Arsenal's senior team Credit: Getty

The midfielder is already the Premier League’s youngest ever goalscorer following his unforgettable strike in the Gunners’ win over Everton last season.

Arteta: Max is a joy to watch

Gunners boss Arteta was of course waxing lyrical about the boy wonder, saying post-match: "When the game opens up a little bit he's incredible at carrying the ball, eliminating players, dribbling and finishing action.

"It was a joy to watch him.

Commenting on Dowman's technique for his first goal, Arteta said: "Unbelievable. That's the thing that he can do. He's so unpredictable. He can go either way.

"He stops you, accelerates, changes direction. He's so fluid and so nice to watch as well. The left footer is even nicer to watch. He was silk."

The perfect response

And Dowman, who was left out of the squad for last Saturday’s 2-0 win at Sunderland certainly gave Arteta plenty of food for thought with his display.

3 Dowman has certainly given Arteta something to think about regarding playing him in the Premier League Credit: Getty

“I wish we could have him [against Sunderland], but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have,” Arteta previously said.

“He will have his chance, he will have his minutes, and he will have to earn them like anybody else.

“We know the talent that we have, we know the player that we have there, and we need to help him and find a way to make sure that he continues to develop and help the team.”

Arsenal are back in action this weekend when they travel to Brighton on Saturday afternoon aiming to continue their 100 per cent start to the season.

Sports.title: ‘It was the moment’ – Thomas Tuchel reveals bizarre World Cup regret
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel says he regrets not eating grass from the Azteca Stadium pitch following England’s heroic World Cup win over Mexico.

The Three Lions’ 3-2 victory over the co-hosts in July was one of the tournament’s most enthralling matches.



5 England battled the altitude and hostile atmosphere to edge to a 3-2 win over co-hosts Mexico Credit: AFP

5 Tuchel loved every moment of the heroic win at the Azteca Credit: Getty

Two goals from Jude Bellingham and a Harry Kane penalty was enough for ten-man England to see off a second-half Mexican onslaught.

The win was made all the more impressive due to the match being played 2,240 metres above sea level – a condition that Tuchel's men were not physically conditioned for.



The German sat down with Daniel Sturridge in ‘Reflections: England’s World Cup Journey’ - to be released on Wednesday - to reflect on the eventful night in Mexico City and revealed his one regret, albeit a slightly bizarre one.

“I texted a friend after the match,” Tuchel said. “And I just wrote: I regret that I didn’t eat some grass after the match, to keep something from this in my body forever. That was the feeling. It was the moment.”



Tuchel holds fond memories of the victory and in particular, the togetherness in the squad.

That was no more evident than when England’s stars gathered around Jordan Henderson after he fell awkwardly over the advertising hoardings, fracturing his wrist.



Fond memories

“This had so much of what you could wish for,” Tuchel added. “If you needed any proof of what it meant to these players, and how they were with each other, it was the moment when Jordan (Henderson) fell over and broke his arm.

“In a second the players were there, every single player was there, stopping celebrations, building a shield, protecting Jordan, not going anywhere, in full empathy. It was so special.”

Tuchel came in for huge criticism following England's semi-final exit to Argentina.

The England boss was vilified for his passive tactical approach in the final 20 minutes which saw the Three Lions concede twice late on and exit the tournament.



5 Henderson's bizarre injury at full time was the only stain on a wonderful night for England Credit: Getty

5 Things quickly went south for Tuchel following an abject second-half display against Argentina Credit: Getty

Despite the huge disappointment, Tuchel believes the 2-1 defeat to Lionel Scaloni’s men saw something his side can build on ahead of Euro 2028.

All eyes on Euro 2028

The 53-year-old also says he is fully focused on a successful home Euros campaign with his side.



“I’m very excited to work with these players, I’m excited to have new young players we can bring into the camp, and they can learn,” Tuchel said speaking for the first time since England’s third-place play-off victory over France in Miami.

“I think we got another step closer. I think we’re there. It’s very difficult to prepare a World Cup in the US, but I think it’s possible to prepare for a Euros. And we prepare in Nations League tier one.

“The target is to have another ten matches. We had ten matches in the US: eight wins, one draw, one painful loss. But that is something to build on.

“We all have the right to hold our heads high, and go with courage and positivity into the next challenges. We have four matches in the Nations League. That’s where the focus is.”



5 It's world champions Spain up next for Tuchel and England Credit: Getty

Tuchel will lead England in their Nations League opener against world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday, September 26, live on talkSPORT.

That match precedes trips to Czechia and Croatia in a newly formatted international break lasting three weeks with those matches also live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi’s former Argentina teammate is now his head coach at Inter Miami after Javier Mascherano departure
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi’s former Argentina teammate is now his head coach at Inter Miami after Javier Mascherano departure

Lionel Messi can win another trophy at Inter Miami whilst playing for a different former teammate this week.

Inter Miami announced towards the end of August that they reached an agreement with Cristian 'Kily' Gonzalez regarding their vacancy.

2 Gonzalez has taken the reins at Inter Miami after Mascherano's exit Credit: Getty

Gonzalez has now officially arrived in Florida and begun his duties at the MLS club.

He has become the permanent successor to Javier Mascherano, who surprisingly resigned as head coach for personal reasons in April.

Mascherano made 414 appearances alongside Messi for the Argentina national team, their Olympic side and Barcelona.

They then won the MLS Eastern Conference and MLS Cup when the former was boss, with a new but fellow familiar face now in charge.

Gonzalez is in his fourth managerial role at Inter Miami after spells at Rosario Central, Union de Santa Fe and Club Atletico Platense.

Formerly a winger at clubs including Boca Juniors, Valencia and Inter Milan, he scored ten goals across 56 appearances for Argentina.

Two of his caps were won with Messi, with both coming during their qualification campaign for the 2006 World Cup.

Gonzalez is now set to work with the football icon yet again, this time in a different capacity as his head coach at Inter Miami.

His touchline debut comes on Wednesday night as they face Mexican side Cruz Azul in the 2026 Campeones Cup final.

The annual exhibition match is contested by the MLS champions and Mexican super cup (Campeon de Campeones) winners.

2 Messi could land his fourth honour in Inter Miami colours on Wednesday Credit: Getty

What trophies has Messi won at Inter Miami?

Just weeks after completing his shock move to North America in July 2023, Messi helped guide his new club to their first ever trophy.

He scored in the 1-1 Leagues Cup final draw with Nashville SC before Inter Miami triumphed with a dramatic 10-9 penalty shootout win.

Supporters' Shield glory followed in 2024 as the Floridian side had the best regular season in MLS with a league-record 74 points.

Inter Miami then lifted the MLS Cup in December with a 3-1 win over Vancouver Whitecaps, with Messi bagging two assists.

They will therefore win a fourth different honour if they beat Cruz Azul on Wednesday.

Another MLS Cup victory could follow later in the year as they are on course to qualify for round one of the play-offs by sitting second in the Eastern Conference.

Sports.title: Pierre Sage’s replacement at Lens sacked after four Ligue 1 games due to ‘huge behind the scenes bust-up’
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage’s replacement at Lens sacked after four Ligue 1 games due to ‘huge behind the scenes bust-up’

Lens have reportedly sacked manager Dino Toppmoller after just four league games following a bust-up behind the scenes.

Toppmoller replaced Pierre Sage in the dugout in June after the former boss left his position to join Crystal Palace.



2 Sage has left Lens after his assistant was let go by the Ligue 1 side Credit: AFP

However, his tenure in charge of the club has already come to an end, despite his side winning in three of his six matches.

According to reports in France, Toppmoller has lost his job at Lens after his assistant Nelson Morgado was dismissed.

Morgado had worked with the German since 2017 and was one of his closest connections, having teamed up at Eintracht Frankfurt too.



But the assistant is reported to have been demanding more commitment and passion from the French members of Lens' staff, which made them uncomfortable.

And that led to his exit earlier this week - but following that news, manager Toppmoller has also left the club.



Why have Lens sacked Toppmoller?

Toppmoller is reported to have stood in solidarity for Morgado and found his coach's dismissal unacceptable.

German outlet BILD claims he argued with the club about their direct interference with his team of staff.



That bust-up seems to have led to his sacking, rather than it being anything to do with results.

Lens beat PSG to win the Trophee des Champions at the start of the season and won their Ligue 1 opener 5-2 against Auxerre.

Two league defeats then followed, but they then beat Slavia Prague 3-2 in the Champions League last week, going on to draw away at Le Mans on Sunday.

2 Toppmoller leaves the club with Lens sitting 10th in the league table Credit: Getty



Toppmoller's managerial career

Toppmoller was named Lens manager after Sage left for the Premier League, returning to management after five months away.

He left his previous role at Frankfurt in January after just under three years at the Bundesliga club.

The 45-year-old took charge of 121 games for them, winning 51 in all competitions and taking them to the Champions League.

Before that, Toppmoller hadn't had much of a managerial career, getting the Frankfurt job after working as an assistant to Julian Nagelsmann at RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich.



As a player, he was on Manchester City's books in 2001, but played most of his football in the German lower leagues.

Now, he is going to be on the lookout for another job after seemingly taking a stand that has led to his sacking at Lens.

Sports.title: ‘Absolutely broken’ – Ex-Rangers forward Nacho Novo’s stepson dies aged 26
Sports.content:
Rangers legend Nacho Novo has announced the tragic death of his stepson at the age of 26.

The Spaniard, who now manages Scottish seventh tier outfit Darvel FC, shared the news stepson Ross’s untimely passing in a heart-breaking Instagram post.



3 Novo shared moving images of his time with his late stepson Credit: Instagram @nnovo10

The 47-year-old wrote: "Nothing in my life could’ve prepared me for this post. We are absolutely broken to share the sad news that our beautiful boy has tragically passed away.

"Please respect our family's privacy during this extremely difficult time. Forever in our hearts my boy".

Ross's younger brother posted his own tribute on Tiktok, writing: "U were the best ever.



He continued: "Rest in peace to my big brother. Going to miss you so much. Hope you're okay and safe up there.

“Thanks for always looking after me. I love you so so much, I can't believe it's true. You were the best brother ever. Forever 26."



A statement from Darvel FC read: “The Club’s thoughts are with Nacho and his family at this sad time and we ask that everyone respects the families’ privacy during this extremely difficult time.”

Tributes pour in

Further tributes quickly poured in from fans, media personalities and ex-teammates.



Presenter Laura Woods wrote: "I'm so sorry for your loss Nacho, rest in peace your beautiful boy."

Wrestling star Grado replied: "So sorry to hear this Nacho - absolutely heart breaking. My thoughts are with you and your family."

Ex-Rangers teammate Michael Mols also commented writing: “Unbelievable Nacho. My thoughts and prayers and my condolences.”

3 Novo was inundated with tributes from fans and former teammates following Ross's passing Credit: Instagram @nnovo10



Meanwhile, former Rangers star Steven Davis added: “Thoughts with you all at this difficult time.”

A spokesperson for Rangers FC wrote: "The thoughts of everyone at Rangers are with you at this sad time Nacho."

Ross's cause of death has not yet been disclosed.

Nacho married Ross’s mother Donna Clark in 2015 following a long-term relationship.

The couple share a teenage son and Novo is stepdad to Donna’s sons Ross and Dylan.



The former striker, who netted 70 goals in 250 games for the Gers, retired from football in 2017.

3 Novo helped fire the Ibrox club to three SPL titles

His efforts saw him inducted into the club’s Hall of Fame three years before hanging up his boots.

During his time at Ibrox, Novo won three league titles and three league cups while lifting the Scottish Cup twice.



Aside from his stint at Rangers, he enjoyed spells with Raith Rovers, Dundee and Greenock Morton.

In 2018, he suffered a heart attack while playing for a Rangers legends team in Berlin and underwent emergency surgery to save his life.

Sports.title: 'I'm f****** angry... we're stuck on a hamster wheel and people are killing themselves': Former Wales star ALIX POPHAM bares his soul as rugby's civil war over brain injuries drags on - and insists he is not trying to 'ruin' the sport
Sports.content:
As he relaxes on the sofa in his home on the outskirts of Newport, South Wales, a pair of crutches lie next to Alix Popham – an aid to help with recovery from a recent hip replacement.

‘I’m 46 – young to have one,’ the former Scarlets, Newport and Wales back-rower tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘I got told five days before having this operation my other hip needs doing as well. I'm not complaining.

‘I knew that could happen from rugby. When I was playing, I saw ex-players who were wobbling around clubhouses due to bad backs, shoulders, knees and hips.

‘That, for me, was part of the game. But because brain injuries are invisible, they were never discussed then. We've opened the can on that.’

It has now been six years since Popham, to use his own words, ‘opened the can’. In April 2020, he joined England's 2003 World Cup winner Steve Thompson and others in revealing he was struggling with neurodegenerative diseases such as early onset dementia.

Their revelations launched legal action against rugby’s authorities, claiming their issues were as a result of their playing careers. Since then, the reality is little has changed.

It has been six years since Alix Popham joined a host of rugby players in revealing he was struggling with neurodegenerative diseases such as early onset dementia

The former Scarlets, Newport and Wales back-rower says he is 'f****** angry' at the lack of progress he and fellow ex-pros have made in their legal fight

Despite constant legal wranglings, countless court hearings and spicy media headlines, there has been no sign of a resolution to the case.

Last month, the legal action involving Popham and more than 500 rugby claimants was brought back from the brink of collapse after the High Court gave a reprieve to those who had previously been struck out from the case for failing to disclose necessary neurological testing information to the defendants.

‘I’m f****** angry,’ says Popham, his voice regularly cracking with both raw emotion and genuine fury. ‘We’re six years down the line and we aren’t any further ahead. We're on a f****** hamster wheel that’s just going around and around and around. The job of the defendants is to kick the can down the road for as long as possible.

‘We’re not even arguing over f****** brain damage yet. It’s f****** been six years. What’s being lost in all this is the impact on the humans involved. Think of the people we've lost since 2020.

‘Ex-players have killed themselves because of their suffering – Shane Christie and Billy Guyton in New Zealand. Lots of ex-players are struggling badly. Some have lost everything.

‘They are sofa surfing or washing in streams. Some are homeless. We’ve got a lot of vulnerable ex-players who want their day in court.’

That day still looks a long, long way off. After ditching their previous legal team – led by Richard Boardman of Rylands Garth – Popham and his fellow claimants now have new representation in their search for victory over World Rugby, the game’s governing body, as well as England’s RFU and the Welsh Rugby Union.

In November, the claimants’ new legal team KP Law must satisfy the court they are able to provide the documentary information required for the case to continue.

Popham is frustrated that in the six years since he and Thompson raised their heads above the parapet, rugby’s safety has not improved

'I don't think people appreciate the ripple effect that comes when you’re suffering with these issues,' says Popham. 'It’s a rollercoaster of emotions'

The inertia is doing no good to anyone. Not the ex-players who are struggling, nor the game’s standing and reputation. Popham believes rugby’s authorities are looking to delay a trial for as long as possible. But there can be no doubt that the claimants have questions to answer too.

Popham admits it was ‘tough’ to move on from Boardman and that he did an ‘unreal’ job, but the reality is the size of the case was too big for his small firm.

He is frustrated that in the six years since he and Thompson raised their heads above the parapet, rugby’s safety has not improved.

‘Seasons are longer. There are more games,’ says Popham. ‘They’ve put in guidelines for the number of games players should play (30 full matches in a season). But guys like Maro Itoje, Tommy Freeman and Henry Slade have gone over them. What’s the point in those guidelines if they’re broken?

‘They’re a PR tick to say we’re looking after players. It's the same with the guidelines on contact in training. It's all smoke and mirrors to portray that they care. Do they f***.

‘I can't wait for it to get to court. We just want to know our story has been listened to. If we go to court and we lose, we lose. I want to see it all the way. My personal view is we wouldn’t be happy to settle before court because that wouldn’t lead to changes to make rugby safer.

‘A similar case in the NFL ended in a settlement, but they didn’t accept their role in causing the problem. We would want some changes made that would make rugby as safe as it can be. We’ve got to leave rugby in a better, safer place.

‘That’s what we want. Rugby can continue, but there's got to be huge, huge changes. Players are getting bigger, faster, stronger. There's more internationals and that's to make more money. There is so much rugby. A model like the one Mike Tindall was trying to do with R360, where players were only going to be playing 16 or 17 games a year, is the only way you’re going to stop what’s been going on.

‘They’ve put in guidelines for the number of games players should play. But guys like Maro Itoje have gone over them. What's the point in those guidelines if they’re broken?'

Steve Thompson, a World Cup winner with England in 2003, has early onset dementia and probable CTE

‘I still love the game, but we're not being honest. I've had so much s*** from people saying I’m trying to ruin it. I couldn’t look in the mirror if I stuck my head in the sand and was not being truthful about what is happening. I'm happy to shout from the rooftops about this. I genuinely don't give a f*** about what people think of me.

'I'm not trying to ruin rugby. Rugby is ruining itself. The game as it is, is not safe. So many lives are being affected by it. Kids are starting contact in rugby at nine and should not be doing it. No way.

'Parents aren’t being told the truth. I won't let Darcy my youngest even play touch rugby anymore. It’s sad to say because I love rugby. But I've changed over this six-year period as I’ve become more educated on this issue.'

November is likely to be a last chance saloon for Popham and Co. He says the difference between KP Law’s work and that of Rylands has been ‘night and day’ though the former still have a significant task at hand to appease those heading up a legal case which retains the potential to be one of the most seismic ever seen in professional sport.

If the claimants successfully prove their neurodegenerative diseases are a result of head injuries suffered while playing and that the authorities were negligent in not helping to prevent them, a significant payout would be expected.

A repeat of the more than $1billion handed out by the NFL would ruin World Rugby, the RFU and WRU altogether.

Rugby's authorities deny breaching a duty of care and say safety rules have been updated.

World Rugby said last month: ‘With new legal representation now in place for the players, we hope that the litigation can move forward in accordance with the court’s expectations and in the best interests of the players and the sport.’

'I think of my brain like a kettle and I never allow it to boil over,' admits Popham. 'It's not normal'

Popham, who won 33 caps for his country, says: ‘We just want to speed up this process now to be able to move forward. Hopefully, we’ll get a date for trial in the next two years maximum.

'I don't think people appreciate the ripple effect that comes when you’re suffering with these issues. It’s a rollercoaster of emotions you go through and that can have a big impact on someone who doesn’t have a strong family network. It’s tough.

'I’ve only got a certain bandwidth for how I live day to day. I haven't got the brain capacity of a normal person, so I just try to manage it. I think of my brain like a kettle and I never allow it to boil over. It's not normal. I really, really struggle with sensory overload. If I allow myself to live how I was living before, that's when things build up and there'd be an explosion.

‘It's not a case of living normally as I should be as a 46-year-old. I’ve got brain damage in 14 areas that affects my day-to-day life. It’s as a result of playing rugby.’

For confidential support, call Samaritans on 116 123, visit samaritans.org or visit https://www.thecalmzone.net/get-support

Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo look reborn under Andoni Iraola - but Dominik Szoboszlai wonder strike steals the show as Liverpool pile pressure on Roberto De Zerbi
Sports.content:
It was the reaction of those not in Dominik Szoboszlai's close proximity that helped one understand the true genius behind his strike.

Defender Ronald Araujo ran to the dugouts and zipped along on the sodden turf on his knees like it was he who had scored – and done so in the World Cup final to boot.

Alexander Isak, one of the best strikers in the game, was less animated but put his hands to his head.

Awestruck, yes. Shocked, maybe not. Szoboszlai does this in training a lot and he, like his idol and predecessor to the No 8 shirt at Liverpool in Steven Gerrard, knows how to strike a ball from distance.

'It was scary, not many hit a ball like Dom,' said man-of-the-match Lewis Koumas, the academy starlet who shone.

The Hungarian chested down a loose ball, let it bounce once and unleashed a thunderous strike from 30 yards. It was an early goal-of-the-season contender and helped Liverpool progress in the Carabao Cup at the expense of a wasteful Tottenham Hotspur.

Alexis Mac Allister celebrates scoring his second goal in his last two starts for Liverpool

Cody Gakpo is flying once more after coming close to leaving Liverpool in the summer

The victory was rounded off by a goal-of-the-season contender from Dominik Szoboszlai

Szoboszlai put his finger to his ear in a gesture that might have been directed at those who gave him criticism at the weekend for a poor off-the-ball performance. Some might see him as arrogant, but if you can score goals like that, who wouldn't be?

'The goal is a worldie, outstanding,' said Iraola. 'The thing with Dom is before shooting, you trust him. With other players you might think it is too far away. With Dom, everyone is thinking he might score.'

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Mamardashvili 7.5; Frimpong 6, Araujo 6.5, Gomez 7 (Jacquet 46, 7), Kerkez 6; Nyoni 7 (Gravenberch 62, 6), Mac Allister 8; Ngumoha 7 (Barcola 72, 6), McConnell 7 (Szoboszlai 62, 6); Gakpo 7; Koumas 8 Subs not used: Alisson, Endo, Isak, Munoz, Chambers. Booked: Araujo, Frimpong, Kerkez, Iraola Scorers: Mac Allister 21, Gakpo 54, Szoboszlai 90+1 Manager: Andoni Iraola 7 TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR (4-2-3-1): Dubravka 6; Gray 6, Tosin 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 57, 6); Bentancur 6 (Fernandes 57, 6), Bergvall 6.5; Kudus 6 (Savio 75, 6), Gallagher 7 (Maddison 75, 6), Tel 5 (Solanke 85); Marmoush 5 Subs not used: Kinsky, Van Hecke, Davies, Van de Ven Booked: Marmoush, Bentancur Scorer: Gallagher 69 Manager: Roberto De Zerbi 5 Man of the Match: Koumas

The super strike ended a nail-biting finale at Anfield that saw Conor Gallagher pull a goal back, Omar Marmoush be denied by a finger-tip save and his fellow Manchester City bench-warmer Savio drag a shot wide.

Szoboszlai will take the acclaim as he often does but this victory equally belonged to his team-mates and the supporting cast after Andoni Iraola made 10 changes from the side that looked lethargic and devoid of ideas in a 0-0 weekend draw with Fulham.

The main architects of the win were two players who have points to prove at the club.

One feels unwanted amid a contract stand-off, the other the opposite after a summer departure was kiboshed – but Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo combined to lethal effect here.

First up was Mac Allister, the Argentine who last week revealed he was 'very sad' with the club for not putting a new contract on the table for him and saying they were not in a position to extend his deal at the club.

He has talked the talk but is walking the walk, this his second goal in the two starts since then after a starring role and strike against Atletico Madrid six days ago.

Sadly for the midfielder and his camp, including father Carlos, it appears Liverpool are benefiting from the uncertainty around him. He is playing with a point to prove and this frustrated version of Mac Allister is markedly better than the sloppy, lethargic version of last term.

His goal was a fine, curling finish with the inside of his foot after 21 minutes after Gakpo and Rio Ngumoha combined well and worked the ball into Mac Allister's path, via the help of an unfortunate toe from Destiny Udogie.

Then there is Gakpo. Had the summer window panned out ever so slightly differently, the Dutchman would be at Manchester City or Spurs right now, with both clubs at different times confident of signing him during a saga that felt like it was destined to end with an exit.

The pressure will pile on Roberto De Zerbi after Spurs were dumped out of the cup

Lewis Koumas, one of several youngsters trusted by Andoni Iraola in this new era, was energetic throughout

But Liverpool ultimately pulled the plug on those moves and, like his fellow goal-scorer, Gakpo is flying once more, with two goals and four assists in his first five appearances of the season.

Gakpo's strike was a thumping finish after Mac Allister's incisive assist.

Both cases should serve as a reminder to fans to not write off players so quickly. Neither were anywhere near their best last term but both have looked reborn under Iraola.

Another thing the new boss has given is a trust in youth. Koumas, 20, was the man of the match here in an outstanding display. Iraola described him as 'contagious' which is bang on: the Chester-born forward is a bundle of energy leading from the front.

Koumas spent the second half of last season on loan at Hull City and was a substitute in the play-off final. Few then could have foreseen his rise, but his hard work, attitude and pressing ability have impressed Iraola. Midfielder James McConnell is also worthy of praise.

Another deserving of a shout-out is goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili.

Despite being the first top-flight goalkeeper to concede to Tottenham this season, and being at fault for flapping at a cross in the process, it could have been more if not for two fine saves – one at the start to deny Lucas Bergvall, the other in the dying stages to thwart Marmoush.

Conor Gallagher had halved Liverpool's lead, heading home a Matheus Fernandes corner, and Anfield was soon transformed into a theatre of nerves once more but big Georgian Mamardashvili, plus Szoboszlai's wonder-strike, saw the Reds into the next round.

Roberto De Zerbi said he had won games playing much worse than tonight and he is right. But the Italian could do with a lucky break after blanking four times in the league and already being dumped out of the cup.

Spurs were better here and could have got a result on another day. De Zerbi said: 'We have to shoot more times, we have to shoot better, we have to finish better the clear situations, but we are sorry for the result, disappointed, frustrated for the result.

'I think it's unfair, but we have to accept it and to be stronger than this unlucky moment.'

Sports.title: Forget blaming JJ Gabriel - it is Man United's fault the 15-year-old wants to leave, writes OLIVER HOLT. Why would his family entrust the future of English football's hottest youth property to the greedy Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe?
Sports.content:
Forget blaming JJ Gabriel - it is Man United's fault the 15-year-old wants to leave, writes OLIVER HOLT. Why would his family entrust the future of English football's hottest youth property to the greedy Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe?

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

When a young player wants to leave a football club, it is a default mechanism in the culture of English football to blame the kid for being a prima donna with ideas above his station or, more often, point the finger at a pushy parent or an unscrupulous agent for putting dollar signs ahead of development. And so it has been with JJ Gabriel.

When the news broke on Tuesday afternoon that Gabriel, who is 15 years old and perhaps the most feted young player at Manchester United since Ryan Giggs, had asked to leave the club ahead of his 16th birthday next month, it was greeted with a mixture of dismay and horror at Old Trafford.

But instead of blaming the kid or his parents or an intermediary, or all three, the breakdown in relations between Gabriel and the club feels more like yet the latest symbol of the decline of a club that is learning the hard way that more than a decade of mismanagement at the top of the organisation comes with consequences.

At one level, that means that United can no longer attract the best players in the transfer market. This summer, Elliot Anderson, Mateus Fernandes, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Adam Wharton were said to be United's top targets in their attempts to strengthen their midfield. None of them came.

Fernandes and Tonali went to Spurs, Guimaraes went to Arsenal, Anderson went to Manchester City, Wharton stayed at Crystal Palace. United had to settle for Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, all good players but not good enough to close the gap to the teams already ahead of United.

That is the reality for United now. They are not the preferred destination for the best players in the world. Even on the back of a positive season last season when Michael Carrick and Steve Holland took the team back into the top four, United's recruitment let them down in the summer and they have started this season poorly.

Manchester United's teenage prodigy JJ Gabriel, 15, announced on Tuesday that he wants out

The breakdown in relations between Gabriel and the club feels more like yet the latest symbol of the decline of Manchester United

Who can blame him for wanting to leave the club with the way Sir Jim Ratcliffe is running it

The club is still a mess of dysfunction. The idea that they will fix the team department by department, moving on to replace a creaking defence in the next summer window, is deeply flawed. The dynamics of football teams do not work like that. It feels, once more, as if United are going backwards.

And then there is the farrago involving the club declaring war on a section of its own fans. They are trying to root out ticket touts, the club says, but the removal of hundreds of supporters' season tickets has created a poisonous atmosphere at Old Trafford at a time when Carrick least needs it.

Think about that and it feels rather amusing that some are accusing those around Gabriel of greed. Greed? United and their current clutch of misbegotten owners wrote the book on it. If there is any moral high ground in an episode like this, United will find it very hard to scramble up to it.

Switch the question around. Why would the hottest youth property in English football want to stay with the modern Manchester United? Why would JJ Gabriel's parents entrust their son to club owners like the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe? It is not surprising that the lad is looking for a way out. It would be more surprising if he wasn't.

I saw Gabriel play for United in the FA Youth Cup against Oxford United at the Kassam Stadium last February and it was obvious that all the hype about him was true. He was a special talent. It was not just that he was electric with the ball at his feet, he had an instinctive awareness of space and how to find it and vision that went beyond his years.

It is said that Carrick was planning to include him in the United squad for the Carabao Cup tie against Brighton on Wednesday evening but it may be that the club has missed a trick by not making him part of the first team at an earlier opportunity. It may be that, even at 15, Gabriel felt he was being held back.

It was expected that Gabriel was to be a part of Michael Carrick's (left) squad to face Brighton

Arsenal, for instance, handed debuts to their own prodigies, Max Dowman and Ethan Nwaneri, as 15-year-olds. Dowman, who has already announced himself as a spectacularly precocious talent, scored in the Premier League last season and was used in the title run-in by Mikel Arteta.

It is said that United are still hopeful they can repair the situation and retain Gabriel's services but it already feels as if it will be hard to come back from a fracture of such a public nature.

The older fans amongst us may still associate United with the Busby Babes and the Class of 92 and all the glories and the romance that came with those groups of home-grown players. But those days are long gone and the club that produced them disappeared long, long ago.

Sports.title: Nick Woltemade is ripped apart by Italian press weeks after loan move to Juventus - as £69m Newcastle flop is accused of 'doing everything WRONG'
Sports.content:
Nick Woltemade is ripped apart by Italian press weeks after loan move to Juventus - as £69m Newcastle flop is accused of 'doing everything WRONG'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The Italian media have ripped into Newcastle flop Nick Woltemade despite the German striker having only just moved to Juventus.

Woltemade, 24, joined the Italian giants on a season-long loan on Deadline Day, and he has made two substitute appearances over the past few weeks.

However, after Sunday's 3-2 defeat by Sassuolo - a game in which Woltemade missed two clear-cut chances - Italian outlet Gazzetta dello Sport were heavily critical of his display.

'Woltemade is clearly having major problems integrating himself into the team's dynamic,' they wrote.

'He tried his best. But in the decisive moments, he lacks clarity in his actions, which is particularly noticeable in these games where every action can be crucial.'

They added: 'Woltemade squanders: The German lacks precision and does everything wrong.'

The Italian media have ripped into Newcastle flop and Juventus loanee Nick Woltemade

Woltemade has struggled in his two substitute appearances since joining the Italian giants

Woltemade and fellow attacker Randal Kolo Muani, who struggled on loan at Tottenham last season, have come under particularly heavy criticism after being two of the club's statement summer signings.

Writing about the pair - who are yet to 'make a difference' since joining - the same outlet said: 'Four games and not a single goal, plus several scenes that quickly circulated as mocking social media clips among rival fans.

'Clumsy ball control, botched back heel flicks that landed at the feet of the opposition, and – what is particularly troubling – hardly any dangerous scoring opportunities. No, this cannot continue. Juventus' attack is not working.'

That view was echoed elsewhere, with Corriere dello Sport similarly brutal in their assessment of the two strikers.

'How annoying is it when the very new signings you chased for months (and paid far too much for) turn out to be the biggest disappointments of the team?,' they wrote.

The latest criticism for Woltemade comes after Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti bizarrely compared him to 'a horse that likes to be petted and ridden' after his debut.

The German striker had come off the bench in the 75th minute of a clash against AC Milan, with Juventus trailing 1-0.

Woltemade nearly made an immediate impact when the ball fell kindly for him in the penalty area and he swung a boot at it, but was ultimately unable to keep his shot down as the chance went begging.

Woltemade did manage to win a free-kick in stoppage time, however, and the Turin side capitalised, with Federico Gatti heading home a dramatic equaliser to secure a valuable point against Ruben Amorim's side.

After the match, Spalletti compared his new player to a Friesian horse, the breed known for its long, flowing mane and tail.

Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti previously bizarrely compared Woltemade to a Friesian horse

Spalletti told Tuttosport: 'What type of horse is he? I have a Friesian, he seems very similar to me.

'He is statuesque, he inspires a bit of fear from a physical point of view and then he is very sweet and lets himself be stroked and ridden.

'He becomes very good also in relations with his teammates. He’s good at holding his own physically, and ever since I met him, he’s been smiling constantly. He’s so happy to be here, and that’s already a big thing.'

Juventus have seven points from four Serie A games so far this season, and are back in action on Thursday when they take on NEC Nijmegen in the Europa League.

Sports.title: Moment Raheem Sterling is arrested with balloons and canisters in his £270,000 Lamborghini as he pleads GUILTY to dangerous driving and drug possession after crash while on 'hippy crack'
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling told police he had 'a problem' with laughing gas after submitting rush hour motorists to a terrifying 90-minutes of dangerous driving in his Lamborghini while high on the chemical.

The former England international, 31, zigzagged across the M25 and M3 motorways in his car, forcing other motorists to get out of his way, before swerving onto a slip road and crashing into a metal gate.

He was arrested by police who claim he tried to hide nitrous oxide, or laughing gas, from them by moving it to the back seat of his black Lamborghini Urus SUV, which is worth around £270,000.

Police bodycam footage shows the moment that Sterling was arrested with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap. An officer can be heard saying 'you can put that down' to the footballer after opening his car door.

He can then be seen taking the items from his lap and putting them behind his seat.

Sterling is asked 'can you jump out for me' and who was at the wheel at the time of the crash, but does not reply.

Police bodycam footage shows the moment Raheem Sterling is arrested with canisters and a deflated balloon on his lap

Image issued by the Crown Prosecution Service shows the damage to the Lamborghini Urus being driven by Sterling

The former England international was pictured arriving in court today to face charges following a car crash in May

Sterling, 31, crashed his £270,000 Lamborghini Urus and was charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas

The officer adds: 'So you refuse to answer, okay.'

Sterling is told to get out of the car, asked his name and age at the roadside and to 'put the phone down, stop playing games. Stop tensing up.'

The former Manchester City and Chelsea star is then read his rights as he is arrested after being asked to put his arms behind his back.

His arrest, near the Minley interchange on the M3 in Hampshire, happened four weeks after he had returned to the UK following the end of an abortive attempt to revive his football career at Dutch club Feyenoord.

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty on Tuesday to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen after a single vehicle collision at 8.45am on May 28. Police found six cannisters of nitrous oxide in his car.

Basingstoke Magistrates' Court heard that Sterling was so impaired by the laughing gas that he was unable to perform basic police station tests like placing his finger on his nose or placing one foot in front of another.

Barrister Simon Jones, prosecuting, said of Sterling: 'He appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting. Eye lids drooping consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He said he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.'

Motorist Fiona Jennings told police she had looked across to witness the driver of the Lamborghini with a balloon in front of his face which was so big she thought it was an air bag.

Nitrous oxide cannisters were found in the car after it was stopped by police

Sterling, from Berkshire, pleaded guilty on Tuesday to dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen

Image shows the damage to the Lamborghini Urus which was being driven by Sterling when he was detained by police officers

It was so big that 'she had no idea how the driver would have been able to see the road ahead,' Mr Jones said. Ms Jennings described Sterling's driving as 'absolutely horrendous' and expressed 'genuine concern that the driver may kill someone.'

Evidence presented to court suggested Sterling was also inhaling laughing gas while at the wheel of the Lamborghini a full seven hours before his arrest.

A concerned witness called police after seeing the driver of the same car entering a McDonalds car park alarmingly fast at 1.10am the same morning and seeing the driver holding up 'a pink, inflated balloon.'

By 7.45am that morning, another motorist concerned by the Lamborghini erratically changing lanes, saw the driver placing a white balloon to his mouth and inhaling its contents. For 30 minutes, that motorist watched the vehicle weave from inside to outside lane and back and come close to smashing into the central reservation.

It was after Sterling had left the M3 near Farnborough, Hampshire, hit the gate and come to halt with the tyres of his wheels ripped up, that police found him sitting in T-shirt and shorts in the passenger seat of the car.

One officer told him to 'stop tensing up' after he had stepped out of the car. Sterling replied: 'I'm not tensing up.' Sterling provided breath tests, which established he was not under the influence of cannabis, cocaine or alcohol. But he later refused requests for a blood test, insisting that a lawyer of his choosing must be present, having rejected the offer of a duty solicitor. He also refused to answer any police questions.

Mr Jones said of Sterling's conduct: 'He was attempting to impose a condition on provision of a specimen. He was told the investigation could not be delayed for that reason. At the roadside, there was cooperation without the need for legal advice. When the search for the presence of drugs started, the cooperation ended.'

Sterling's barrister, Jason Bartfeld QC, told the court that there was 'extensive personal mitigation' in his case and that the footballer had taken 'voluntary steps to mitigate his difficulties.'

Mr Bartfeld agreed that this was a 'top category case' because it was a prolonged period of dangerous driving and Sterling was suffering 'serious impairment'. But he said the nitrous oxide would only have caused impairment in 'short periods' and that the chemical did not pose the same risks as cannabis or alcohol.

He claimed police had left Sterling confused about the blood sample. Sterling later told police in a statement: 'I asked for a solicitor. I did not fully understand I had not slept all night and was tired and confused.'

Sterling could face a maximum two years' imprisonment. The case was adjourned until November for pre-sentencing reports.

Sports.title: Mercurial Max Dowman makes a mockery of his opponents in Arsenal's 4-2 win at Ipswich: Star, 16, further stakes his claim for first-team place - Man United wantaway JJ Gabriel should take note, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
Mercurial Max Dowman makes a mockery of his opponents in Arsenal's 4-2 win at Ipswich: Star, 16, further stakes his claim for first-team place - Man United wantaway JJ Gabriel should take note, writes ISAAN KHAN

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

In the red half of Manchester, a 15-year-old child in JJ Gabriel is trying to force a way out of his club.

It's a markedly different story in the red portion of London, Max Dowman, 16, lighting up Portman Road to further bolster his case of regularly breaking into the Arsenal first team.

That is not a given, for the likes of World Cup winners Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi have yet to start in the Premier League this season, for example. Yet, Dowman is a mercurial talent, one who we'll see plenty of in the months ahead.

Having intercepted the ball in midfield, the teenager played a one-two pass with Eberechi Eze before sprightly running towards the box.

Ipswich Town's Cedric Kipre tried, and failed, to tackle the youngster while back-pedalling, before hitting the deck. Dowman reached the area before powerfully striking past goalkeeper Christian Walton on seven minutes with his weaker right foot.

The way he had embarrassed a burly 6ft 3in defender 13 years older than himself reflected what Dowman has done in his short senior career thus far: make a mockery of those much older than he.

Max Dowman (right) scored twice for Arsenal as they won 4-2 at Ipswich in the Carabao Cup

Dowman watches on as his shot flies towards the back of the goal for a fine individual opener

The 16-year-old watches on after scoring his second and the Gunners' third of the night

The attacker, playing in the No 10 role, wasn't done there. Two minutes into the second period, Zubimendi's prodded pass found the teenager into the area, who softly curled the ball home for a second goal.

Amid these strikes, he constantly looked for through balls and, in a big improvement from last season, tracked back to help his team out in defence. So, a mature performance all round.

Mikel Arteta was left purring over Dowman. He said: 'That's something very natural for him, and he can deliver those actions effortlessly. That's his biggest quality.

'He's an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play at the biggest stage and still handle the situation with such naturality.

'At 16 to already do what he does, it's just incredible.'

It was also a promising  to talented youths across the country - like Gabriel. Despite Arsenal's strength in depth as reigning Premier League champions, there is still a pathway for youngsters to breakthrough.

Dowman wasn't the only example here, Marli Salmon, 17, starting at centre back. He occasionally strayed out of position, but looked comfortable on the ball and played some solid attacking passes. He did his prospects no harm in his display, either, in a line-up involving four teenagers, including Myles Lewis-Skelly, 19, and later substitute Theo Julienne, 18.

Arteta opted to start Bukayo Saka and bring Declan Rice off the bench in the Carabao Cup third round against Port Vale last season. This time around, he had Saka on the bench and Rice at home.

Dowman's time at Arsenal contrasts with the situation of wantaway JJ Gabriel at Man United

After the insane workloads both players endured previously, Arteta seems to have learned his lesson, a positive step in the right direction.

A quirky defence featured midfielder Zubimendi at right back, while Viktor Gyokeres was given a chance up front again after starting against Napoli in the Champions League last week.

A goal up from Dowman's strike, Noni Madueke doubled Arsenal's lead after a crunching Bruno Guimaraes tackle set the ball loose.

It fell to Merino, his chip over the top reaching Madueke. He opened up his body and rifled the ball home with the outside of his left boot.

The shackled were completely off just 16 minutes in, the Gunners' players queuing to try get their names on the scoresheet.

Dowman added Arsenal's third in the second half, before Merino latched onto Zubimendi's pass - which Dowman faintly touched - and struck from outside the area, the ball cannoning in off the left post.

Anis Mehmeti pulled back a consolation goal for Ipswich, with Hale End graduate Chuba Akpom also making the scoresheet in injury time for the home side, though the night belonged to Dowman.

JJ Gabriel would be wise to take note.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace chairman Steve Parish frustrated with new boss Pierre Sage for dropping Jaydee Canvot just four games into the season
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace chairman Steve Parish is understood to have been frustrated by Pierre Sage’s choice to drop Jaydee Canvot for Saturday’s defeat by Ipswich Town.

Sage described the decision to leave the defender out of the squad as a ‘sporting’ one, following a poor display against Fulham the previous weekend and a disappointing week in training.

But Daily Mail Sport understands his stern treatment of Canvot, a young, valuable asset, has gone down badly in the boardroom.

The 20-year-old became a regular starter in the second half of last season after Marc Guehi joined Manchester City and had started Palace’s first three Premier League games under new boss Sage.

The French coach was previously praised for his hardline approach towards understudies Dwight McNeil and Evann Guessand, leaving them out against Fulham to provoke a response.

However, Canvot is viewed internally as a key part of the project and his omission has therefore been taken more negatively.

Pierre Sage leaving Jaydee Canvot out has been viewed negatively at Crystal Palace

Canvot (pictured) became a regular starter in the second half of last season after Marc Guehi joined Manchester City

Steve Parish is understood to have been frustrated by Sage’s choice to drop Canvot for Palace's defeat against Ipswich Town

Palace have suffered a disappointing start to the season, losing three of their opening four Premier League matches, including the 3-2 loss to newly-promoted Ipswich.

Sage has not yet had his best team to choose from, with Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta among those sidelined.

Their defence is unsettled, though, conceding 11 goals in their first four league games - a worse rate than Sheffield United managed during their record-breaking 2023-24 campaign, when they shipped 104 goals.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner, who won the FA Cup and Conference League while at Selhurst Park.

The Frenchman arrived from Lens, where he won the French Cup and guided the club to a second-place finish in Ligue 1.

Sports.title: Harry Brook's stunning 42-ball hundred makes you wonder what Kevin Pietersen actually has to teach him, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Harry Brook's stunning 42-ball hundred makes you wonder what Kevin Pietersen actually has to teach him, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

On nights like this, you wonder what Kevin Pietersen might usefully teach Harry Brook.

As England's new white-ball mentor watched on admiringly from the Utilita Bowl dressing-room, their captain inspired his team to a massive 119-run win over Sri Lanka with a scintillating 42-ball century, confirming his status as the world's most exciting all-format batsman.

Pietersen would have been thrilled to have played such an innings, and not just because he never made a T20 hundred for England.

On Instagram, Ben Stokes – who had pushed for Brook to replace him as Test captain, before the job went to Joe Root – evidently agreed: 'I don't think even the genius of KP could come close to what Harry Brook has talent-wise… You are an absolute freak, Harry.'

Brook's innings contained all the daring and verve that once made Pietersen an outlier in English cricket, and plenty of the power too: after the early loss of debutant Aneurin Donald for 12, including a third-ball six, he responded by pummelling 30 off an over from the left-arm spin of Dunith Wellalage. After that, the Sri Lankans looked broken.

Brook later admitted that he had been watching highlights of Pietersen's batting during the 2005 Ashes on his phone, marvelling at the way he hit the ball to unusual parts of the ground. 'Hopefully he can have a big impact on my career,' he said. 'It's awesome to have a man of his calibre in the changing-room.'

Harry Brook hit a scintillating 42-ball century to power England to victory over Sri Lanka

On nights like this, you wonder what Kevin Pietersen might usefully teach Brook

The only pity is that Brook and Pietersen never got a chance to bat together. Instead, Brook had to make do with the companionship of Jos Buttler, who followed his 131 off 64 balls here against India in July with a brutal 80 off 44, and looked well rested thanks to a month off after the Hundred final. On another night, he would have been the headline act.

But it was Brook who stole the show in the first of six white-ball games against the Sri Lankans, having insisted to head coach Brendon McCullum that he didn't want to sit out the series and take a rare breather after the Test series against Pakistan.

That was just as well for a crowd of over 11,000 in Southampton, where in three successive T20 internationals the locals have been thoroughly spoiled, witnessing England totals of 248 for three against West Indies last summer, 257 for three against India and now 254 for four – their third-, fourth- and fifth-highest scores ever.

When Brook reached 94 off 38 balls, he had a chance to equal Phil Salt's England-record for the quickest T20 century. But he could only slice Dasun Shanaka for two to deep point, and in the end had to settle for equalling Liam Livingstone's 42-ball effort against Pakistan at Trent Bridge in 2021.

His eventual 114 off 49, with 10 fours and six sixes, meant his last three T20 innings have brought him 288 runs without being dismissed. No one would bet against him breaking Indian Tilak Varma's world-record unbeaten sequence of 336 when these teams meet in Cardiff on Thursday because no bowler right now seems capable of stopping him.

'I feel like I've let myself down a couple of times this summer,' he said. 'Thankfully I didn't give up that opportunity today. It was a special feeling to get to three figures.'

Sri Lanka will need to improve quickly if they are to have even a sniff. Faced with a mammoth target, they were three down in the six-over powerplay, with Sonny Baker taking his first white-ball international wickets, and limped to 135.

This was their 13th successive T20 defeat by England, a sequence that stretches back a dozen years and now looks in danger of extending beyond the summer. The punishment may barely have begun.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Reds confirm midfielder return as star admits regret at Anfield exit
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Reds confirm midfielder return as star admits regret at Anfield exit

Liverpool have been busy behind the scenes even after the summer transfer window shut

View 2 Images Liverpool have confirmed a new addition as manager Andoni Iraola prepares to take on former club Bournemouth (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

This weekend brings a big test for Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola, who will lead the Reds out against his former club Bournemouth. Both teams have drawn three of their first four matches but victory on the south coast could help the new boss kick-start his spell on Merseyside.

‌



The first four league matches of the season have brought questions about squad balance despite the addition of France star Bradley Barcola. Things haven't quietened down on the transfer front despite the window shutting on September 1, with another new addition confirmed on Tuesday.

‌



Iraola will have time to take stock of his options after that match at the Vitality Stadium. An extended international window means Premier League teams will go three weeks without a game, with Liverpool hosting Manchester City when they return from the break on October 11.

‌



We've got more information on the Reds' latest transfer business as well as a former star whose time at Anfield was arguably too short-lived. Here is the latest news coming out of Anfield...

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk holds meeting with boss to decide future READ MORE :

Farkas completes Anfield return

Hungarian youngster Patrik Farkas has rejoined Liverpool for a second spell, the club have confirmed. Farkas spent a year in the Reds' academy before joining Blackburn in 2022 and will now link up with the Reds' Under-21 squad.

‌



"It's a dream come true to sign here, I'm really happy and just excited to get started," said the midfielder, whose brother Erik plays for Liverpool's Under-18s. "I'm enjoying being back at Liverpool, there are some new faces but it's good to meet everyone and also see lots of old friends as well.

"I'm a technical player, a box-to-box player who can play in multiple positions and try to make things happen. The coaches have just asked me to excite them, to get playing, be confident and show them what I can do. From there anything can happen. Work hard and take the next step from there."

Luis Alberto's exit regret

View 2 Images Luis Alberto played just 12 competitive games for Liverpool (Image: AMA/Corbis via Getty Images)

‌



Former Liverpool midfielder Luis Alberto believes he may have been too quick to leave the club. The Spaniard was signed by Brendan Rodgers at the age of 20 but made just 12 appearances and left for Lazio after two loan spells in his three years at Anfield.

"I came to England because of Brendan Rodgers," the 33-year-old told ABC. "I knew it wasn’t going to be easy; going from Barcelona B to Liverpool was a big change, and that was to be expected. I trained, did what they asked of me, and got a few games and some playing time.

“I always say I made a mistake by not accepting reality. I should have stayed longer, even if it would have taken me some time to break into the plans, I wasn’t patient enough, and I left the following year.”

Sports.title: Man Utd news: JJ Gabriel drops exit bombshell as Wayne Rooney questions squad decision
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: JJ Gabriel drops exit bombshell as Wayne Rooney questions squad decision

Manchester United will look to bounce back from their Premier League defeat to Manchester City as they face Brighton in the Carabao Cup

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel has stunned Manchester United by asking to leave (Image: Getty)

Manchester United host Brighton in the third round of the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening. Michael Carrick had planned to name 15-year-old JJ Gabriel in his matchday squad, but the teenager has shockingly requested to leave the club.

‌



Carrick's United haven't started the season in flying form. An opening day 2-0 defeat at the hands of Hull City was quickly forgotten about with a 5-2 win over Ipswich Town. But a disappointing 2-2 draw against Everton came next, followed by a 4-0 win over Sabah FK in the Champions League, then a derby-day defeat against Manchester City.

‌



United failed to score and were held off by the 10-man City on Sunday at Old Trafford, with questions now being asked about the squad. Wednesday evening gives Carrick's side the perfect chance to bounce back in the Carabao Cup against Brighton.

‌



Fans had hoped they might see Gabriel on the teamsheet, with the 15-year-old touted as one of the club's most promising young talents. But that now seems unlikely. Mirror Football takes a look at this bombshell and more news coming out of United.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

JJ Gabriel asks to QUIT Man Utd immediately as club left completely stunned READ MORE :

JJ Gabriel's request

United have been left in a state of shock after Gabriel, who was likely to be handed a spot on the bench and could even have made his competitive debut against the Seagulls, has asked to leave.

‌



View 3 Images Gabriel had embarked on pre-season with the first team (Image: Getty)

Gabriel's request emerged on Tuesday afternoon and it is understood he refused to train with the club in an attempt to quit. He would have become United's youngest-ever player if he had officially debuted against Brighton. Club chiefs have been left bamboozled by the decision and are unsure what exactly has caused this demand to leave. Gabriel has been with United since the age of 11.

However, the club feels the situation is rectifiable. It is understood Gabriel cannot be deregistered, despite his request. He can't sign a professional contract until he turns 17, or a scholarship agreement until he turns 16, but under current rules, he is registered to United until at least the end of this season.

‌



Director Jason Wilcox had to jump in when Gabriel asked to leave the club in 2025 and he was convinced to stay. Gabriel could move abroad when he turns 16 as he has an Irish passport. Barcelona hold a firm interest in the starlet, although clubs in both Germany and England are sure to be on high alert.

Wayne Rooney questions transfer

Elsewhere, United legend Wayne Rooney has questioned Carrick and the club's summer transfer decisions, specifically the signing of Andrey Santos from Chelsea.

‌



View 3 Images Rooney has questioned the signing of Santos (Image: Stick to United)

Speaking on Stick to United after the City loss, Rooney said: "We need to be a bit more clever with the players we're bringing in. What I don't understand is that we've signed [Youri] Tielemans and Santos and then we signed [Carlos] Baleba, who I think is a good signing.

"But then you've got Santos on the bench. So then, when Baleba is fit, is Tielemans gonna go to the bench? Is [Kobbie] Mainoo gonna go to the bench?

Article continues below

"Then you'd have two players you've brought in [benched] or one of your younger players who has probably been United's best player over the last couple of games in Mainoo, on the bench.

"If that's the case, if Carrick doesn't fancy Santos for whatever reason, that signing has still been made, so why has that money not been used on full-backs or another striker?"

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Star makes feelings on new team-mate clear as Mikel Arteta issued warning
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Star makes feelings on new team-mate clear as Mikel Arteta issued warning

Arsenal are aiming to keep their 100% Premier League record going with a win away to Brighton on Saturday afternoon

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has been handed a new warning (Image: Ed Sykes/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

David Raya has opened up on Arsenal newcomer Bruno Guimaraes, dubbing the Brazil international a "warrior" on the pitch. The midfielder was instrumental in keeping the Gunners' Premier League winning record alive, scoring a stunning strike before combining with Mikel Merino and playing Bukayo Saka through to land them a penalty against Sunderland.

‌



The ex-Newcastle star made his thoughts clear about the Black Cats after his goal and heavily impressed his new teammates with his performance. Now, the north London outfit are preparing to visit Brighton on Saturday in a bid to keep their winning streak in the Premier League alive.

‌



Meanwhile, Mikel Arteta has been warned that he is making a huge mistake in not relying on Viktor Gyokeres up top. An ex-Arsenal star claims the club are misusing the Swedish striker after he was involved in major transfer speculation over the summer.

‌



Here, Mirror Football has the latest headlines coming out of the Emirates Stadium.

Mikel Arteta compared to Sir Alex Ferguson after Arsenal take drastic referee action READ MORE :

Arsenal call up summer signing from Man Utd as Mikel Arteta prepares changes READ MORE :

Raya delivers Guimaraes verdict

Raya was full of praise for Guimaraes following his major impact on the squad in their win over Sunderland. After saving Enzo Le Fee's penalty at the Stadium of Light, the Brazilian went up the other end and scored before putting it on a plate for Saka to win a spot kick at the death.

Regarding Guimaraes' influence, the Spanish goalkeeper said: "It is incredible. Obviously, Bruno has been very unlucky with his start. He had two little injuries that kept him out of the team. It is not only the starters, but the people coming from the bench who are really important.

‌



View 3 Images Raya was full of praise for the Brazilian (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

"We had Bruno scoring, and then he and Merino made the pass for Bukayo to win the pen. The whole squad is going to be very important throughout the season."

Pointing out the 28-year-old's physicality, Raya added: "He brings a lot of things. He brings maturity, competitiveness and leadership. He is a warrior, but he is so technically gifted. He reads the game very, very well, and he will put his life [on the line] to defend and attack. He is a fantastic player to have with us - and hopefully he stays free of injury so we can enjoy him a lot."

‌



Mikel Arteta issued warning

Former Arsenal striker Jeremie Aliadiere claims that Arteta is not utilising Gyokeres correctly, stating that the club won't get the best out of the Swede on the bench. Speaking to LiveFootballTickets.com, the ex-Gunner said: "I think he’s just got to be patient, keep the faith, have a strong mindset and mentality and really believe in his quality and that he will turn things around.

"Obviously, I know how difficult it is when suddenly you’re not playing and you’re on the bench and you don’t really understand why. When you look at it, he was the top scorer last year. Obviously there was some criticism and people expected more for the money invested, but in the end he did deliver. I think he scored some important goals and he gives you something different.

View 3 Images Arteta has been told he isn't using Gyokeres correctly (Image: Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



"My only concern is that I just feel we’re not playing the style that suits him, and that’s more my concern. Mikel always seems to go back to Havertz. Even after Havertz was out for a long time, he brought Havertz back in for the big games because Havertz fits the way we play and the style we play.

"We’re not a team that, in transition, just hits the long ball straight away for the striker to run the channels. That’s not really what we do. We like possession, we like to keep the ball and we like to go wide to our wingers. I do feel sometimes, particularly last season, Viktor struggled because he wanted the ball quickly, to be one-v-one with a defender and run the channel, and he never really got that service."

Despite sticking up for Gyokeres, Aliadiere couldn't predict what Arteta could do to fit the striker into the team more than he is now. He added: "So my question is more: can we play with him in this team?

Article continues below

"And we can’t deny when we watch the games that when Havertz plays, he performs and does really well. It’s tough to justify saying Viktor should be in and Havertz should be on the bench when Havertz is doing so well."
