World.title: FM Orbán files criminal complaint over former FM Szijjártó’s countless private jet travels
World.content:
Hungary’s Foreign Minister Anita Orbán has filed a criminal complaint over the use of private and military aircraft for official trips during the tenure of her predecessor, Péter Szijjártó.

Billions in additional costs alleged

Orbán said an internal review of the Foreign Ministry had uncovered serious irregularities and alleged that the routine use of chartered aircraft from 2022 onwards may have caused significant financial damage to the state. She says the ministry increasingly replaced scheduled commercial flights with private or military aircraft even though the number and nature of diplomatic engagements had not changed significantly.

She estimated that private flights between 2022 and 2026 cost around HUF 4 billion (currently more than EUR 10.9 million) more than travelling on scheduled services. This figure, she stressed, does not include the cost of military aircraft, meaning the total could be higher.

According to FM Orbán, they haven’t even considered cheaper options

Orbán also claimed that aircraft were chartered for relatively short journeys to cities including Bratislava, Vienna and Belgrade, where travelling by car or train would have taken only a few hours. She said investigators found no evidence that cheaper travel options had been systematically considered before individual journeys, even though these private flights should have not been considered as an opportunity, according to the policies of the ministry, writes ATV.

On that basis, Orbán said she believed the circumstances raised suspicions of mismanagement causing particularly significant financial damage and potentially involved responsibility among the ministry’s former senior leadership.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s Telegram channel!

Fidesz calls complaint ‘frivolous’

The Fidesz parliamentary group rejected the allegations, calling the complaint frivolous and insisting that Szijjártó’s flights complied fully with the relevant government regulations. The party argued that the former foreign minister’s travel schedule was organised efficiently, claiming that Szijjártó frequently travelled overnight so that he could conduct meetings during the day.

It also said he returned home immediately after official programmes rather than unnecessarily extending his stays abroad. Fidesz further defended Szijjártó’s record as foreign minister, pointing to what it described as record levels of investment and job creation during the period.

Stay up-to-date: Hungarian Parliament elects five new constitutional judges

Szijjártó’s flights have long been controversial

The former foreign minister’s use of private aircraft has attracted media scrutiny for years. According to figures previously published by the Foreign Ministry, 53 private-jet journeys were made for Szijjártó over four years at a reported cost of HUF 4.87 billion (more than EUR 13.3), writes HVG.hu.

The issue has also been complicated by disputes over access to travel-cost information, with the government previously changing legislation concerning the disclosure of such data. The latest complaint is therefore likely to reignite a long-running political dispute over the cost and transparency of Szijjártó’s official travel. Any criminal responsibility, however, remains to be established.

World.title: Exotic South American animal spotted in Hungary’s mountains
World.content:
A trail runner had an extraordinary encounter in the Börzsöny hills after spotting and filming an exotic South American animal wandering through the forest.

Out-of-place exotic animal runs around in Hungary

Dániel Bárdos was running towards the Hárombarát Saddle on Sunday afternoon when he noticed an unusual animal moving through the woodland. He quickly took out his phone and recorded the creature, which appears to be a coati, also known as a red-nosed coati, a relative of the raccoon native to South America.

‘It wasn’t particularly interested in me’

Dániel said the animal was clearly aware of his presence but showed little fear. It continued sniffing and searching for food while moving in his direction, eventually prompting the runner to move away himself. He later shared the footage in the ‘Csak a Börzsöny!’ Facebook group, describing the encounter as an unexpected meeting with a South American mammal.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s Telegram channel!

Is it the same coati seen last year?

The sighting has raised questions because a similar animal was reported in the Börzsöny area on 21 November 2025. At the time, speculation suggested that the coati could have escaped from the Törökmező Tourist Centre and Small Animal Park near Nagymaros. The park did not officially confirm this, however, writes KEMMA.hu.

Following the latest sighting, the park reportedly confirmed that all of its coatis were accounted for. It said it would nevertheless work with the local municipality to try to locate the creature and would be willing to take it in if it was found to be healthy.

The park’s owner believes the animal may instead have escaped from private ownership. Although the two sightings occurred in the same region less than a year apart, there is currently no evidence that they involved the same individual.

Hungary is full of exotic creatures: Hatvanpuszta zebra scandal deepens as details of illegal keeping, escaped animals, and carcasses dumped in a pig pit emerge

Keeping coatis is prohibited in Hungary

Norbert Riezing of the Duna–Ipoly National Park Directorate said that keeping coatis is prohibited in Hungary. The species was added to the European Union’s list of invasive alien species of Union concern in 2016, bringing strict restrictions on keeping, breeding, reproducing and trading the animals.

Certain people who legally owned coatis before the rules took effect on 3 August 2016 were allowed to keep them for the remainder of their natural lives, provided they prevented the animals from escaping or reproducing. For now, the origin of the coati filmed in the Börzsöny remains a mystery.

World.title: Russian Despatch: Moscow Plays Old Cards in Balkan Elections
World.content:
Russia enters autumn in an atmosphere of foreboding. Intensified Ukrainian strikes, a gasoline deficit, and lack of progress on the battlefront are leading more and more people to surmise that the Kremlin is no longer able to wage its war against Ukraine as a distant operation that has little impact on Russian everyday life.

It will only get worse, and soon the regime will demand more sacrifices for its geopolitical adventures.

The date for change looks set for late September, following parliamentary elections.

Though the vote is tightly managed by authorities, the Kremlin still pays lip service to democratic procedures. It avoids taking unpopular steps during the campaign and strives to preserve a semblance of stability at least until after voting day.

World.title: European Parliamentarians Slam Serbia for ‘Disturbing’ Funeral of Ratko Mladic
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp

EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos told a debate in the European Parliament on Tuesday about the glorification of convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic that images from Mladic’s funeral in Belgrade were “profoundly disturbing”.

The debate was held a week after Mladic’s funeral with military honours in Belgrade prompted strong reactions from European institutions and several EU member states.

“It was especially disturbing to see Serbian ministers, state officials and military representatives alongside leaders and politicians from [Bosnia’s Serb-led entity] Republika Srpska, attend the funeral and publicly honour a war criminal,” Kos said.

Serbia is an EU candidate state and Kos said that Belgrade must fulfill its responsibilities. “By applying for EU membership, Serbia committed to our standards, principles, and values,” she said.

“The European Commission has been clear that the glorification of war criminals, genocide denial and revisionism is fundamentally incompatible with these values. It has no place in the EU. It has no place in the EU candidate countries,” she added.

Mladic, who died in The Hague while serving a life sentence for genocide and war crimes, was buried at Belgrade’s Topcider Cemetery in Belgrade on September 7. The funeral service was led by Serbian Orthodox Church Patriarch Porfirije, and Serbian government ministers came to pay their respects.

At Tuesday’s debate, several Croatian MEPs slammed the Serbian administration and President Aleksandar Vucic for their role in Mladic’s funeral.

Davor Ivo Stier, MEP for Croatia’s Croatian Democratic Union, HDZ, which sits with the European People’s Party, EPP, group said Serbian President Vucic “did not organise a state funeral, but as commander in chief, is responsible for the military honours shown to Mladic”.

“We need to be loud and say clearly that our politics towards Serbia have been mild and ineffective and we need to show and decide that there is no place in Europe for those who glorify Ratko Mladic, and we should not give European funds to those who do not want to distance themselves from [former Yugoslav leader] Slobodan Milosevic’s politics,” Stier added.

Tonino Picula, from the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats group in the European Parliament, said that it is “justified to ask whether the European Union needs to continue negotiating with Serbia while this government is in power”.

Helmut Brandstatter, who sits with Renew Europe, said that the EPP should cut its ties with Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party.

“We cannot tolerate the celebration of a war criminal. A government that glorifies such atrocities can never be part of the European Union,” Brandstatter added.

Brandstatter also highlighted that Serbian society is European and that Serbia should be part of the European Union, but as a democracy.

Commenting on Serbia’s upcoming snap elections, Brandstatter said: “He [Vucic] wants to have a small majority again to get our money – and friendship with Russia, and that cannot happen. The Serbs are welcome here but the authoritarian regime is not part of the European Union.”

World.title: Romanian Sheep Farmers’ Protest Turns Violent in Bucharest
World.content:
A protest by Romanian sheep farmers in front of the government building in Bucharest descended into clashes on Tuesday, with riot police using tear gas as groups of demonstrators broke through security cordons and threw objects at officers.

Around 15 people, including seven gendarmes, required medical assistance after being exposed to tear gas. Four people were detained for violent behaviour.

President Nicusor Dan condemned the incidents. “Attacks and assaults, as well as acts of vandalism, are unacceptable and must be severely punished in accordance with the law,” Dan said. Interim Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan said he respected all citizens’ legal right to peaceful protest but Tuesday’s events “degenerated into regrettable acts of violence”.

Thousands of sheep farmers from across Romania had gathered to protest the extension of a ban on live sheep exports until the end of the year. The European Commission imposed the measure following outbreaks of Peste des Petits Ruminants, or sheep and goat plague, citing insufficient preventive measures by Romanian authorities.

Crop farmers also joined the protest, angered by reduced drought compensation. Although they had been promised 100 euros for every hectare of affected crops, they will now receive only 19 euros per hectare, which they say is far below the losses caused by the prolonged drought.

World.title: Police in The Hague Brace for Rallies Ahead of Kosovo Trial Verdict
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp



Supporters of Hashim Thaci and his co-defendants rally in Pristina, September 12, 2026. Photo: EPA/Georgi Licovski .

Ethnic Albanians and supporters of the Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA, are expected to demonstrate in The Hague on Wednesday as Kosovo’s ex-President Hashim Thaci and three other former guerrilla fighters hear their war crimes verdict.

The announcement of demonstrations and of numerous ethnic Albanians travelling to the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague for the verdict has prompted the court and Dutch police in The Hague to take special security measures.

Prior to the verdict, several transitional justice NGOs from Kosovo and Serbia, which are part of the Specialist Chambers’ outreach forum, the Court Information Network, were notified that their scheduled meeting at the court had been cancelled for security reasons.

Sofija Todorovic, director of the Belgrade-based Youth Initiative for Human Rights Serbia, told BIRN that NGOs that were part of the Court Information Network had a meeting planned when the verdict was to be announced in The Hague.

“But we received information from the court that due to the announced demonstrations and the large number of people coming to The Hague for the verdict, basically the circumstances had changed and they could not guarantee that we will not be recognised by someone and will not face some sort of hostility, so they decided to cancel the meeting,” Todorovic said.

Dusan Radakovic, from a North Mitrovica-based civil society organisation, Advocacy Centre for Democratic Culture, ACDC, told BIRN that “the decision to cancel the visit was primarily related to security concerns and the announced large-scale protests, as can also be inferred from the explanation provided in the email informing us about the cancellation. Particular concern was likely related to the protests expected outside the court following the anticipated decision.

“As a lawyer, I considered it a valuable opportunity to directly observe the work of such an important institution at a time when it is dealing with a matter of considerable public significance,” Radakovic said.

A Dutch police spokesperson in The Hague told BIRN: “We do not announce measures taken and we do not comment on threats in general. We know there will be demonstrations and we will be present in the location.”

Angela Griep, the court’s spokesperson, told BIRN that the Kosovo Specialist Chambers was “undertaking all necessary security measures within its authority and responsibilities on 16 September, also taking into account the announced possible protests”.

Thaci, together with former Kosovo parliament Speakers Kadri Veseli and Jakup Krasniqi, and former MP Rexhep Selimi, are accused of committing crimes against humanity – including murder, torture and illegal detention – during the Kosovo conflict in the late 1990s. They have been in detention in The Hague since November 2020 and have all pleaded not guilty.

Prosecutors at the Kosovo Specialist Chambers have called for a 45-year prison sentence. Defence lawyers have urged acquittal.

This is the highest-level case held at the so-called Kosovo Special Court and has been marred by delays and controversy.

It has also been accompanied by protests staged by supporters of the defendants in Pristina, Tirana, Skopje, Strasbourg and The Hague. Many ethnic Albanians consider the court biased against the KLA’s war against repression by the Serbian authorities. The trial has been surrounded by accusations of fake news and hate speech, and has even led to witness intimidation charges and convictions.

Radakovic told BIRN that, “although I can understand the security considerations that may have led to the cancellation of the visit, I believe that such a decision, particularly the way it was communicated, and if no further explanation is provided, may further increase mistrust among certain groups of citizens and reinforce perceptions of insufficient transparency on the part of the court”.

Todorovic told BIRN that the cancellation of the NGOs’ visit was “not in general a good message”. While she understood the importance of security measures, especially for the protection of witnesses, she said this level of security measures for the monitoring of civil society organisations was problematic.

“The monitoring visit does not affect the outcome of the verdict whatsoever, it just is part of a dialogue that should be ongoing in general with the people that work on these topics [of transitional justice] and the work of the court reflects the work of dealing with the past that we have on the ground,” she said.

She added that the cancellation “decreases the trust in the overall impact of the work of the court. That is the big issue and it fuels this feeling of uncertainty among many people who are waiting to see the output of the work of the court while waiting for the verdict.”

Rallies have been announced across Kosovo, with family members and supporters announcing they will be waiting for the verdict at Pristina’s main square starting from Tuesday evening.

The US embassy in Pristina issued a demonstration alert for Wednesday, warning that “these demonstrations may cause large crowds, road closures and severe traffic disruptions. It is advised to limit travel to the immediate area of your residence and to avoid travel to your workplace and schools if your route passes through impacted areas, as you may not be able to complete the journey in a timely manner.”

On September 12, thousands of supporters of the defendants also marched through Kosovo’s capital, Pristina.

Prosecutors accuse the four men of individual and command responsibility for crimes committed against prisoners held at KLA detention facilities in Kosovo and in neighbouring Albania. Those include more than one hundred murders. The charges cover the period during and just after the Kosovo war in 1998 and 1999.

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers was created specifically to try former members of the KLA. As prime minister in 2014, Thaci signed the agreement with the European Union to establish the court.

It is based in The Hague and staffed by international judges and prosecutors due to doubts about the Kosovo justice system’s ability to try former KLA fighters. Veterans are widely viewed as heroes in Kosovo and the potential for witness intimidation was a serious concern.

During the trial, the prosecution argued that the defendants’ senior roles in the KLA meant they were responsible for subordinates who committed crimes. The defence insisted that the KLA did not have a proper army command structure, so the defendants did not have real authority over lower-ranking fighters.

World.title: Albania’s High Court Rules Against Tirana Mayor’s Release
World.content:
Jailed Tirana mayor Erion Veliaj being accompanied to the Constitutional Court in October 2025. Photo: LSA.

Albania’s High Court ruled on Tuesday that Tirana Mayor Erion Veliaj, who is accused of corruption, money laundering and concealment of wealth, should remain in jail after his arrest was challenged in several courts.

Veliaj’s defence has strongly challenged the enforcement measure that has kept him in detention for about a year-and-a-half. After losing an appeal in the Court Against Corruption and Organised Crime of First Instance and Appeals and in the High Court, the case was taken to the Constitutional Court with the argument that the arrest was disproportional.

The Constitutional Court redirected the case to the High Court, which has decided that Veliaj should stay in detention.

The ruling was “an extremely concerning development for the rule of law, legal certainty, fundamental rights, and, above all, for democracy in this country,” his lawyer, Plarent Ndreca, told the media.

Veliaj was arrested in February last year. The Special Prosecution Against Corruption and Organised Crime, SPAK, accused him of creating “a complicated scheme” whereby public money was transferred to a group of NGOs “de facto” run by his wife, Ajola Xoxa, using several local businessmen.

His wife faces the same charges. He and his wife both deny the accusations.

Although his trial is ongoing, there have been no significant developments because of repeated delays.

Only a few days before the latest court ruling, on August 28, Veliaj dismissed Tirana’s acting mayor, Anuela Ristani, and his lawyer declared that he would run the city from pre-detention, asking for “practical conditions” to be provided for this.

Many saw this as an attempt to put pressure on the court by portraying his role in the city as too important to be exercised from a jail.

Albanian analyst Andi Bushati said on Tuesday that following the court decision against Veliaj, he should resign.

“The court decided to keep Veliaj in jail. And now the entire strategy devised in recent weeks risks backfiring on him. If the primary concern up to this point was serving the residents, caring for the city, and ensuring the smooth running of Tirana, shouldn’t Veliaj consider resigning for the sake of these very causes?” Bushati wrote on the Lapsi news site.

Veliaj was dismissed by the Municipality Council in September last year after Prime Minister Edi Rama declared that Tirana needed an active mayor.

New elections for Tirana were called and a campaign started – but the Constitutional Court then ruled in November that the way in which Veliaj had been dismissed was unconstitutional. Therefore he remains mayor of the city.

World.title: Kosovo’s New Govt Challenged in Court as Presidential Pick Withdraws
World.content:
Prime Minister Albin Kurti’s cabinet take their seats in parliament, September 13, 2026. Photo: BIRN.

The opposition Democratic Party of Kosovo, PDK, on Tuesday asked the country’s Constitutional Court to assess whether the parliamentary vote that re-elected Albin Kurti as Kosovo’s Prime Minister three days ago was valid.

“We consider that parliament has been inaugurated by violating the constitution. A parliament which is inaugurated unconstitutionally cannot produce constitutional institutions,” Perparim Gruda, a PDK MP, told media on Tuesday.

“Even earlier, we called [on parliament] to not proceed with further decisions before clarifying question marks,” Gruda added.

Tuesday’s filing by the PDK is the second in as many days that it has taken to the top court. On Monday, it complained to the court that Sunday’s inauguration of parliament had violated the rules.

The PDK claims that Kurti’s ruling Vetevendosje party violated the 30-day deadline to inaugurate parliament and that the assembly cannot be considered inaugurated until all five deputy speakers are elected.

On Sunday, the PDK withdrew its candidate for the post of deputy speaker, while four other deputies were elected.

Vetevendosje leader Kurti was re-elected Prime Minister by MPs at a session boycotted by opposition parties. A narrow majority of 62 MPs out of 120 voted in favour of Kurti’s new cabinet. Eight MPs from the Belgrade-backed Srpska Lista voted against.

However, on Monday evening, the election of a new state President received another setback when the sole candidate for the post, Bekim Sejdiu, announced his withdrawal following disagreements within his Democratic League of Kosovo, LDK, over his candidacy.

Kurti and LDK leader Lumir Abdixhiku had agreed on his name on August 31 – but six LDK MPs then announced they would not support him, leaving the potential vote without the necessary quorum.

Failure to elect a new President within two months of the inauguration of parliament would trigger new elections, the fourth within less than two months.

“Under such circumstances, characterised by the lack of the necessary parliamentary support for my election as President and by the deviation of the entire process into the vortex of internal political dynamics and clashes, I have decided to withdraw from the candidacy for President,” Sejdiu, a former Constitutional Court judge and diplomat, said in a Facebook post.

“I call on the political parties to find a way out of this vicious circle, which, more than anything else, is eroding citizens’ hopes of a prosperous future for them and their families,” he added.

LDK leader Abdixhiku lamented the lack of support for his candidacy. “His withdrawal in the face of political hysteria shows exactly why a person with such a character would be an appropriate pick for President,” Abdixhiku said.

“It’s a pity that we don’t have a President today. Instead of a solution, we have political chaos, a blockade as a means, and new elections, once again, as a goal,” he added.

Vetevendosje also regretted the withdrawal – and accused opposition MPs of trying to provoke new elections.

“When a boycott is used to make a vote impossible, then we don’t have political difference around a candidate but the blockage of a constitutional process and taking the country to repeated elections,” Vetevendosje said.

World.title: Autism Centre: 35 Million Euro Zagreb Project Gets Underway After 20+ Years
World.content:
September the 16th, 2026 – The long awaited Autism Centre is an enormous 35 million euro Zagreb project that is finally getting underway after a long 20+ year wait.

After over 20 years of announcements, the City of Zagreb has finally obtained a building permit for the construction of a new Autism Centre in Oporovec. It will provide modern and adapted conditions for learning, development and professional support for around 200 children, and will bring together programmes that are currently run at multiple locations across Zagreb.

Poslovni reports that the estimated value of the new Autism Centre in Oporovec is around 35 million euros, of which 19.3 million euros will be financed from EU funds through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NPOO), while the remaining amount will be secured from the City of Zagreb budget. Once the building permit becomes final, the preparation of project documentation and the public procurement procedure for selecting the contractor will follow. Construction is planned to start in the summer of 2027, with a planned duration of 18 months.

The new school will have 48 classroom departments and educational groups, as well as three preschool education and care groups. Specialised spaces are also planned for music and art therapy, household skills and aquatic therapy with a pool, sports halls and other facilities adapted to the needs of users.

According to the project by the architectural office SODA-ARHITEKTI, the centre will cover more than 9,600 square metres on three floors, with 60 parking spaces, nine of which are designated for people with disabilities. Attention has also been paid to the outdoor landscaping, with a main square featuring a sensory park, fountains and facilities for developing motor skills planned. “This is another of the projects that have been promised in Zagreb for more than twenty years, and now it is finally going into realisation,” said Zagreb Mayor Tomislav Tomašević.

Deputy Mayor Danijela Dolenec stressed that the new school will represent a major step forward in the quality of spatial and programmatic conditions for the education and upbringing of children and young people with autism. The Autism Centre currently cares for around 300 users through preschool programmes, primary education, full-day and half-day stay programmes, and organised housing, she said.

Dolenec added that the City of Zagreb continues to invest in the existing capacities of the Autism Centre. A public procurement for the renovation and arrangement of the sports hall in Ljevakovićeva Street, worth 250,000 euros, was recently launched, and around 750,000 euros has been invested in the renovation of the Centre’s existing facilities in recent years.

By the end of the year, the opening of a new Centre space in Juraj Dalmatinac Street is also planned, where early developmental and psychosocial support services will be provided for 40 children, as well as a stay programme for 30 adults with autism spectrum disorders. The City of Zagreb has also stated that 24 new special classroom departments and educational groups have been established in the new school year, increasing existing capacities by almost a quarter.

The number of special classroom departments has grown from 64 back in 2021 to 126 in 2026, while the network of schools implementing these programmes has been expanded to 55 schools across Zagreb, according to the City of Zagreb press release.

World.title: Zadar Mobile Boat Pharmacy is in the Final for the Best EU Project Award
World.content:
September the 16th, 2026 – The very commendable Zadar mobile pharmacy on a boat is in the final for the Best EU Project Award.

The Zadar project “Mobile Pharmacy – boat for the islands of Zadar County” has secured a place in the final of this year’s competition for the best EU project in the category Contribution to the Local and Regional Community. Morski reports that this very commendable initiative is primarily aimed at introducing a mobile pharmaceutical service in the island area in order to significantly facilitate residents’ access to medicines and professional advice, especially those in more traffic-isolated places.

The competition is organised by the Croatian Association of Counties, the Office of the European Parliament in Croatia and the portal Župan.hr, under the auspices of the Ministry of Regional Development and EU Funds. In strong competition from almost 50 projects submitted from all over Croatia, the expert jury selected a total of 36 finalists, with the Zadar mobile pharmacy competing among the 18 best in its category.

The winners in the readers’ choice category are decided by the public, and public voting officially ran from the 8th to the 15th of September, 2026.

World.title: Croatia to Get Most Modern Thermal Spa in Historic €42 Million project
World.content:
September the 16th, 2026 – Croatia is set to get its most modern and largest thermal spa as a historic 42 million euro project finally nears completion.

Works on Wellovar in Veliki Korenovo, the largest construction project in the history of Bjelovar worth €42 million, have entered the final stage. Poslovni reports that the enormous complex with a total of ten pools is already taking on its final appearance, and finishing works and system checks are currently underway before opening. Bjelovar Mayor Dario Hrebak regularly visits the construction site and emphasises that the focus is now on the details and on balancing and calibrating one of the most complex and modern heating, cooling and hot water systems in Croatia.

“Works on the largest thermal spa in Croatia, our Wellovar, are nearing completion. Only minor details remain, but this is one of the most complex and modern heating, cooling and hot water systems in Croatia. We now have to ensure that the entire system is balanced and calibrated. It is hard to say when we will open the doors. Our great wish is that it will be on the 29th of September, on the Bjelovar City Day, but it is very difficult to predict,” said Hrebak. He added that at this moment the exact opening date is not crucial; the most important thing is that the project is completed to a high standard.

“What matters is that everything we see is heading towards its final stage and that the people of Bjelovar will get a standard that 95 percent of other cities in Croatia do not have. Croatia will also get an excellent centre for the development of water sports,” he stressed. In addition to tourist and recreational facilities, Wellovar is also expected to play an important role in the development of sport. According to Hrebak, the facility has been designed to meet the standards for hosting national and international swimming and water polo competitions. “We are truly looking forward to it soon opening its doors and delighting our citizens, as well as all tourists and visitors with its facilities,” Hrebak concluded.

With the completion of this massive €42 million project, Bjelovar is set to gain a major new sports, recreational and tourist complex. Although the official opening date has not yet been confirmed, the city administration’s wish is for Wellovar to welcome its first visitors as early as the 19th of September, on Bjelovar’s City Day.

World.title: Croatia to Make Changes to ENC Usage as of March 1st, 2027
World.content:
September the 16th, 2026 – Croatia will make significant changes to ENC usage as of March the 1st, 2027, and drivers with multiple vehicles need to pay particular attention to what is coming.

The much anticipated new Croatian road toll collection system will use ENC technology, but also automatic licence plate recognition via cameras. Poslovni reports that for years now, ENC has been one of the simplest ways to pay motorway tolls across Croatia. You put the device in your car, drive through the marked lane, and the system automatically handles the payment. However, with the introduction of the new electronic toll collection system, one thing becomes much more important than before: the ENC will also be linked to the vehicle’s registration plate.

From the 1st of March 2027, when the new system starts operating, the vehicle’s registration number, data on the ENC device, and a valid means of payment will have to be registered in the system for the ENC model to be used. The law expressly stipulates that a driver using ENC must pass through the toll point in a vehicle whose registration plates are identical to those linked in the system to the ENC device in the vehicle. This means it will no longer be enough simply to take a working ENC device and put it in any car. Before driving, it will be important that the vehicle being used on the motorway is properly registered in the new system.

this is particularly important if you use one enc for multiple cars

The change is especially significant for those who currently use the same ENC in several cars. Under the current rules of Croatian Motorways, an ENC device for vehicle categories IA, I and II is not tied to a single registration number. It can be used in multiple vehicles of the same category, provided the same device is not used simultaneously in more than one vehicle. The new system introduces a different principle: the registration number becomes an integral part of the data linked to the ENC device. Therefore, drivers who currently simply move the ENC from one car to another will have to make sure that the registration of the vehicle they are using is correctly linked to the device in the Electronic Toll Collection System.

The law itself does not currently stipulate that one ENC can necessarily be linked to only one registration number. The detailed rules on use and changes to data will be regulated by the rules of the new system. However, it is clear that the previous practice of simply transferring the device without checking the registration will no longer be sufficient. The good news for existing users is that current ENC devices will not become unusable. The law obliges motorway operators to include ENC devices purchased before the establishment of the new system into the new ESNC no later than its start.

the new cameras will read license plates

The new toll collection system will use ENC technology as well as automatic licence plate recognition via cameras. For passenger cars and other light vehicles, drivers will be able to choose between the ENC model and a model based solely on the registration number and a registered means of payment. When using ENC, the system will therefore have data on both the device and the vehicle’s registration number. Cameras will record the vehicle’s passage and read the licence plates in order to identify the vehicle and verify payment. For drivers, this brings a new habit: before driving, it will no longer be enough simply to check whether the ENC is in the car and whether there are sufficient funds on the account. They will also have to make sure that the vehicle’s registration number is correctly registered in the system. This is precisely what could be particularly important for those who currently use one ENC in multiple cars.

World.title: adidas and HNS Unveil New Croatia National Team Kits
World.content:
adidas has unveiled the long-awaited new official kits for the Croatia national football team, the first set produced under a long-term partnership with the Croatian Football Federation (HNS).

Combining cutting-edge performance innovation with elements founded in Croatian culture and identity, the new kits celebrate the heritage, pride and passion that define Croatian football.

The unveiling marks the start of a new chapter for one of international football’s most recognizable national teams. Having cemented its place among the world’s leading footballing nations, Croatia will step out in an adidas kit for the first time as part of the partnership announced earlier this year.

HNS / adidas

The new home shirt offers a modern take on Croatia’s iconic red-and-white checkerboard pattern, one of the most striking visual symbols in international football. For the first time, letters from the Glagolitic alphabet — the oldest known Slavic script and an important symbol of Croatian cultural heritage — have been woven into the checkerboard design, running throughout the pattern to give one of Croatian football’s most recognizable emblems a fresh, contemporary twist. The back of the collar also features the word “HRVATSKA” written in Glagolitic script, further tying the shirt to Croatia’s cultural history.

The away shirt, meanwhile, draws inspiration from Croatia’s long tradition of lace-making, a craft passed down through generations and another significant part of the country’s cultural heritage. An intricate lace-inspired motif runs across the shirt’s navy base, offering a modern interpretation of that tradition. The design is completed by a collar detail bearing the word “HRVATSKA” in typography inspired by cross-stitch embroidery, linking the traditional craft to contemporary football design.

HNS / adidas

“These shirts are much more than innovative football kits and striking design. Working with adidas, we chose a design that perfectly combines local pride with a global perspective. Those are exactly the values Croatia has always stood for, and now a new generation of fans and players will carry them forward,” said Marijan Kustić, president of the Croatian Football Federation.

Both shirts were developed to meet the demands of football at the highest level and feature the latest adidas CLIMACOOL+ technology. Specially developed stretch fabrics and 3D body-mapping technology improve ventilation and breathability, helping players stay dry through high-intensity matches and in hot conditions. Perforated three-stripe panels and strategically placed mesh zones further boost airflow and comfort.

Croatia’s men’s national team will wear the new kits for the first time during the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures.

Alongside the new shirts, adidas is also launching a wider Croatia national team collection that includes shorts, socks, training wear and leisurewear, designed for fans who want to show their connection to the national team both on and off the pitch.

A video unveiling the new kits has been posted on the Instagram profiles of @adidasfootball and the Croatian Football Federation.

The new Croatia national team kits, along with the full HNS x adidas collection, are available to buy from today at the official HNS online store. Pick out your kit, step into a new era of Croatian football, and wear it with pride.

World.title: CRANE Forum 2026: Productivity as a European Priority, Judiciary as the Greatest Obstacle to Investment
World.content:
September the 15th, 2026 – The CRANE Forum 2026 was recently held, which welcomed around 200 guests from the fields of investment to politics, and from economics to financial institution representatives.

As stated, around 200 guests involved with the Croatian economy, entrepreneurs and investors, members of the Government, ambassadors and representatives of international financial institutions, as well as county prefects and mayors, gathered at the Tihočaj estate in the Žumberak – Samobor Hills Nature Park to discuss investment prospects and the frameworks in which they will be implemented.

In Jastrebarsko on the 12th of September 2026, the fourth CRANE Forum, organised by CRANE, the Croatian Association of Investors and Business Angels, was held. The location was the Tihočaj estate in the Žumberak – Samobor Hills Nature Park. Once again this year, the Forum brought together all levels of decision-making on a single investment in one place: 200 guests from the top of the Croatian economy, entrepreneurs and investors, members of the Government, ambassadors and representatives of international financial institutions, as well as county prefects and mayors.

“Since 2008, CRANE has been connecting entrepreneurs and investors and bringing together capital, knowledge and experience with those who make the decisions. For development and new investments, finding an investor is not enough. What is also needed is a state that cooperates and understands the vision, and a local environment that knows how to create the conditions for its implementation. That is why we do not build the Forum as a conference, but as a working meeting at which everyone who decides on a single investment is present,” said Davorin Štetner, President of CRANE.

The key topics of this year’s Forum were the new multiannual financial framework of the European Union after 2027, the tax system as a competitive advantage, the role of local self-government in attracting strategic investments, and investments in healthcare.

Speaking about what Croatia can expect from the EU’s multiannual financial framework after 2027, Nataša Mikuš Žigman, Minister of Regional Development and EU Funds, stressed that the priorities coming from Brussels are focused on security, defence and climate efficiency, but equally on investments in productivity and competitiveness. Croatia, she announced, has already begun preparing a future competitiveness investment programme that will combine public and private funds, with the aim of raising the productivity of the economy. Among the novelties are milder requirements for technical documentation at the application and contracting stage, the possibility for applicants with smaller tax debts not to be excluded from the procedure but to settle them before the decision on the award of support is made, and raising the threshold for the implementation of procurement procedures with simple procurement via the eKohezija platform. In the negotiations on the new multiannual financial framework, Croatia insists that administrative burden relief actually reaches end-users and does not remain only on the Brussels–Member State axis.

On the panel dedicated to the tax system, in which Tomislav Ćorić, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, Davor Baković, President of the Croatian Exporters Association and Chairman of the Management Board of Končar MT d.d., Davor Tremac, Executive Director of Fono, and Domagoj Kamenski, Executive Director of Kamgrad, participated, it was emphasised that the Croatian tax framework in itself is not an obstacle to growth, but in certain segments even represents a competitive advantage, with a corporate income tax rate lower than the average of developed countries and excellent incentives for investment and research and development.

That the tax rate is not decisive is also shown by comparison with the surrounding region: ahead of Croatia on investment attractiveness rankings are the Czech Republic and Slovenia, which have significantly higher corporate income tax rates. The key problem, as Tremac stressed, is distrust in the judiciary, because what is contracted on paper is difficult and slow to enforce before Croatian courts, and this has been pointed out for thirty years without progress. The price of this distrust is measured in capital that does not arrive: when the enforceability of contractual protections is not certain, investors do not abandon the investment, but the jurisdiction, so Croatian companies register their holding companies in Ireland, the Netherlands or Luxembourg, and the tax base moves with them. The conclusion of the panel is therefore that lowering tax rates would not solve a problem that the rates did not create; the greatest contribution to the investment climate would come from judicial reform, i.e. the speed and predictability of resolving commercial disputes.

Speaking about investments in healthcare from the Government’s perspective, Minister of Health Irena Hrstić emphasised that the Government of the Republic of Croatia has invested around €3.4 billion in the healthcare system over the past ten years or so, and that investments continue in line with the policy of balanced regional development – from the new University Hospital Centre Osijek and the project for a new University Hospital Centre for Dalmatia, which the Ministry and the Government have already given the green light, to the hospital in Blato, whose foundation stone will soon be laid and which will be the first “Carbon Zero” hospital in Europe, heated by geothermal energy and financed by European funds. The leading principle is smart investment, with the emphasis that the goal is functional healthcare equally accessible to all parts of Croatia.

A strong diplomatic dimension was given to the Forum by the presentation of new interlocutors of the Croatian business community at the international level: Ronke Amoni Ogunsulire, World Bank Director for Croatia and Slovenia, Her Excellency Anne Toft Sørensen, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Denmark to the Republic of Croatia, and His Excellency Glenn Morrison, Ambassador of Australia to the Republic of Croatia. Their presentation opens new channels of cooperation and a direct link between the domestic business and investment community and partners outside Croatia, which is crucial for attracting investment and strengthening export opportunities. In addition to them, the Forum also gathered other esteemed ambassadors and representatives of international financial institutions, thereby confirming its role as a meeting place of the Croatian economy with international partners.

what is crane?

CRANE – the Croatian Association of Investors and Business Angels is otherwise the oldest Croatian association of investors and business angels, founded in 2008. It connects ambitious entrepreneurs with investors who invest money, knowledge, skills and business contacts in their projects, with the aim that as many innovative companies in the early stage of development as possible grow into successful business stories. CRANE is the national representative of Croatia in the European Business Angels Network (EBAN) and a member of the Global Business Angels Network (GBAN), and in addition to its investment activity systematically advocates a better regulatory and tax framework for entrepreneurs and investors in Croatia and at the level of the European Union. More at www.crane.hr.

World.title: Hybrid Electro-Diesel Train Between Split and Zagreb Now Operational
World.content:
September the 15th, 2026 – The very first hybrid electro-diesel train between Split and Zagreb is now fully operational. Here are all the details.

As of today (September the 15th, 2026) the very first electro-diesel train will enter service on the Split – Zagreb Main Station route. The train departs (as it has today) from Split station at 07:54. Poslovni reports that the new train is adapted to the specific characteristics of the Zagreb–Split line, which is partly electrified and partly non-electrified. It has 150 seats, and passengers have access to free Wi-Fi, power sockets next to the seats, a modern information system, visual and audio announcements, ramps for people with disabilities, and space for bicycles. The train also features self-service machines for buying coffee and other hot drinks, water, soft drinks, sweets and snacks.

The introduction of the new electro-diesel trains for long-distance transport continues the modernisation of the HŽ Passenger Transport fleet, while at the same time reducing energy consumption, noise and greenhouse gas emissions. Experts from the KONČAR Group, in cooperation with numerous Croatian companies, were involved in the development and production of the trains.

As part of this massive project, six electro-diesel trains are being procured, financed by a loan from the European Investment Bank amounting to 57.3 million euros. All six trains will be put into service by the end of this year. As of December 2026, with the start of the new timetable, Zagreb and Split will be connected by four daily trains, further improving the connectivity of Croatia’s two largest cities and the quality of travel.

Ahead of the first regular journey of the new train, statements for the media will be given by State Secretary for Railways Žarko Tušek from the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure, President of the Management Board of HŽ Passenger Transport Željko Ukić, President of the Management Board of KONČAR Gordan Kolak, Split-Dalmatia County Prefect Blaženko Boban, and Deputy Mayor of Split Matea Dorčić. Also present on the journey will be Zadar County Prefect Josip Bilaver and Šibenik-Knin County Prefect Paško Rakić.

World.title: Brač Fire: Residents Without Electricity Told to Follow TV and Radio
World.content:
September the 15th, 2026 – Brač residents worried for their properties and indeed their lives in the recent Milna fire were very clumsily advised to follow the TV and radio – despite having no electricity.

The Early Warning and Crisis Management System (SRUUK) was activated on Saturday evening because of a large fire in the wider Milna area on Brač. Lukrecija Zderic reports for Index that residents in that area received a message on their mobile phones with a link to instructions on how to act, along with advice to follow further announcements on television and radio. At the same time, part of Brač had no electricity, which raised the question of how exactly people without power were supposed to obtain new information about the fire.

On Saturday evening, the fire, driven by strong wind, spread rapidly towards Milna as well as the bays of Duboka and Osibova, where Resort Gava with a large number of tourists is located. More than 200 firefighters were on the ground trying to stop the fire from spreading towards the populated area.

false evacuation and sruuk activation

The red sky above Brač and Milna was visible even from Split, while Index readers filmed the firestorm approaching the settlement. As the situation became increasingly serious, various pieces of information about a possible evacuation began to arrive. Shortly before 23:00, a notice about the evacuation of the population was published on the Facebook page of the Milna Volunteer Fire Department. It stated that the situation was critical and called on citizens to make their private boats available for evacuation needs. The post was deleted about half an hour later, and services on the ground reported that there was no official evacuation.

At 23:28 the SRUUK was activated. Citizens in the endangered area received a warning via SMS or Cell Broadcast about the danger, together with a link to additional information. Clicking the link opens a page of the Ministry of the Interior (MUP), i.e. the Civil Protection Directorate, containing “Instructions for Citizens.” These are general instructions on how to behave during a fire, and below them citizens are directed to follow further announcements via television, radio and links of the Civil Protection Directorate. At that moment Milna was already without electricity. The earlier post about evacuation further confused residents. Some did not know whether they should leave the place, so they prepared for evacuation and went out onto the street by the sea.

The SRUUK activated once again that evening at 00:22, when citizens once more received a link with instructions on how to act in the event of a fire. Why residents in the endangered area without electricity were recommended to follow information via TV and radio remains unknown for now. Because of the approaching fire a partial evacuation of the most endangered parts of Milna and the surrounding area was carried out, while the entire settlement was never evacuated at any point.

a fire warning for a fire on an island was received in split… on the mainland

The Civil Protection Directorate was therefore asked for an explanation as to exactly why citizens in an area affected by a power outage were directed to television and radio, who in such a situation is responsible for delivering key information, and how many times the SRUUK was activated during the fire on Brač. We will publish the answer when we receive it. However, the problem was not only in the content of the messages. Residents we spoke to said that some received the warning around 23:00 and then again after midnight, while others received only the first message. According to their accounts, some residents of Supetar received no warning at all.

At the same time, a warning about a significant fire danger was also received by some citizens who were at that moment in Split and on the island of Hvar, even though they were not on the territory of Brač. We have also requested an answer from the Civil Protection Directorate on this issue.

a heavily criticised system

The SRUUK has previously been criticised for not being activated during crisis situations. The last time this happened was during the large fire near Omiš, in which three people died and five more are still fighting for their lives. The fire left enormous consequences — people were left without homes and jobs, thousands of hectares of forest burned, and the safety of the population remains threatened due to possible landslides.

The non-activation of the system at that time was justified by Split-Dalmatia County Prefect Blaženko Boban with the assessment that sending a warning could cause panic. On Brač the opposite question has arisen: did the unclear communication from the services further contribute to confusion and panic among residents? In the fire that has been burning on Brač for several days, around 4,000 hectares of forest, low vegetation and maquis have totally burned, as have private buildings, cars and one resort. Around 700 people were evacuated and two people were injured. There is still some smouldering on the ground, the fire has not been completely extinguished, and firefighters remain on alert.

Over 200 firefighters on the ground have for days been making superhuman efforts to defend houses and protect residents. For the locals they are heroes who risk their own lives to protect people and property. Yet the question remains how much help they receive in crisis situations from a system that the state paid 8.4 million euros for. The SRUUK was conceived as a tool for timely warning of citizens. On Brač, however, it has been shown that simply sending a message is not the end of its job, the key question is whether citizens can, after that message, actually receive clear, timely and useful information when they need it most.

World.title: Crimes against the Estonian state plea deal: Defendant faces 7 years in prison
World.content:
A plea agreement was struck on day one of the trial of a pro-Kremlin propagandist charged with activities harmful to Estonia's national security.

Oleg Bessedin's hearing began on Tuesday at the first-tier Harju County Court. He has been in custody since his arrest last November, and faces seven years in prison under the terms of the plea agreement.

Lead State Prosecutor Taavi Pern told ERR's Russian-language portal that, following negotiations with the defendant and his lawyer, the Prosecutor's Office agreed to resolve the criminal case via a plea agreement provided Bessedin serves seven years of actual prison time and the court confiscates more than €73,000 in assets obtained via the crimes.

Those crimes are primarily acting against Estonia's national security. "According to the evidence, Oleg Bessedin, in cooperation with Russian state institutions and their representatives, has consistently participated in influence activities directed against Estonia. The aim has been to spread propaganda and disinformation in order to divide Estonia's population and sway people into supporting Russia's political choices," Pern said.

According to the indictment, Bessedin also disseminated narratives which Russia has used to justify attacks on neighboring states, amplifying them in such a way as to give those involved in Russia's political decision-making the impression that these represented the overall views of Estonia's Russian-speaking population; he also benefited materially from these activities.

"According to the evidence, Oleg Bessedin has directly harmed Estonia's security, and earned criminal proceeds in doing so," Pern said. "Therefore, Oleg Bessedin's crimes against the state must be followed by a severe and effective punishment. The prosecutor's condition for resolving the criminal case through a plea agreement was a lengthy actual prison sentence and the confiscation of proceeds obtained through the crimes."

Bessedin's lawyer, Dmitri Školjar, said that after two preliminary hearings, Tuesday's hearing began via ordinary proceedings, and an agreement was reached during the day. "We met, discussed it all day and resolved the disputed issues. Ultimately we signed a plea agreement and submitted it to the court today, asking for the proceedings to continue under a plea agreement," Školjar said.

He added that the court only received the materials on Tuesday, and still needs to review them, meaning it will make a decision on the agreement on Monday, September 28.

Sentences to run concurrently to 7 years' real prison time

Under the agreement, Bessedin will be sentenced to seven years in prison, comprising two years and nine months for violating sanctions and six and a half years for activities against the state. The agreement provides for the sentences to run concurrently, with the more severe sentence partially absorbing the lesser one, resulting in a total sentence of seven years.

The sentence will also take into account the time Bessedin has spent in custody since last November. He will be eligible to apply for release on parole after two and a half years.

The court also granted the defense lawyer's request to lift additional restrictions on his client. Bessedin has been held in solitary confinement, and according to his lawyer, his isolation from other detainees should now end, which will also allow him to communicate with his family.

The charge sheet states that from May 2022 at the latest, Bessedin actively participated in influence activities conducted for the benefit and in the interests of Russia and, in the course of these activities, was in contact with various Russian institutions, officials and individuals involved in Russian influence operations.

According to these charges, by taking part in these influence activities, he committed non-violent acts directed against Estonia's independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity.

Additionally, prosecutors have charged him with distributing sanctioned Russian television shows and content in Estonia via television and social media channels under his control, as well as making sanctioned content available to other channels. The purpose of the international sanctions imposed on Russia is to prevent the spread of Russian propaganda and disinformation and to curb Russia's capacity for aggression.

World.title: Defense agency rejects Datasel talks as EU funding period ends
World.content:
The State Defense Investment Centre (RKIK) has rejected a proposal by arms firm Datasel to resolve an ongoing dispute through a joint working group, noting the financing period for the contracts has expired.

Datasel, an Italian company acquired in 2024 by Indian-owned Neco Defense Munitions, signed four contracts with RKIK to supply artillery ammunition for Ukraine using EU European Peace Facility (EPF) funding. However, disputes over delayed, substandard deliveries led the RKIK to terminate and pursue legal action.

Revelations Estonia had paid up to €70 million in advance for artillery shells for Ukraine that were never delivered led to the resignation of Hanno Pevkur as defense minister.

Datasel this week sent a letter to the government, members of the Riigikogu and the RKIK proposing a joint working group to resolve disagreements and confirming its readiness to complete deliveries. The company said it has the resources and supply chain to fulfill its contractual obligations.

"It is not too late to resolve the disagreements," lawyer Veiko Viisileht, acting for Datasel, told "Aktuaalne kaamera". "Datasel is ready to sit down with the RKIK at the same table and resolve all disagreements."

RKIK gave a blunt response, however, with its lawyer Maria Pihlak noting the contracts had been financed through the European Peace Facility, but the period for using that funding has now ended.

"Simply put, this means that the RKIK does not have the budgetary resources today to accept the remaining ammunition that has allegedly been produced or is being produced in the future," Pihlak said. "Negotiations like these will not lead anywhere, anymore. We have an ongoing lawsuit, we have an ongoing arbitration dispute, and we will continue to defend our rights in these proceedings."

Datasel's homepage. Source: Screenshot.

The two sides also disagree over the termination of the contracts. "These contracts were terminated because they repeatedly violated deadlines," Pihlak noted. Viisileht countered that whether the contracts were validly terminated "is a contentious issue both in court and in arbitration."

SDE MP Raimond Kaljulaid, a member of the Riigikogu National Defence Committee, said Datasel's latest appeal had not served to boost the company's credibility either, pointing to the European Public Prosecutor's Office (EPPO) investigation into the use of EPF funds by Estonia.

"What has changed is that news has come that this company is also being investigated very seriously at the European level," Kaljulaid said. "My first reaction was that maybe this has given them some idea that whatever it takes, let's try to fulfill our contractual obligations now so that we can somehow get this issue off the ground."

Datasel is being represented on the Estonian side by law firm LINKLaw and the PR company Powerhouse.

In 2024, the RKIK signed four contracts with Datasel, an Italian firm acquired by Indian-owned Neco Defense Munitions, paying roughly €70 million up front. Deliveries were however reported as being delayed or substandard, leading RKIK to terminate and pursue legal action. Datasel denies any wrongdoing.

The National Audit Office (Riigikontroll) had flagged the same inventory problems a year earlier, and the Ministry of Defense promised to fix them, but it did not. The same audit also found €59.8 million in prepayments to Datasel for munitions for Ukraine, none of which actually arrived in Ukraine. The EPPO is investigating that.

Hanno Pevkur (Reform) resigned as defense minister on September 2, taking political but not personal responsibility for the saga. His replacement has been named as Martin Herem, former Estonian Defense Forces commander and a retired general.

World.title: Estonian dance scholarship winner: Folk dancing is a bug you can't shake
World.content:
Folk dance teacher and choreographer Helena-Maria Reimann, this year's recipient of the prestigious Ullo Toomi Scholarship, says Estonian folk dance is thriving.

Reimann was awarded the 39th Ullo Toomi Scholarship, named after Estonian folk dance teacher and choreographer Ullo Toomi, at Tallinn Town Hall on Monday.

The scholarship, awarded since 1987 and considered the field's highest honor, recognizes outstanding contributions to Estonian folk dancing. Reimann said the honor means a great deal to her.

"Ullo Toomi was someone who didn't just leave us dances; he gave us a concept and tradition that we must preserve and pass on to future generations," she said.

Reimann has worked with young dancers in Tallinn's Sõleke folk dance troupe for more than three decades. Among other contributions, she has also been involved as a choreographer or assistant principal choreographer in every Estonian Youth Dance Festival and Dance Festival since 2011, serving as principal choreographer for the XXI Dance Festival in 2025.

Helena-Mariana Reimann at the XXI Dance Festival "Kinship" ("Iseoma") in Tallinn July 2025. Source: Rein Leib

The scholarship recipient said Estonian folk dancing is thriving, and infectious to boot.

"I like saying it's like a bug — once you've been infected, there's no shaking it anymore," Reimann said. She pointed to dancers in her own troupe who initially came together for a single dance festival but have now been dancing together for a decade.

'I love our Estonian dance'

Reimann said there is always something new on the horizon. Her troupe is currently working on a demo video for the next Dance Festival in 2028, for which registration just began.

She also simply enjoys both the dancing itself and creating new choreography.

"I really love being involved in folk dancing," she said. "I love dance, I love our Estonian dance, and I love creating new dances to wonderful Estonian music that sometimes just begs to be choreographed."

Previous Ullo Toomi Scholarship recipients include prominent folk dance figures such as Maie Orav, Mait Agu, Ilma Adamson, Helju Mikkel and Ülo Luht.

World.title: Norstat poll: Center catching up to Isamaa, Reform bouncing back
World.content:
The gap between Isamaa and the Center Party has narrowed to a minimum. Meanwhile, support for the Reform Party and Parempoolsed is trending upward, according to the latest Norstat poll.

Support for Isamaa stood at 23.3 percent in the latest poll, its lowest level since November 2023. By comparison, Isamaa's support was 25.3 percent two weeks earlier, 26.4 percent in the second week of August and 27.3 percent in early June.

The Center Party has risen to virtually the same level as Isamaa, with 22.2 percent of respondents backing the party in the latest poll. Support for the Center Party has remained very stable throughout the year, mostly hovering around 20–22 percent. The narrowing gap between the two parties is therefore primarily the result of declining support for Isamaa.

These figures reflect the combined results of the past four weeks, covering 4,000 respondents. Looking specifically at the results from the most recent week, based on 1,000 respondents, support for the Center Party was actually higher than for Isamaa. The Center Party had 23.3 percent support, compared with 21.6 percent for Isamaa. In the weekly poll, the Reform Party also overtook the Social Democratic Party (SDE), with support at 14.7 percent and 14.0 percent, respectively.

According to the poll's four-week combined results, however, SDE remains in third place with 15.8 percent support. A week earlier, SDE's support stood at 15.9 percent. By comparison, the party's rating was 13.5 percent in July.

Despite scandals in the defense sector that led to the departure of the Reform Party defense minister, support for the prime minister's party has risen. The Reform Party had 13.8 percent support in the latest poll. The last time its support was at this level was in February this year.

Support for the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) stood at 12.1 percent in the latest poll, while Parempoolsed had 7.5 percent. Parempoolsed's support is at its highest level in the party's history in Norstat polling.

Eesti 200, which is also part of the governing coalition, remained at 1.6 percent for the fourth consecutive week, leaving it well below the electoral threshold.

The coalition parties had the combined support of 15.4 percent of respondents, while parties in the Riigikogu opposition had 73.4 percent.

Based on the current polling figures, Isamaa would receive 26 seats in the Riigikogu, the Center Party 25, SDE 17, the Reform Party 14, EKRE 12 and Parempoolsed seven.

The latest combined results cover the polling period from August 17 to September 13. A total of 4,000 Estonian citizens of voting age were surveyed.

World.title: 'Mystery' of Tartu's floating silver balls solved
World.content:
Silvery balls spotted hovering in the skies above Tartu are blimp drones being used as part of a demonstration event, Maaleht reported .

The drone demonstration flights are part of a defense industry event, Electromagnetic Warfare Live, or EWLive, Maaleht wrote, in response to a reader's letter.

The event is a high-level international defense industry event focusing as its name suggests on electronic warfare and cyber and electromagnetic activities. It started earlier in the month and runs to Thursday.

Various demonstrations form an integral part of EWLive and will include flights of smaller unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in the vicinity of the airfield and the Estonian Aviation Academy's (Eesti Lennuakadeemia) teaching building this week.

EWLive 2026 is being held on the grounds of Tartu Ülemurme Airport for the seventh time and is organized by Tangent Link, the Ministry of Defense and the Estonian Defense Forces (EDF). It is a closed event requiring registration.

A helium-filled blimp (photo is illustrative). Source: Srđan Popović / Wikimedia Commons

Organizers say there is no cause for concern among local residents; the drones' use is being coordinated by the aviation academy.

As they are usually helium-inflated, blimp UAVs, also known as LTA (lighter than air) UAVs, can hover in place for extended periods of time and also fly much more quietly than their heavier-than-air counterparts. It also makes them "plummet proof" – if power fails, they fall more gently and so are safer where crowds of people might be expected.

Their hovering capacity saves on battery power, and means their applications can include "eye in the sky" surveillance and security, geospatial mapping and gas leak location. They can also serve as floating WiFi or radio hotspots in times of emergency. They have been used in Ukraine to augment the capacities of attack drones.

World.title: Education minister promises smoother high school admissions next year
World.content:
Minister of Education and Research Kristina Kallas (Eesti 200) says high school admissions should run more smoothly next spring under a unified schedule and revamped system.

The changes follow a chaotic admissions season this year, when nearly 1,900 basic school graduates still weren't enrolled in either high school or a vocational school a week before the new school year began.

While each school will continue to set its own admission requirements, for the coming admissions cycle, high schools and vocational schools across the country will follow a common schedule. Students will apply through SAIS, Estonia's unified admissions information system, ranking their school choices by preference.

SAIS was also supposed to handle admissions this year, but the plan was scrapped in February after problems with the latest version, SAIS3. Kallas said the system has since undergone load testing, and schools can now practice entering their admission requirements ahead of time in a test environment.

"We're currently working on developing the preference system's functionality," she said, adding that the full system will open for schools in January.

Next spring, students can apply to schools from March 29 through May 18. Estonia's system will allow students to apply to any number of schools, though the minister acknowledged that unlimited choices can make the process confusing for kids.

The possibility of setting a limit, she said, warrants broader public discussion. Ranking preferences, however, will also help schools identify applicants who have placed them first.

"They can, for example, start interviews with those who listed the school as their top choice and don't have to interview everyone," Kallas said.

Chance to change application

Another change will allow students to review and adjust their preferences after receiving their basic school exam results. Exam results will be entered into the Estonian Education Information System (EHIS) on May 17, and students will have one day to revise their applications before schools begin making offers.

"We wanted to give them three days, but school principals weren't on board with that, so we're giving them one," the minister said.

Estonian students ready to take an exam. Photo is illustrative. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Schools must begin making their admissions offers by June 11, with the main admissions round running through July 2. Kallas urged students to accept offers promptly so that enrollment does not remain tied up while other applicants wait.

"The problem this year was that very strong students received admissions offers from several schools and took a long time to accept one," she explained. While others received rejections right away, many students in between waited in limbo and uncertainty over the summer.

The minister said schools should keep rolling admissions going in July to avoid a repeat.

Admissions to end earlier

Following an interim review by July 5 to identify remaining vacancies, rolling admissions must begin no later than July 15 and will end August 23, a week earlier than this year. All students not yet accepted to a high school or vocational school will then be able to reapply for remaining spots on equal terms.

"That's a week earlier, so kids won't have to wait as long for schools to make their decisions," Kallas said.

She acknowledged the earlier cutoff may mean shorter summer vacations for teachers, but urged schools to rotate staff vacations so admissions can be completed on time. Teachers' total number of vacation days, she added, will not change.

The education minister said the longer-term goal is to automate as much of the admissions process as possible, reducing the workload on teachers. She pointed to Finland, where students can rank up to seven schools and an algorithm handles much of the matching, issuing offers automatically.

"Everything is settled within a month and teachers don't have an endless stream of lists and interviews to handle," Kallas said.

The new SAIS3 system is also intended to make rolling admissions easier for students by showing enrollment availability all in one spot.

This means that instead of having to call around to various schools individually to find out if they are still accepting more students, applicants will be able to see a consolidated list of schools that still have spots available for new students.
