World.title: Education minister: Most students still without a school place have almost no Estonian
World.content:
Over 60 percent of young people left without a school place hail from Russian-language basic schools and could not enter vocational school due to virtually nonexistent Estonian skills, Education Minister Kristina Kallas said.

A day before the start of the school year, around 1,300 young people subject to compulsory education still had no school place. As of September 11, 485 basic school graduates remained without one.

Kristina Kallas said the problem, which was most acute in Tallinn, primarily affected graduates of Russian-language basic schools who accounted for more than 60 percent of those without a place.

"They couldn't even get into vocational education simply because their Estonian language skills are virtually nonexistent, despite having studied Estonian for nine years," Kallas said.

She added that such students cannot be admitted to vocational schools even if allowances are made, as vocational education includes technical subjects and students cannot participate in classes if they cannot even understand safety instructions.

Kallas said Tallinn's city government had strongly criticized the Ministry of Education over students being left without school places. While the state certainly also bears responsibility, she said Center Party-led Tallinn had defended Russian-language schools for years and insisted they should not be dismantled.

"The fact that these children don't go on to study anywhere has always been the case; until now, they have simply been out of sight. It's painful to see what actually happens to those coming out of Russian-language schools. It's hypocritical of the Center Party to suddenly be so concerned when, for all these years, it has firmly defended Russian-language schools and Russian-language instruction in them," she said.

According to the education minister, these children studied Estonian for 45 minutes every day for nine years, while nothing else at school took place in Estonian. It is also possible that explanations during Estonian lessons were given in Russian. Their exposure to Estonian was therefore virtually nonexistent.

Schools transitioning to Estonian-language education are required to administer proficiency tests in fourth grade. The average score was above 50 percent both among students who began Estonian-language instruction in 2024 and those who began last year. Kallas noted, however, that this cannot be considered a good result when only half meet A1, the most basic level of language proficiency, meaning the other half cannot even reach that level.

"This shows that children who had studied in Russian for three years and studied Estonian for three years were unable to pass an A1-level proficiency test in fourth grade. This is a real problem we face," the education minister said.

Ministry considering language exception for mathematics exam

A separate question for the ministry is what language children who switched to Estonian-language education two years ago and are now in sixth grade will use to take their basic school final mathematics exam in three years. Kallas said the options are either to allow students to choose the language of the exam or to offer it in simplified Estonian, since the aim is to assess mathematics rather than language skills.

"This is a major question for us. We're trying to discuss it with university experts and proficiency tests will begin to show us what level of Estonian the students have," Kallas said. She cited Latvia's PISA results as a cautionary example, saying they fell below the OECD average.

The reason, she said, was the Latvian government's decision to require all children to take the PISA test in Latvian, even though Russian-speaking children had been studying in Latvian for only two years.

A language proficiency assessment will also be added to the school readiness report issued at the end of kindergarten, allowing schools to see children's language proficiency when they leave kindergarten. The assessment, designed for kindergartens and first grade, is currently being piloted.

"If necessary, it will be refined, so it should be in wider use by next fall and spring," Kallas said.

Estonian-language schools to qualify for language training support

Helna Karu, head of the Ministry of Education's department overseeing the transition to Estonian-language education, said the way language-learning support is distributed has also changed. While funding was previously provided to schools where most students were native Russian speakers, many such children are now moving to Estonian-language schools, which therefore also need support.

"Local governments apply for the funding for their educational institutions and schools use it according to their most pressing needs, whether to provide additional language instruction, differentiate subject teaching in class, tailor language instruction to students' proficiency levels or organize informal activities that help develop children's language skills," Karu said.

Kallas said schools and kindergartens have also undergone major staffing changes. Just 144 teachers now fail to meet language proficiency requirements, compared with 1,802 two years ago. Nearly 10 percent of Estonia's teaching workforce has changed during the transition period.

"Teachers who have learned the language have taken up positions or teachers have been replaced," Kallas said.

Karu said the Ministry of Education is in close contact with schools and conducts many classroom observations, giving it a good overview of the situation. The most important factor is using effective teaching methods in the classroom, but that expertise develops over time.

World.title: Anbar Health Directorate clarifies pork-breeding rumors amid recent Najaf case
World.content:
Anbar (IraqiNews.com) – The Anbar Health Directorate issued an official denial on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, firmly debunking viral social media claims alleging that its oversight teams had raided an illicit pig-breeding facility and confiscated pork intended for commercial distribution within the governorate.

In a formal statement received by Shafaq News Agency, health authorities stressed that the rumors circulating online are entirely groundless, fabricated, and completely disconnected from any inspection operations or actions executed by the directorate.

Health officials warned that amplifying such sensationalized misinformation fuels public panic and directly undermines institutional trust in state healthcare and food-safety regulators.

The directorate urged citizens, digital outlets, and news organizations to exercise journalistic due diligence by sourcing public health updates exclusively through accredited, official institutional channels while refraining from amplifying unverified social media posts.

The rumor mill in Anbar appears to have mirrored a verified, high-profile incident in Najaf governorate, where intelligence squads arrested a local butcher on Wednesday, September 9, for hunting wild boars in the marshlands of Al-Hurriya subdistrict, Kufa district, and processing the meat into minced beef products for unsuspecting consumers in central Najaf.

Judicial authorities in Najaf confirmed on Saturday that the butcher’s criminal dossier was formally referred to the Najaf Criminal Court after investigators compiled comprehensive forensic evidence, with the defendant now awaiting trial and sentencing under the provisions of the Iraqi Penal Code.

World.title: ‘You are Iraqi in any language’: PM Al Zaidi affirms pluralism in Berlin
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A candid exchange between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi and an Iraqi Kurdish journalist captured widespread attention during the Iraqi-German Business Dialogue Forum in Berlin on Tuesday, September 15, 2026.

When the journalist stood up to address the forum and apologized for not speaking Arabic professionally, Al-Zaidi interjected with a smile: “In whatever language you speak, you are Iraqi.”The gesture drew spontaneous applause across the hall, reframing a routine press exchange into a high-profile affirmation of civic identity.

The encounter resonated deeply against Iraq’s complex social tapestry, highlighting that national identity transcends linguistic or sectarian boundaries.

Iraq remains an ancient crossroads of diverse ethnicities, religions, and native languages, where Arabs, Kurds, Turkmen, Syriac-Assyrians, Yazidis, Armenians, and Shabaks form the core fabric of the nation.

The Prime Minister’s spontaneous remark served as a reminder that every citizen—whether communicating in Arabic, Kurdish, Syriac, Turkmen, or an international tongue—holds an equal, indivisible place within the Iraqi state.

World.title: Iraq signs Energy Cooperation Agreement’s fourth phase with Siemens
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz oversaw on Tuesday the signing ceremony for the fourth phase of the Energy Cooperation Agreement between the Iraqi Ministry of Electricity and Siemens.

The agreement that marks the progression into phase four of the ongoing long-term energy strategic partnership was signed as part of al-Zaidi’s trip to Europe.

The ongoing partnership aims to modernize Iraq’s power sector, build highly efficient generation capacities, and expand transmission and distribution networks throughout the country.

In August 2025, the Iraqi cabinet adopted the fundamentals of an energy cooperation strategy with Germany-based Siemens Energy.

Siemens has previously been engaged in electricity projects in Iraq, including long-term service contracts for three power plants in 2023 as part of larger energy cooperation efforts. Siemens also signed an agreement to improve Iraq’s electricity infrastructure in the same year.

Iraq relies heavily on natural gas supplies from Iran to generate electrical power and frequently experiences electricity outages. These outages worsen during the summer months when temperatures exceed 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) in different parts of the country.

To address the country’s increasing energy demand, the Iraqi government is collaborating with Siemens to develop new power plants with a total capacity of 14,000 megawatts.

The new power plants are expected to use local fuel and combined cycle technology, increasing production efficiency and lessening reliance on imported fuel.

Iraq’s electricity grid is experiencing a daily shortage of over 35,000 megawatts due to restricted fuel availability for power plants and a reduction in some external supply sources. In early August, output was barely 24,600 megawatts.

Demand in the summer fluctuates between 55,000 and 60,000 megawatts, exacerbating the supply imbalance and causing continued operational issues for the system. Production levels rely on gas supplies from Iran, which stand at around 20 million cubic meters per day.

World.title: Iraq may import LNG from French company
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is exploring new avenues to secure fuel for its power plants, with the Ministry of Electricity seeking to diversify its gas sources.

The endeavor includes a preliminary agreement with a French company to discuss the supply of liquefied natural gas (LNG) and its regasification within the country in the coming phase.

The Electricity Ministry said on Monday that Electricity Minister Ali Saadi Wahib signed a preliminary agreement in Paris with TotalEnergies to supply LNG to power plants in Iraq.

The step comes as Iraq seeks to reduce its reliance on limited gas sources and secure a more stable fuel supply for its power plants, thereby increasing electricity supply hours and providing the Ministry of Electricity with additional options during upcoming negotiations with suppliers.

The agreement establishes a framework for discussions and negotiations regarding the potential delivery of LNG via a floating platform that would dock at Iraqi ports in Basra. The LNG would then be regasified and injected into the Iraqi national grid.

The agreement includes exploring the deployment of a floating platform to receive LNG shipments in Iraq and conduct regasification operations before transporting the fuel via the national gas pipeline network to power plants, according to the operational needs of the Iraqi grid.

The proposed approach seeks to enhance the flexibility of the fuel system, as LNG can serve as an additional source when necessary. This strategy also enables Iraqi authorities to evaluate the quantities, timing, and both commercial and technical terms prior to finalizing a binding agreement.

Under the initial memorandum of understanding, Iraq is continuing negotiations with the French company to finalize details regarding supplies, infrastructure, and regasification mechanisms.

This new endeavor aligns with another initiative focused on supplying LNG to the Khor Al-Zubair port in Basra. Baghdad has entered into an agreement with US-based Excelerate Energy to establish a regasification terminal that will operate independently.

World.title: ITEX IRAQ 2026 signs strategic media partnership with Al Shabab TV
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – ITEX IRAQ 2026 has concluded a strategic media partnership with Al-Shabab TV, establishing an integrated broadcasting and digital coverage framework ahead of the country’s flagship information and communications technology summit.

The bilateral agreement aims to amplify the exhibition’s media reach and deliver comprehensive programming across both local and regional audiences, showcasing Iraq’s accelerating pivot toward modern digital infrastructure and public-sector technological transformation.

Scheduled to convene from September 30 to October 3, 2026, at the Baghdad International Fairgrounds, ITEX IRAQ serves as the nation’s premier convergence point for telecommunications, enterprise IT, FinTech, cybersecurity, and digital governance.

Under the newly inked arrangement, the partnership pairs the multimedia broadcast network of Al-Shabab TV with the executive convening power of ITEX IRAQ 2026, creating an expanded promotional runway for participating multinational tech vendors, domestic startups, technical forums, and public-private initiatives shaping the country’s digital economy.

The expanded media coverage framework will track core milestone events across the four-day expo, including specialized panel sessions on emerging technologies, enterprise cloud modernization, artificial intelligence integration, and high-level regulatory forums.

By broadening multi-platform coverage, both entities seek to spotlight actionable investment opportunities and homegrown technological innovations, connecting institutional decision-makers with a wider demographic of young professionals, tech entrepreneurs, and regional commercial stakeholders.

World.title: Economist warns of demographic time bomb over Iraq youth unemployment
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Prominent Iraqi economic expert Manar Al-Obeidi has warned of an impending demographic crisis facing the nation’s leadership, cautioning that a looming human time bomb could soon see millions of unemployed youth taking to the streets in widespread protests demanding jobs.

In a televised interview with journalist Muna Sami, Al-Obeidi grounded his warning in demographic findings from the Ministry of Planning’s recent nationwide census, which registered Iraq’s population at 47 million people and revealed that nearly half of the country is under the age of 25, while active participants in the workforce account for just 30 percent.

Al-Obeidi emphasized that over the next five to ten years, this massive youth cohort will reach prime working age, creating an unprecedented wave of job seekers that the public sector cannot absorb.

With state payrolls already saturated, federal institutions will have zero fiscal or administrative capacity to offer additional civil service appointments unless the government enacts radical economic restructuring to build productive industrial lines and real production capacities.

Consequently, Al-Obeidi argued, an inability to accommodate these incoming labor cohorts will inevitably trigger widespread social unrest as youth exercise their legitimate right to demand viable livelihoods.

Compounding this looming crisis is a structural paradox within the domestic economy: despite high unemployment figures, private-sector enterprises face chronic talent deficits.

Al-Obeidi observed that nearly every private firm, including his own organization, struggles to recruit qualified local personnel because the traditional public education system fails to equip graduates with modern, market-relevant competencies.

This systemic failure places accountability squarely on the Ministries of Education and Higher Education, whose outputs remain disconnected from private industry demands.

Under standard economic models, every one-percent expansion in a specific sector’s gross domestic product typically generates a two-percent rise in corresponding job opportunities.

However, Al-Obeidi pointed out that in Iraq, economic expansion frequently bypasses domestic labor entirely due to this widening skill deficit. In the booming residential real estate and construction sectors, developers have repeatedly turned to Egyptian, Turkish, and Iranian firms and laborers to fill operational needs, underscoring an acute domestic shortage of skilled technical talent capable of matching the execution standards required by modern infrastructure projects.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets German president in Berlin
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in Berlin on Tuesday to discuss prospects for political, economic, and investment cooperation between the two countries.

Al-Zaidi is expected to hold discussions with representatives of 30 German companies to discuss investment opportunities and economic cooperation between Iraq and Germany, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The corporations participating in the discussion, which will address cooperation and investment partnerships between the two sides, expressed a strong desire to invest in Iraq.

The Iraqi prime minister’s discussions in Berlin will include finalizing several memoranda of understanding in the economic and investment sectors, strengthening the partnership between the two countries.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Germany comes a day after he concluded a trip to the French capital, Paris, where he and President Emmanuel Macron oversaw the signing of six memoranda of understanding covering air defense, military supply, energy supplies, civil aviation, development finance, and youth and innovation support.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Germany is a significant step in the Iraqi government’s efforts to strengthen commercial ties with other nations and multinational enterprises.

The visit aims to attract foreign investment and utilize German expertise and technology to support Iraq’s economic development.

World.title: Iraq PM donates 47 billion dinars to renovate five Baghdad hospitals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Specialized engineering teams have initiated extensive rehabilitation and modernization works across five major public hospitals in Baghdad, financed through personal donations provided by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, Minister of Health Abdul Hussein Al-Mousawi announced on Tuesday, September 15, 2026.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Mousawi disclosed that the Prime Minister contributed 47 billion Iraqi dinars out of his personal funds to underwrite the long-overdue infrastructure upgrades after engineering assessments confirmed an absolute absence of allocated state budget lines for the capital projects.

The structural renovation campaign spans anchor healthcare institutions across the capital, comprising Baghdad Hospital within the Medical City complex, Al-Kadhimiya Teaching Hospital, Al-Kindi Hospital, Al-Yarmouk Hospital, and Al-Zafraniya Hospital.

In addition to covering the full 47-billion-dinar reconstruction bill, Al-Mousawi revealed that Al-Zaidi personally donated $2 million directly to the Ministry of Health to procure an essential, life-saving pharmaceutical supply that faced severe procurement delays due to funding shortfalls, allowing specialized medical crews to begin immediate rehabilitation works across the designated hospital wards.

Al-Mousawi explained that publicly spotlighting these targeted private contributions serves to cultivate broader philanthropic and civic engagement, urging corporate institutions and private-sector actors to step forward and assist in rebuilding the country’s burdened healthcare architecture.

The health minister highlighted that this collaborative model has already yielded tangible support from the Association of Private Hospitals, which responded by significantly expanding its corporate social responsibility commitments, pledging to conduct 10 specialized surgical procedures free of charge each month, well exceeding the initial civic target of four surgeries.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Wednesday stepped up its attack against the Centre and accused it of "giving into" United States' demand to get rid of zero MDR and charge for UPI.In a social media post on X, senior Congress leader Jairam Ramesh dubbed the government's decision to introduce merchant discount rate on UPI as "NOTA - Narendra's Ongoing Trump Appeasement" and alleged that the move was aimed at helping US card companies compete with UPI."Tomorrow, the US House of Representatives votes on a Bill that introduces 100% tariffs on India. The US Senate has already approved this draconian law. Meanwhile, the Trump regime has been cracking down on Indian immigrants and making tougher laws against them. H-1B visa costs have been increased and such holders could soon be deported immediately when out of a job. Such holders are mostly IT professionals," Jairam Ramesh said."Here, the Modi Govt has given into a US demand to get rid of zero MDR and charge for UPI. The US Trade Representative earlier this year criticized UPI for being free and having driven out Visa and Mastercard. Why 0.4% MDR? Is it because debit card MDR is also 0.4%? Is this being done to enable US card companies to compete with UPI?" he questioned.The Congress leader claimed that the estimated cost of running the entire UPI ecosystem is around Rs 20,000 crore annually, which he said is less than 10% of what the RBI has been transferring to the Union government in the past few years to show healthy public finances for the Modi government."Is this going to make UPI 'sustainable' as the Govt claims? The estimated cost of running the entire UPI ecosystem is around Rs 20,000 crore annually. This is less than 10% of what the RBI has been transferring to the Union Govt in the past few years so as to show healthy public finances for the Modi Govt," he said."The PM has redefined NOTA - Narendra's Ongoing Trump Appeasement," the Congress leader added.Jairam Ramesh's remarks came after the National Payments Corporation of India on Tuesday introduced a new MDR framework, under which UPI merchant transactions above Rs 2,000 will attract an MDR of 0.4%, while consumers will continue to transact free of cost using UPI.The revised UPI MDR framework will come into effect from October 15, 2026, and will apply to select merchant transactions.

NEW DELHI: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has warned consumers against using two imported cosmetic creams after testing found them to be unauthorised for sale in India and containing excessive levels of heavy metals that may pose health risks.The cosmetics division of CDSCO has named Goree Beauty Cream and Chandni Whitening Cream, both labelled as âMade in Pakistanâ, in a public health alert dated September 8. The regulator said neither product had been issued a registration certificate by the competent authority for import and sale in India.CDSCO said laboratory testing and analysis had verified that the products were unauthorised and contained heavy metals beyond specified limits, which could cause toxic effects.The regulator has advised consumers not to buy or use the two products, or similarly named products if already purchased. It has also asked sellers, distributors and other establishments not to sell, distribute or advertise them. Regulatory enforcement units have been directed to ensure that the products are not sold in their jurisdictions.CDSCO said consumers should buy only authorised cosmetics carrying details such as the manufacturing licence number, manufacturerâs details, batch number, manufacturing and expiry dates, and, in the case of imported cosmetics, the registration number.The alert comes under the regulatory framework of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Cosmetics Rules, 2020. CDSCO said cosmetic manufacturing for sale requires a licence from the State Licensing Authority, while imported cosmetics must be registered with the Central Licensing Authority.

Amid repeated cases of border strife with China, India had stopped publicly articulating its One-China policy 16 years ago. However, in practice, Indiaâs position on both Tibet and Taiwan has remained unchanged under successive governments.

Government maintains its policy on Taiwan is clear and consistent, as it facilitates and promotes interactions in areas of trade, investment, tourism, culture, education and other such people-to-people exchanges.





On Tibet, India continues to recognise that the Tibet Autonomous Region is part of the territory of the Peopleâs Republic of China, as stated in the Declaration on Principles for Relations and Comprehensive Cooperation signed by then PM Atal Behari Vajpayee and Premier Wen Jiabao in 2003. The declaration also stated that India does not allow Tibetans to engage in anti-China political activities in the country.

World.title: 7 Keralam wards face bypolls as civic representatives quit for secure jobs
World.content:
The lure of a permanent job and a better life is hard to resist, at least for a few civic representatives in Keralam who quit their posts, paving the way for bypolls in the wards they represented.

Of the 38 local body wards going to polls on September 28, seven grama panchayat wards have fallen vacant after elected representatives resigned after securing jobs.

While two of them have travelled abroad, three have landed part-time government jobs. One member quit following her appointment as an anganwadi supervisor and another after being appointed to a minister’s staff. Of the seven people, two each are from the Congress and the CPI(M), and three from the IUML.

Choosing between the responsibilities entrusted to them by the electorate and the need for financial security has not been an easy task, some of them say.

“I was totally confused when I got the opportunity to go to Italy. I had applied for a visa in 2024. I accepted the offer to contest the election as the visa got delayed. I’m sad that I had to leave the responsibilities entrusted upon me by the people, but I didn’t have another option,” said Raji Rajeev, who quit as the member of the Puliyanam South ward of Parakkadavu grama panchayat.

She said the CPI(M) leadership allowed her to take the decision she felt was best for her life, though the reaction of the people was mixed. She hoped her decision would not affect her party’s prospects in the bypoll.

Sindu Sanjayan of the Congress quit as the member representing Blockpadi ward of Ranni Grama Panchayat in Pathanamthitta district after securing a part-time job through the Employment Exchange. She was in her fourth term as a panchayat member. “I had always wanted to find a job, and I kept renewing my application at the Employment Exchange. My party leadership and the people in the ward supported my decision,” she said.

Both Ms. Rajeev and Ms. Sanjayan said that the monthly honorarium of ₹8,000 for a panchayat member was hardly sufficient to meet their requirements.

Low payment cited

Former Kochi Mayor M. Anilkumar, also the co-chair of the Kerala Urban Policy Commission, said the low payment had been making the job of an elected local body representative unattractive to many, including the youth.

“For long, even Corporation councillors have been quitting after securing jobs as many elected representatives find it difficult to run their day-to-day affairs with the honorarium they get. The Urban Commission had recommended increasing the amount considerably,” he said.

Soumini Jain, another former Kochi Mayor, meanwhile, felt it was wrong to relinquish the responsibilities of an elected representative midway for better income.

“Once you enter electoral politics, you should be totally committed to it and aware of what you are going to do. Leaving the people’s mandate midway and causing an unnecessary bypoll is not the right thing to do,” she said. She, however, stressed that the honorarium being paid was so low that increasing it was necessary to curb corruption.

Of the remaining 31 wards going to bypoll, 15 fell vacant following the death of sitting members, while seven became vacant after members resigned for political reasons and one after a member reportedly quit due to job stress. Bypolls were necessitated in eight wards after the members were elected as MLAs.

A grama panchayat member is eligible for a monthly honorarium of ₹8,000 and ₹200 per sitting, capped at ₹1,000 a month. The honorarium was just ₹3,000 as recently as 2022.

Elected members of a district panchayat are eligible for ₹9,800 per month, while those in block panchayats receive ₹15,600. The honorarium for municipal councillors and corporation councillors is ₹8,600 and ₹8,200, respectively.

Heads of local bodies and different standing committees are eligible for higher amounts. A district panchayat president is eligible for ₹16,800 a month and a block panchayat president for ₹15,600. In grama panchayats, presidents get ₹14,200, while the honorarium for municipal chairpersons and corporation mayors is ₹15,600 and ₹15,800, respectively.

The State Finance Commission has recommended increasing the honorarium of elected representatives in local bodies.

World.title: ED arrests Kolkata man in land grabbing-linked PMLA case
World.content:
The Enforcement Directorate has arrested a Kolkata-based man in a money laundering case linked to alleged land grabbing and forgery of land records, officials said on Wednesday (September 16, 2026).

They said Amit Ganguly was taken into custody on Tuesday night (September 15, 2026) under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).

Mr. Ganguly is alleged to have acquired control over properties belonging to different persons and entities through the use of "forged" board resolutions, fabricated agreements for sale containing forged signatures and fabricated deeds and other documents.

It is also alleged that such illegal acts were done by manipulation of land records, institution of civil proceedings on false or fabricated claims, denial of lawful entitlements of landowners, and the use of threats and physical force against persons seeking their legitimate rights, the officials said.

Mr. Ganguly faces as many as 23 police FIRs registered against him and linked entities by the West Bengal Police, they said.

World.title: Police search DMK Minister Anbil Mahesh’s house over alleged multi-crore fraud involving private schools
World.content:
A team from the Central Crime Branch, Chennai City, began a search at the residences of former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi at Tiruchi and Chennai on Wednesday (September 16, 2026).

A five-member team began the operation at 7:30 a.m. at Mr. Poyyamozhi’s residence in Thennur Anna Nagar, Tiruchi, related to an alleged multi-crore fraud involving private schools during the previous DMK regime when he was Minister.

Earlier, the Central Crime Branch had registered a case and arrested B.T. Arasakumar on charges of collecting large sums of money amounting to around ₹100 crore from private school managements for upgrading schools, gaining permanent recognition and securing building plan approvals.

Arasakumar had run an unregistered association named Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association.

Raid an act of political vendetta, diversionary tactic of TVK-led government: Stalin

DMK president and former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin termed the police searches at the houses of former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi in Chennai and Tiruchi an act of political vendetta and a diversionary tactic of the TVK-led government.

In a post on X, Mr. Stalin listed several issues in Tamil Nadu, including protests by people affected by power cuts; protests by fishermen in Pattinapakkam against the construction of an Assembly-Secretariat complex; protests by relatives of those who went missing in Nepal flash floods over not receiving a proper response from the government; people struggling due to a shortage of Aavin milk; a double murder in Ramanathapuram; a government bus driver beaten to death during the Vinayagar Chaturthi procession in Chennai; and the harassment of a woman police constable by a TVK functionary in Ayanavaram.

“Ignoring all these issues that are shaking the State, the Chief Minister [C. Joseph Vijay] is conducting a shoot in London. In frustration over its inability to resolve these issues, the incompetent TVK government has unleashed raids as a weapon against former Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi to divert the people’s attention,” Mr. Stalin said.

He said the DMK would legally fight against what he termed “a blatant act of political vendetta.” Mr. Stalin also said conducting searches against the Opposition cannot ease the people’s anger and that the TVK-led government will soon realise that false allegations will not stand before the law either.

World.title: ‘I am a TamPunj and would not live anywhere else but Chennai’
World.content:
I was born in 1946 in that part of Punjab that is now in Pakistan. My family moved to Coonoor before the Partition. In the 1960s, we needed to move out for work and education requirements and looked for opportunities in other places in the country but chose Madras since we had people in the city at the time. By 1965, we moved to Madras.

The people were so nice, soft-spoken, and extremely helpful. When I was new here, I didn’t know my way around and so if I asked for an address, people would walk with me and show me the place — even if it was two streets away. The city used to be so quiet, not much traffic. We could walk on Mount Road on Sunday afternoons. Now, there is traffic everywhere. The city has grown, Gen Z is here.

But the city still has a lot of goodness in its heart. During COVID-19, when we had to prepare food for people who were travelling home by train, shopkeepers opened their stores when we said we were from the Punjab Association, though they did not know us. When they learnt why we wanted provisions, they voluntarily gave some items for free.

Chennai is relatively safer than most other cities and is also more affordable. Sometime ago, I went to Nagpur and a friend had given his car for local use, but I could not drive on those roads. You can still drive comfortably in Chennai. Over the years, we have all learnt Tamil and our friends have learnt Hindi and Punjabi. I am a TamPunj and wouldn't live anywhere else but in Chennai.

(As told to Deepa H. Ramakrishnan)
