World.title: Kazakhstan to host South Korea, Central Asian parliament meeting in 2027
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 16. Kazakhstan will host the fourth meeting of the Speakers of the Parliaments of South Korea and Central Asian countries in spring 2027, South Korean National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik said.

According to the Kazakh president's press service, he made the remarks during a meeting with Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev in Seoul.

"I hope that Kazakhstan and the Republic of Korea will continue to make even greater progress in mutually beneficial cooperation and joint prosperity. The National Assembly of the Republic of Korea, for its part, will actively support these efforts. In addition, the fourth meeting of the Speakers of the Parliaments of the Republic of Korea and Central Asian countries will be held in Kazakhstan next spring. I also plan to participate in this forum and hope to meet with you again in Kazakhstan," Cho said,

He noted that Kazakhstan is South Korea's largest trade and investment partner in Central Asia, highlighting energy, digitalization and artificial intelligence as key areas of cooperation between the two countries.

Cho also welcomed the expansion of cultural and humanitarian ties and tourism exchanges between Kazakhstan and South Korea.

Tokayev, in turn, said that interparliamentary dialogue between the two countries had deepened in recent years and that contacts between Kazakhstan's Parliament and South Korea's National Assembly would continue through the deputies of Kazakhstan's Kurultai.

The president also highlighted the expansion of trade and investment ties, noting that more than 1,000 joint ventures with Korean capital operate in Kazakhstan.

He added that around 120,000 ethnic Koreans live in Kazakhstan, describing the community as a "golden bridge" of friendship between the two countries.

Tokayev briefed his interlocutor on the results of the talks held the previous day with President Lee Jae Myung.

"It was a substantive and meaningful meeting. We reached an important agreement to elevate bilateral cooperation to a future-oriented comprehensive strategic partnership," the President of Kazakhstan said.

World.title: OTS becomes active platform for regional cooperation – Secretary General
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 16. The Organization of Turkic States (OTS) has become an active platform for regional cooperation, Secretary General of the OTS Kubanychbek Omuraliev said at the 2nd Conference of the Leading National Analytical Centers of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) in Baku, Trend's correspondent reports from the event.

He noted that the common goal for the Turkic states is clear: to transform shared geography, cultural ties, history, human capital, and economic potential into practical, sustainable development.

"In recent years, the OTS has expanded its multifaceted cooperation, encompassing 63 mechanisms across diverse fields—ranging from foreign policy and trade to energy, the 'green economy,' tourism, digitalization, and even space exploration.

The combined GDP of OTS member and observer states has surpassed $2.4 trillion, their total trade turnover has reached approximately $1.27 trillion, and their total population has exceeded 180 million. These figures demonstrate the scale of our collective economic potential while also reminding us of our responsibilities.

Our goal shouldn't be limited merely to increasing trade volumes. We must also make trade faster, more predictable, digital, diversified, and more beneficial for businesses and communities across the entire region," he noted.

The Secretary General added that the Middle Corridor has become one of the most important instruments for strengthening economic cooperation among the Turkic states.

"This is not merely a transport route. It creates new opportunities for trade, investment, and other economic prospects across the Turkic region. The success of the Middle Corridor does not depend solely on physical infrastructure. Ports, railways, roads, and logistics centers must be supported by complementary systems such as efficient border procedures, regulated tariffs, and reliable digital services," the Secretary General emphasized.

The2nd Conference of the Leading National Analytical Centers of the OTS is being held in Baku.

The conference, dedicated to the theme "Strengthening Economic Cooperation within the Framework of the Organization of Turkic States through Continuous Consultations and Joint Research," is focused on discussions of the prospects for the development of economic cooperation, institutional mechanisms, and opportunities for joint research among the member states of the OTS.

Representatives from various government agencies, think tanks, research institutions, and other organizations of Azerbaijan, Türkiye, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Hungary, and the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus are participating in the conference.

World.title: Kyrgyzstan and Lithuania discuss prospects for expanding bilateral cooperation
World.content:
Photo: Press Service of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kyrgyzstan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 16. Kyrgyzstan and Lithuania discussed prospects for strengthening bilateral political and economic cooperation during the third round of political consultations held in Bishkek.

According to the Kyrgyz Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the consultations took place on September 15. The Kyrgyz delegation was headed by Deputy Foreign Minister Meder Abakirov, while the Lithuanian delegation was led by Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs of Lithuania Krištupas Vaitiekūnas.

The sides emphasized the importance of further strengthening political dialogue, including through the organization of mutual visits at the highest and high levels.

Particular attention was paid to migration and tourism, as well as promising areas of trade and economic cooperation, including digitalization, transport, logistics and energy.

The parties also discussed expanding contacts between the business communities of the two countries, holding a Kyrgyz-Lithuanian business forum, implementing joint pilot projects and further developing the legal framework for bilateral cooperation.

The consultations also featured a detailed exchange of views on regional and international issues and cooperation within international organizations, including the United Nations and the European Union.

World.title: Uzbekistan, British AREMCA explore AI for geological exploration
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 16. Uzbekistan and British company AREMCA are exploring the use of artificial intelligence to analyze geological data, identify prospective mineral areas and improve the efficiency of mining operations.

This was reflected in the statement by the Ministry of Ministry of Mining and Geology of Uzbekistan, following a meeting between First Deputy Minister Feruza Khamidova and representatives of AREMCA to discuss the company’s projects in Central Asia and potential areas for cooperation in Uzbekistan.

During the meeting, AREMCA presented its ongoing projects in the region and outlined opportunities to apply AI-based technologies to geological exploration and mining. The company’s representatives discussed the use of artificial intelligence to process and analyze geological data, identify areas with potential mineral resources and support more efficient mining operations.

The discussion comes as Uzbekistan seeks to expand the use of digital technologies in the geological and mining sectors and improve the efficiency of exploration and resource development.

Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Mining and Geology also presented the country’s system for granting subsoil-use rights through auctions. Officials provided information on the online platforms used to conduct the auctions, as well as recent changes to legislation governing access to mineral resources.

The sides exchanged views on potential areas for further cooperation, including the introduction of advanced technologies into geological exploration and mining activities.

“The introduction of advanced digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, can create new opportunities to improve geological data analysis and the efficiency of mineral exploration and mining,” the ministry said in a statement following the meeting.

The talks also covered workforce development and the need to train qualified specialists capable of working with new technologies in the mining and geological sectors.

The sides expressed interest in continuing dialogue on technology cooperation and identifying practical opportunities for AREMCA to participate in Uzbekistan’s mining and geological development.

World.title: Azerbaijan has top-level capital flows and inflows within Turkic world – analyst
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 16. Azerbaijan’s capital flows and inflows within the Turkic world are at the top level, Executive Director of the Center for Analysis of Economic Reforms and Communication of Azerbaijan (CAERC) Vusal Gasimli said at the 2nd Conference of the Leading National Analytical Centers of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) in Baku, Trend's correspondent reports from the event.

He noted that Azerbaijan is the leader in investment among Turkic states.

"Azerbaijan's Middle Corridor Sustainability Index score stands at approximately 0.5 out of 1. This figure indicates, on the one hand, a solid foundation for sustainability, and on the other, significant opportunities to expand and improve regional infrastructure and to digitize the Middle Corridor," he stated.

Gasimli added that an analysis of the economic and financial indicators of the OTS region reveals that while the region accounts for 2% of global GDP and 2.3% of global savings, its share of global banking assets is merely 0.8%.

"To address the potential financial gap, the primary task is to mobilize the region's savings potential and channel these resources into efficient investments and sustainable economic growth through next-generation financial solutions," he emphasized.

The 2nd Conference of the Leading National Analytical Centers of the OTS is being held in Baku.

The conference, dedicated to the theme "Strengthening Economic Cooperation within the Framework of the Organization of Turkic States through Continuous Consultations and Joint Research," is focused on discussions of the prospects for the development of economic cooperation, institutional mechanisms, and opportunities for joint research among the member states of the OTS.

Representatives from various government agencies, think tanks, research institutions, and other organizations of Azerbaijan, Türkiye, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Hungary, and the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus are participating in the conference.

World.title: China's Zijin Mining Group interested in Kazakhstan's Shalkiya lead-zinc deposit
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 16. China's Zijin Mining Group has expressed interest in developing Kazakhstan's Shalkiya lead-zinc deposit in the Kyzylorda region, Kazakhstan's government said.

First Deputy Prime Minister Nurlybek Naliyev met with representatives of Zijin Mining Group to discuss investment cooperation in Kazakhstan's mining and metallurgical sector, including the development and processing of solid minerals.

"The parties discussed prospects for investment cooperation in the mining and metallurgical sector, including projects for the development and processing of solid mineral resources," the government said.

Zijin Mining Group expressed interest in Shalkiya and readiness to explore the possibility of participating in the project, the statement said. The sides also discussed deep processing of mineral resources, the introduction of modern technologies, job creation, and environmental and industrial safety.

The parties agreed to continue cooperation on promising areas, according to the government.

Zijin Mining Group is among the world's largest mining companies. In 2025, it produced more than 1 million tons of copper, ranking fourth globally, while its gold production reached 90 tons.

In Kazakhstan, Zijin Mining Group operates at the Raigorodok deposit in the Akmola region. The company is investing more than $600 million in the construction of a new gold processing plant. The project will add processing capacity of 10 million tons of ore per year, increasing the total capacity of the mining and processing complex to 16 million tons.

According to ShalkiyaZINC company, the Shalkiya deposit was discovered in 1959 and is one of the world's largest zinc and lead deposits. It contains more than 30% of Kazakhstan's total zinc reserves and ranks among the world's largest deposits by zinc reserves. The deposit is located 17 kilometers northeast of Zhanakorgan in Kazakhstan's Kyzylorda region.

World.title: Uzbekistan maps out greener path for Tashkent’s urban development
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 16. Uzbekistan is placing greater emphasis on environmental considerations and infrastructure capacity as it develops new architectural and urban projects in Tashkent.

This was reflected in the statement by the National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change of Uzbekistan, following a meeting between Head of the Presidential Administration Saida Mirziyoyeva and initiators of major architectural projects, independent experts and urban planners, as well as representatives of leading creative studios and higher education institutions, to discuss the capital’s urban development and environmental challenges.

The meeting focused on the current situation in Tashkent’s urban planning and ecology sectors, with participants stressing the need for careful assessment of the city’s future development.

The committee said new construction projects should contribute to the city’s development without creating additional imbalances or placing excessive pressure on urban infrastructure and territorial systems.

“The future development of Tashkent requires careful analysis to ensure that new construction contributes to the city while preserving environmental balance and the capacity of urban infrastructure,” the committee said in a statement following the meeting.

The discussion comes as Uzbekistan continues to expand urban development in and around the capital. Earlier this year, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev called for urbanization to be aligned with public interests, a healthy urban environment and environmental requirements. The authorities have also identified the expansion of green areas as a priority in Tashkent.

Participants at the meeting also discussed the role of private-sector initiatives in improving the urban environment. The National Committeee emphasized the importance of supporting businesses seeking to make Tashkent more comfortable, landscaped, clean and safe.

Such support was described as one of the priorities set by President Mirziyoyev as part of the broader development agenda for New Uzbekistan.

The meeting brought together specialists from architecture, urban planning, creative industries and academia, creating a platform to discuss how expertise from these sectors can contribute to the capital’s future development.

The government has previously emphasized the need for modern urban planning to preserve green spaces, protect historical and cultural heritage and ensure that transport and engineering infrastructure develops alongside construction.

World.title: Kazakhstan's Air Astana to resume flights to Dubai
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 16. Kazakhstan's Air Astana plans to resume regular flights from Almaty and Astana to Dubai starting October 1 and 2, 2026, respectively, the airline said.

The Almaty-Dubai-Almaty service will initially operate four flights per week in October, with frequency gradually increasing to 12 flights per week by the end of the month.

The Astana-Dubai-Astana service will start with three flights per week and increase to 10 flights per week by the end of October.

"The airline is monitoring developments in the region and may adjust its flight schedule depending on the situation in the Middle East, and will inform passengers of any further changes," Air Astana said.

Air Astana announced the suspension of flights to Dubai on July 12, 2026, amid geopolitical tensions surrounding Iran and heightened risks to civil aviation in the Middle East.

Military and political instability in the region, periodic restrictions on Iranian airspace, and risks related to missile and drone activity have prompted international airlines to take precautionary measures and adjust their flight schedules.

Air Astana, founded in 2002, is Kazakhstan's leading airline and largest air carrier. Samruk-Kazyna National Welfare Fund is the largest shareholder of Air Astana, holding a 41% stake in the company. Other shareholders include the Unified Accumulative Pension Fund, which owns a 6.5% stake, while a group of other investors collectively holds 51.64%.

World.title: Gold Coast mayor apologises for outburst but maintains recollection of Trump dinner
World.content:
Under-fire Gold Coast Mayor Tom Tate says he had a conversation about tariffs with US President Donald Trump just before dinner at Mar-a-Lago — despite the Trump Organization claiming no such dinner happened.

The outspoken mayor today also apologised to Australian viewers and reporters for swearing on Tuesday at a journalist during questioning about the trip, which has resulted in conflicting accounts of a high-profile dinner at Mar-a-Lago.

Loading...

"I was out of line, using a swear word, even though being frustrated … when you wear the mayoralty role you've got to rise above that, and for that, I didn't do my job," he said.

Mr Tate, the energetic mayor of Australia's sixth-biggest city, had attracted headlines when he told multiple media outlets of having dinner with the president at his holiday retreat in Florida in February this year.

He even described sharing tomahawk steaks and drinking expensive wine.

The mayor was in Mar-a-Lago for the signing of an ultimately doomed Gold Coast Trump Tower, with the ceremony between a Queensland developer and the Trump Organization, headed by the president's son Eric.

Altus CEO David Young with Trump Origanization Executive Vice President Eric Trump. (Supplied: Altus Property Group)

He told media they had a later evening function with the president. "Mate, I had dinner with him," he told Triple M Gold radio.

But the ABC revealed on Monday conflicting accounts, with the White House saying the president and first lady Melania Trump "did not have dinner with that group" including Mr Tate. And an ABC right to information request with council turned up little documentation about the Florida trip.

While a business associate of Mr Tate's told local media he was at the dinner and backed the mayor's recollection, the Trump Organization issued a further blistering statement describing the Gold Coast politician's account as a "complete fabrication".

"President Trump has never had dinner with Mayor Tate," a Trump Organization spokesperson said. "While the president was on the patio, he briefly said hello to the mayor's table, as he typically does with guests at Mar-a-Lago. He then proceeded to a separate dinner that had absolutely nothing to do with Mayor Tate or his event."

Mayor Tom Tate says he had dinner with the US President at Mar-a-Lago earlier this year. (Reuters: Nathan Howard)

Mr Tate today said: "I have to disagree. I had my conversation, we had dinner, and I won't get into some of the wonderful things we discussed, because it's private."

He described having a conversation with the president "before dinner, outside the dining room" that touched on tariffs and Australia's movie industry.

"There's many other conversations I had with the president, with Eric, with Lara (Trump, Eric's wife), and I still have the belief that what went on during that dinner function, I didn't want to betray … the privacy there."

He played down any damage to business deals. "I'm not having a war with the Trump Organization. I'm telling you what my recollection is and what's happened with me. How they record that on their side, I'm going 'Well, good you got to do what you got to do' ".

Gold Coast Council records from the time show Mr Tate's itinerary was full many days in other cities when he was on the global journey in February, even detailing what clothes to wear and briefing packs about people he was to meet.

The itinerary's three days at Mar-a-Lago only contain four words about events: "Meeting with Trump Organization."

Mr Tate was in Florida for the signing of the proposed Gold Coast Trump Tower. (Supplied: Altus Property Group)

His council report and official Instagram also contain a multitude of selfie photographs from the global trip, including with representatives from Airbnb. No selfies were posted from Mar-a-Lago.

Ratepayers paid for flights to Florida, and Mr Tate has said he was invited there as mayor.

He initially recorded in gift registers to having accepted the Trump Organization's accommodation and meals for the trip, sparking controversy given a $1.5 billion tower on the Gold Coast was planned.

The mayor later changed his register to say he had paid for the accommodation — not the meals — and said he had always intended to pay personally but had just been waiting for an invoice to arrive.

He has declined to hand over the invoice in a right to information request, now saying the trip was private.

He told journalists on Monday he had not been charged mates rates but would not divulge the amount.

World.title: Major AI company Anthropic signs deal to use $32b Queensland data centre
World.content:
AI giant Anthropic has signed its first deal in Australia to use a $32 billion data centre hub on Queensland's Western Downs.

The facility will be built near Dalby by a Singaporean developer and is expected to create thousands of ongoing jobs.

The Western Downs Digital Park is set to be the largest facility of its kind in the country, with a power draw comparable to 1.5 million average Australian households.

Anthropic aims to be able to start using the centre in 2027, despite the development application only being filed with the local council last month.

The ABC understands Anthropic would use the site to power its artificial intelligence program Claude to answer user questions, rather than for training AI models.

The multi-billion-dollar investment in is almost five times greater than the 2032 Brisbane Olympic and Paralympic Games infrastructure budget.

The data centre would be located near existing gas-fired power stations. (ABC News: Brandon Long)

Premier David Crisafulli said it was a direct result of his recent trade mission to the US.

"This is a major win that will deliver more jobs, put more energy into Queensland's grid and drive down power prices for Queenslanders," he said.

"My meeting with Anthropic during the trade mission was to outline why Queensland was the place to invest, with energy security, locations to invest and a streamlined approvals process to get it right."

Mr Crisafulli has promised data centre investment will drive down energy costs for consumers, and companies must add energy to the local grid.

Data centre could draw quarter of state's power The proposed $30 billion data centre in Queensland has a peak capacity comparable to the average power requirements of 1.5 million households.

The government said the digital park would not require any new transmission infrastructure, and would use minimal water during operation.

The Western Downs hub's water usage will be broadly comparable with a conventional office building of the same size.

The plot earmarked for the park is about 725 hectares, with the facility expected to take four to six years to build.

Anthropic's lease is subject to Foreign Investment Review Board approval.

David Crisafulli is lobbying for coal and gas to power data centres as well as renewables. (ABC News: Matt Roberts)

The Queensland government and the Commonwealth recently locked horns over rules for new data centre development.

The federal Labor government had wanted all new data centres to be anchored by new renewable energy projects.

But the state LNP administration successfully argued Queensland go its own way and use a range of energy sources including coal and gas.

"To have secured Anthropic's first major investment in Australia is an endorsement for our state's open for business approach, and the commonsense decision endorsed by the prime minister and national cabinet to allow Queensland's unique position in owning its power generation and transmission assets," Mr Crisafulli said.

CEO and Co-Founder of Anthropic Dario Amodei recently issued a public warning about the pace of AI development. (Reuters: Denis Balibouse)

"This allows our state to be at the forefront of locking in data sovereignty and adding energy generation for lower power prices for Queenslanders and employment opportunities."

Anthropic will be required to invest in local communities and hire an engagement manager to ensure residents' and councils' concerns are heard.

It is understood that Anthropic would cover the full cost of connecting to the grid, including any network updates required.

The AI giant has been contacted for comment.

World.title: Unpacking the 12 days that threw Ed Sheeran's tour into chaos
World.content:
Ed Sheeran's upcoming shows look to have no support acts after the remaining openers, and a touring band he shares songs with, pulled out in solidarity with Macklemore after he was removed from remaining tour dates.

"After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates," Messina Touring Group told Rolling Stone.

American rapper Macklemore, real name Ben Haggerty, has been condemned for pro-Palestinian comments at recent shows.

Irish touring band Beoga and Irish support act Aaron Rowe, Danish group Lukas Graham and US musician Finneas have now all said they would longer participate in the tour.

Beoga had been performing several songs, including some the Irish folk band co-wrote with Sheeran, around the middle of each set.

The support of Macklemore by these fellow artists has put pressure on Sheeran who is set to resume the tour this weekend.

And the deterioration of Macklemore's time on Sheeran's Loop tour has played out via the media in real time, with other industry voices weighing in.

So how did it get to this point?

September 4: 'Free Palestine' comments at show

Macklemore has always been one of the music industry's most vocal critics of the Israel-Gaza conflict.

In 2024 he released a song called Hind's Hall, delivered in solidarity with US students protesting on university campuses for a ceasefire in Gaza.

"Block the barricade until Palestine is free," he raps on the track.

Loading...

But this particular fallout started on September 4 at his opening show for the tour in New Jersey.

When introducing Hind's Hall he said: "A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine."

The next day he echoed similar sentiments and said criticising Israel is no criticism of "my Jewish brothers and sisters".

September 6: Petition launched

After the shows in New Jersey concluded, the Israeli American Council launched a petition calling for the removal of Macklemore from Sheeran's line-up.

"Ed Sheeran, do not allow your stage to be used to divide people or spread one-sided political propaganda!" a post by the Israeli American Council on Instagram read.

"At Ed Sheeran's September 4 MetLife show, Macklemore used his opening set to push a one-sided political message through Hind's Hall, imagery from Gaza, and inflammatory and disputed political claims.

"Freedom of expression does not give anyone the right to turn someone else's stage into a platform for political propaganda."

September 7: Macklemore releases statement

In response to the petition, Macklemore posted a video of him performing at the stadium with the caption: "Wanting all humans to be treated equal should never be controversial."

Macklemore is known for incorporating his activism and pro-Palestinian stance in shows. (Instagram)

September 11: Pink gets involved

Enter the singer Pink, who released an extensive statement on her Instagram account criticising the rapper's comments.

The Jewish singer said she had reposted content that was critical of Macklemore earlier in the week and wanted to speak on the topic in her own words.

"Of course I don't speak for Israel, or for any government," she said.

"I never have. What I said in October 2023 is still exactly what I believe: Hamas is a terrorist organisation.

"Palestinians deserve a future that honours their humanity and their aspirations. Protecting innocent life comes first, everywhere, and nobody should ever celebrate the death of a child. Anybody's child."

Jewish artist Pink released a statement on Instagram. (Reuters)

She went on to recall a costume worn by Macklemore in 2014 that was widely criticised as antisemitic.

"He apologised, and I let it go, because that's what we do. We let it go," Pink wrote.

"Then last weekend he stood in front of a stadium full of music-loving families, with violent images from a war on the screens, dedicated a song to the movement of his choice, and then took the mic to tell all of the Jews in the stadium that it wasn't about them.

"You don't get to decide that for us."

September 14: Macklemore dropped from tour

A few days later Mackelmore announced that after a week of "difficult conversations" with Sheeran that he was dropped from his eight remaining shows on the Loop tour.

Macklemore dropped from Sheeran tour Macklemore says he has been dropped from Ed Sheeran's US tour over pro-Palestinian comments made on stage earlier this month.

Macklemore insisted the talks were rooted in "love and respect" but ended in a place of "fundamental disagreement" after he was told Robert Kraft, the owner of the next stadium Macklemore was to play at, asked Sheeran to remove him.

"Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium," Mackelmore wrote.

"Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour you will not be allowed to play in our venues."

The rapper said Sheeran was in a "f***ed up position".

Loading Instagram content

"His typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before," Macklemore wrote.

"He told me that the words 'Free Palestine' and the image of the Palestinian flag were hurtful to a lot of people he spoke with.

"I told him that if those words were more offensive that tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood."

Macklemore said Sheeran "couldn't get past his public facing 'I don't take sides'."

The statement also questioned why this was an issue, as Macklemore had been vocal about the issue for three years.

Macklemore has been dropped from Ed Sheeran's tour. (Reuters: Steve Marcus)

After he was named in the statement by Macklemore, Robert Kraft, who owns Gilette stadium and the New England Patriots Football Stadium shared his own statement.

"Based on Macklemore's recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran's shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line," Kraft said in a statement shared with ESPN.

Messina Touring Group, promoter of the US leg of Sheeran's Loop Tour, then told Rolling Stone that venue owners on the upcoming US tour dates notified the promoters they would not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore in the line-up.

September 15: Sheeran speaks out, support acts leave

In response, Sheeran released his own statement on Instagram.

He started out by saying he was "appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine" and that Macklemore asked to join his tour and was given the freedom to select his set list.

He said the decision to pull Macklemore was the promoter's decision.

"I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance rather than everything that was said," Sheeran wrote.

He confirmed there was a discussion with Mr Kraft and other venues on the tour.

"I was also involved in direct talks with promoters along with activists on both sides to try and find a mutual resolution for all, but the venue's and promoter's decision was final," he wrote.

Loading Instagram content

"I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I do not choose to speak publicly, it doesn't mean I don't have them, and it doesn't mean I don't care."

The same day, the remaining support acts pulled out of the tour.

Irish acts Beoga and Aaron Rowe, Danish band Lukas Graham, and US artist Finneas posted on Instagram about their decisions.

Rowe and Lukas Graham would have been replacements for Macklemore on Sheeran's remaining US dates.

"Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed," Finneas wrote.

Sheeran's support acts leave tour All four supporting acts for upcoming dates of Ed Sheeran's Loop tour have withdrawn in solidarity with rapper Macklemore who has been dropped for making pro-Palestinian comments.

"I have decided to withdraw from my upcoming tour dates with Ed Sheeran.

"I stand with Palestine and its people."

Danish band Lukas Graham wrote they loved Ed but could not carry on with the tour "as things stand".

"I'm sorry we won't be there," they wrote.

"This is a difficult decision but it's one I need to stand by."

Where to now?

The tour is scheduled to continue on Saturday in Philadelphia and no replacement opening act has been announced.

Sheeran has nine more tour dates in North America before moving to South America where he was due to be supported by Finneas.

Sheeran took the tour to Australia earlier this year, breaking attendance records for several stadiums.

World.title: Commissioner says system 'failing' amid reports kids living alone in squalor
World.content:
Reports more than a dozen children, including some as young as five, had been living unsupervised in squalid conditions in a town fuelled by resource-sector wealth have prompted WA's Children's Commissioner to declare the safety nets to protect children are "failing".

In a report by The Australian newspaper that has since been contested by the state government, the children had been living in a state-owned house in South Hedland, where the average weekly income is almost double the Australian average due to the wider region's vast mining operations.

An abandoned shopping trolley at the end of the street. (ABC News: Alistair Bates)

Child Protection Minister Jessica Stojkovski flew to the Pilbara on Monday to meet with representatives from police, sector partners and government departments.

It is not clear whether she visited the house itself, which sits in a cul-de-sac next to the town's main shopping precinct, but she said she had visited the street twice.

There were fiery exchanges in state parliament the following day, with the government conceding Port Hedland was about five child protection officers short.

The saga has prompted Children's Commissioner Jacqueline McGowan-Jones to declare the system created to protect vulnerable young people is "failing many children".

Jacqueline McGowan-Jones spoke about the Hedland issues on Wednesday. (ABC News: Jasmine Hughes)

"I've spoken to children in Hedland who don't feel safe at home and therefore they and try and find somewhere else to stay … who come in from more remote communities and then they're in overcrowded houses that aren't safe," she told 102.5 ABC Perth.

"These children themselves are not bad children — these are children who need the love, care and protection of everybody.

"If we've got children living in those sorts of conditions, then the whole system is failing. Education, health, mental health, child protection and policing."

Dr McGowan-Jones accepted parents must be expected to care for their children, but said more drug and alcohol rehabilitation facilities were necessary for a "whole-of-system approach".

Minister admits investigation was slow

Housing Minister John Carey today rejected accusations state agencies only addressed child protection issues in the Pilbara after they were highlighted in the media.

Speaking in parliament on Tuesday, Ms Stojkovski also contested reports the children were "regularly unsupervised".

Jessica Stojkovski addressed the Hedland issue in parliament, which was dominated by the topic on Tuesday. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

"I did not find evidence of this occurring as suggested — my view has been informed with input from not only the departments, but sector partners that I spoke to during my visit," she said.

Ms Stojkovski asked that child protection workers be acknowledged for the difficult jobs they do, but also admitted the investigation into this matter had progressed too slowly.

"Although child safety investigations are a comprehensive process that do require engagement with families and building trust, in this case, the child safety investigation has taken too long," she said.

"The department is working urgently to conclude this investigation."

Despite the revenue generated within the town, South Hedland is an area of disadvantage. (ABC News: Alistair Bates)

Dr McGowan-Jones said that was not surprising.

"[In] those regional and remote areas [it is] very difficult to find staff, and then if you do find them, they can't get housing," she said.

The minister has also ordered the state's top child protection worker oversee all child safety investigations and intensive family support cases in Port Hedland until the end of the year.

Opposition Leader Basil Zempilas said the minister must explain when the department found out about the Hedland situation, and what actions were undertaken, while the WA Greens are calling for Labor to convene an urgent roundtable on child safety.

Mobile surveillance towers have since been erected at the beginning of the cul-de-sac. (ABC News: Alistair Bates)

Frontline police 'frustrated'

WA Police Commissioner Col Blanch said police would always respond to reports of crime, disturbance and welfare concerns, but cannot be expected to care for neglected children.

Col Blanch says officers were frustated at the situation in Hedland. (ABC News: Lauren Smith)

"At a constable level, they're just re-attending and re-attending problem houses across this state, and they will feel exhausted, frustrated, fatigued … but at the district level, they are meeting with [relevant departments] and they are coming up with solutions," he said.

"We have to solve those problems, they're quite complex, they take a long time.

"We put in effort every day, and I've got to say, the people who do the work on the frontline are there for the right reasons, trying to do the right thing, and that doesn't mean we always get it right."

World.title: Breaking: Emergency warning for fire at Blackmore, west of Berry Springs
World.content:
Authorities have issued an emergency warning for a fire at Stockwell Road in Blackmore, west of Berry Springs, advising anyone who is unprepared to leave now.

Bushfires NT said structures had been impacted as the fire moved towards Mieland Road and Tuey Close, with residents in the area advised to enact their bushfire survival plan immediately.

A watch and act is also in place for a fast-moving fire at Uralla Road in Katherine East, with residents there urged to start taking action now to protect themselves and their property.

That fire is burning towards the Victoria Highway between the rail corridor and Uralla Road, and residents south of Bicentennial Drive are encouraged to enact their bushfire survival plan.

Bushfires NT crews are working to contain the fire at Uralla Road in Katherine East. (ABC News: James Elton)

Bushfires NT confirmed crews were working to contain the fire on the corner of Zimin Drive and the Victoria Highway but said there was "still a lot of work to take place to the north of the Adelaide-Darwin railway line" in the coming hours.

A 24-hour fire ban period for the Top End has also been extended into tomorrow.

Structures reportedly 'engulfed'

Acting Chief Fire Control Officer Nathaniel Stanford told ABC Radio Darwin properties along Mieland Road were under threat.

"Crews are currently working to install some tactical back burns to try and prevent it getting there, but I am seeing spot fires occurring ahead of the front on our mapping system at the moment," he said.

Mr Stanford said reports were coming from the fireground of structures being "impacted and engulfed".

"We haven't confirmed all the details on that yet," he said.

" At the moment, we're really trying to prevent that fire impacting any further structures. "

"If residents are unprepared for a fire coming towards their properties, the best advice is to leave now.

"If your plan is to stay and defend your property, ensure that you are in your bushfire survival plan and that you are taking all steps to protect yourself and your property from this."

Mr Stanford said the fire was expected to continue to spread to the north-west over the next hour before a change in wind direction at about 5pm.

"That could come earlier or later and that will change the direction of this fire and start taking it towards other areas," he said.

Bushfires NT has received unconfirmed reports of structures being "impacted and engulfed". (Facebook: Bushfires NT)

"We will keep all of our messaging up to date as to the likely spread of this fire so that community members can be aware."

Mr Stanford said observations on the ground appeared to confirm the fire had crossed to the western side of Mieland Road, with spot fires approaching "a number of homes".

"We are still getting numerous spot fires travelling ahead of this fire front and they are taking on the western side of Mieland Road," he said.

"So the situation is still unfolding, but it's not good news at this point, unfortunately.

"We're seeing flames in excess of 5 metres high and the spotting ahead, which is causing this fire to move incredibly fast."

Mr Stanford said it remained unclear whether the structures already impacted were homes or other buildings, with the fire's perimeter now in excess of 10 kilometres and growing "quite rapidly".

"When conditions allow, we will be undertaking further back-burning which will increase that to try and contain this fire, but at the moment our main focus is on the protection of the properties along Mieland Road and Tuey Close," he said.

Fire front 'just huge'

Blackmore resident Cindy, who lives on Stockwell Road, said the fire was "probably about three properties away" from her.

"This is our first year living here … I think, where the fire started, the house on that block is just gone," she told ABC Radio Darwin this afternoon.

"It's just huge, I could hear things blowing up because they had some old cars on their properties, so I think they're blowing up as the fire goes through.

" We've got a fire engine, we've got volunteer [firefighters], we've got planes dropping water, so it's all happening. "

Cindy said neighbours and locals volunteers "on buggies" were carrying water over to the fire.

"We have water tanks so if it was to come this [direction] we don't have much water to save ourselves, so hopefully it doesn't turn," she said.

World.title: Bazzana whacks two home runs in vital MLB win for Guardians
World.content:
Australian Travis Bazzana has continued his impressive rookie season with two home runs, helping Cleveland secure a crucial 7-6 win over the Chicago White Sox in its battle for a Major League Baseball play-off berth.

The Guardians have beaten the White Sox at home in their last two games, meaning they trail Chicago by just half a game in the American League Central standings.

Whoever finishes their division on top will go through to the post-season. Cleveland has topped the AL Central standings for the last two years.

Even if they finish second behind the White Sox, the Guardians are also well placed to progress with a wildcard berth.

It was the second time in his debut MLB season that Bazzana has hit two homers in a game. The first Australian number one baseball draft pick has racked up hits in his last five games.

On Wednesday (AEST), the all-star second baseman hit a solo homer in the first inning to give Cleveland a 3-0 lead.

The Guardians were 6-4 down in the bottom of the sixth when Bazzana hit another solo shot.

Brayan Rocchio ripped a two-run double with two outs in the ninth inning, scoring two runs to win the game.

The shortstop, nicknamed "Rocctember" and "Playoff Rocchio" for his late-season heroics, starred with two for three, including a walk and two runners batted in (RBIs).

Bazzana hit two for four with two RBIs.

The Guardians improved to a 77-75 record and have 10 games left in the regular season, while the White Sox are at 77-74.

World.title: Two NSW footballers behind bars after being found guilty of rape
World.content:
Two country New South Wales footballers are now behind bars after being found guilty of raping a woman at Scone in the Upper Hunter Valley in 2023.

Warning: this story includes details that some readers may find distressing.

Scone Thoroughbreds rugby league players Hayden Charles Topliss, 37, and Ryan Matthew Hawkshaw, 27, stood trial for a week in the Newcastle District Court.

Both faced four counts of aggravated sexual intercourse in company, while Topliss faced two additional charges of aggravated sexual intercourse and sexual touching.

The court heard the woman repeatedly said "no" and "stop" during the assault.

Hayden Topliss (L) and Ryan Hawkshaw (R) will be sentenced in November for raping a woman at Scone in 2023. (ABC News: Tamara Penniket)

The men had pleaded not guilty, claiming there was consent.

A jury today rejected that, finding the men guilty on all counts after deliberating for one day.

Supporters of the guilty pair sobbed and gasped as the verdicts were handed down.

Night of 'torture'

The offences happened in a spare bedroom at Topliss's house in Scone.

The woman told jurors she had consensual sex with Hawkshaw before Topliss came in and forced her down.

She said she was pulled around the bed, repositioned and had her hair pulled.

In her closing address, Crown Prosecutor Charisse Hodgeman said the woman was "unshaken and firm" when giving evidence that was "inherently believable".

"Her account was a detailed one rather than a false or reconstructed account," Ms Hodgeman said.

Ms Hodgeman said the woman never imagined there would be group sex.

The woman told jurors what happened in the spare bedroom that night was "torture".

The jury accepted there was no consent and the woman was repeatedly raped.

The men had been on bail but that has been revoked.

They will be sentenced in November

World.title: Family visas for foreign students targeted in migration crackdown
World.content:
International students would effectively be banned from bringing family members to Australia under a long-awaited overhaul of the immigration system, to be unveiled by Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke tomorrow.

In a speech entitled: "The work of managing the migration program: who arrives, who stays, who leaves", Mr Burke will outline changes to try to ensure the government meets its target of reducing net overseas migration (NOM) from 300,000 to 225,000 by 2028.

Mr Burke had planned to announce the policy six weeks ago but was forced to abruptly postpone the National Press Club (NPC) address because of a disagreement between ministers weighing competing priorities.

The ABC understands the reworked plan was endorsed by Cabinet's Expenditure Review Committee this week ahead of the rescheduled NPC address on Thursday.

The government plans to bring down the NOM by cutting the number of temporary visas, which has risen to three million, ensure migrants leave Australia once their visas have expired (to prevent so-called "visa hopping") and curb their ability to claim protection.

While international student numbers are expected to be left untouched, the ABC has been told they will effectively lose the ability to bring their families to Australia under the crackdown.

Migration is more complicated than this one number It's one thing to set a net migration target, but working out how to achieve that is a conversation political leaders have been less keen to have.

Last financial year, 337,427 student visas were granted and of those, 45,991 were secondary applicants, classed as dependents or family.

Labor's plan has some similarities to One Nation's migration policy, released this week, which included a crackdown on family visas for both students and skilled migrants.

It is unclear whether the government will also target the families of skilled migrants, but Mr Burke recently used his powers to dramatically slow down the processing of skilled and family visas lodged by applicants offshore.

Ahead of the announcement on Thursday, Mr Burke told Question Time he would like to implement Labor's planned overhaul via legislation but will pursue other "levers" if he could not get parliamentary support.

"Since the Hawke and Howard years, a whole lot of our immigration system has been demand-driven, and processing speeds is one of the only things, with planning levels, we currently have available," Mr Burke told Question Time today.

"The more tools that are available, the better we can target the system.

"The best form of outcome there will be if we are able to sort our way through for a legislative option. In the absence of that, there are still more levers the government will be able to use, and I'll be making those announcements tomorrow."

Changes expected to bridging visas

To address a blowout in bridging visas, the government has also been considering removing the work rights of temporary migrants whose claims for protection have been rejected by Home Affairs.

An average of 1,580 claims for protection are being lodged onshore every month, mostly by people from China, India and Malaysia who have come to Australia on a student or visitor visa.

The government is under pressure to bring down migration numbers. (AAP: Dean Lewins)

About 90 per cent of those claims are rejected, but applicants have the right to appeal the rulings through the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART) and the Federal Court, a process that regularly takes up to eight years.

During that time, a person is placed on a bridging visa allowing them to stay in the community and work, prompting government concerns some are simply "gaming the system".

Labor had also been considering changing the favourable treatment of British backpackers to make the scheme less attractive before the prime minister intervened and ruled out any move that could breach the Free Trade Agreement between the two countries.

Under pressure to bring down overseas arrivals, Mr Burke has already made sweeping changes to the migration system, pausing or slowing down the processing of working holiday maker visas in July, and reprioritising the processing of skilled visas.

The changes, under Ministerial Direction 119, mean any worker applying for a skilled visa from overseas is now at the back of the queue, pushing visa wait times from days to over a year in some cases.

World.title: A Looney Tunes live action long in the making, plus other new movies to watch this week
World.content:
(PG) 103 minutes

It all began in 1990 with an inspired piece of comic writing in the Shouts and Murmurs section of The New Yorker.

Humorist Ian Frazier dreamed up a court case starring Looney Tunes’ Wile E. Coyote as the plaintiff in a suit against Acme, the fictional manufacturer of the many specialised products the hapless predator had tried in his eternal pursuit of the Road Runner. The list included “itching powder, giant kites, Burmese tiger traps, anvils and two hundred-foot rubber bands” and the injuries to Mr Coyote caused by these dubious purchases had been serious enough to be “a major impediment” to his social life.

Will Forte as lawyer Kevin Avery and Wile E. Coyote, voiced by Eric Bauza, in Coyote vs Acme. Ketchup Entertainment via AP

This sparked strong interest from Looney Tunes’ studio, Warner Bros, and shooting eventually began on a film that mixed animation with live action in the manner of the 1988 hit Who Framed Roger Rabbit. The studio’s animation division struck hard times before the film could be released and management decided it should join Batgirl, among other animated films it was shelving at the time as tax write-offs.

World.title: Is a blood test for microplastics too good to be true?
World.content:
LifestyleLife & relationshipsWellness Is a blood test for microplastics too good to be true? Sarah Berry September 16, 2026 — 4:29pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Around the world each year, an estimated 20 billion kilograms of plastic ends up littering the environment. Inevitably, some of that waste breaks down into tiny particles called microplastics, which we inhale, eat or drink. Last year, American longevity influencer Bryan Johnson announced his company, Blueprint, had devised the “world’s first” at-home microplastics blood-testing kit for US$135. New microplastics tests are a response to concerns about their effect on our health. Getty Images/iStockphoto “The average male testicle has 8.2milligrams of microplastics and the average brain has more than 50 per cent more microplastics than 10 years ago,” said the 49-year-old on YouTube to an angsty soundtrack of violins. “The problem is bad, and it’s getting worse.” While Johnson’s company may have been the first, multiple other companies now offer at-home blood tests, including in Australia, where they can cost up to $750.



Why would you want your blood tested for microplastics? Related Article Health ‘Forever chemicals’ are everywhere. Here’s how to avoid them One small, new study found that people who had suffered a serious heart attack had higher levels of micro- and nano-plastics in their blood; another study published last week found that people with lung cancer were also more likely to have high levels of microplastics in their lungs; and other research has linked microplastics with reproductive, digestive and respiratory issues, with a suggested link to colon and lung cancer. It is understandable that people who feel concerned for their wellbeing might be interested in finding out the levels of microplastics in their bodies, so they can understand their risk factors and try to mitigate them. As the saying goes: “You can’t improve what you don’t measure.”



Johnson (over)shared an update of his own apparent improvements in May. “I had 165 microplastic particles in my semen just 18 months ago,” he wrote on LinkedIn, attributing the change to regular sauna sessions, a reverse osmosis water filter and removing plastics from his home. “Now, I have zero.” A promising result – except there are three key issues with testing for microplastics: the tests themselves are flawed; lipids in the blood can be mistaken for microplastics; and even if we can accurately measure microplastics in our bodies, there is no consensus about their impact. Why at-home tests are ‘useless’ and microplastics studies are complicated According to Oliver Jones, a professor of analytical chemistry at RMIT, these tests and the biomarkers they are testing are not validated, meaning the data they give you is “useless”. “The information you would potentially be getting is inaccurate, so there is nothing you can do with it. It’s meaningless,” Jones says. “No knowledge is no power.”



Measuring microplastics in our bodies is further complicated by the fact that microplastics look the same as fat compounds in the blood. This can lead to false positives, says Mark Green, an associate professor in reproductive biology at the University of Melbourne. “It is very, very hard to measure a small piece of plastic, which is made up of carbon and hydrogen, from a human matrix, which is also made up of carbon and hydrogen,” says Professor Kevin Thomas, director of the Queensland Alliance for Environmental Health Sciences at The University of Queensland. As a result, researchers still haven’t definitively proven microplastics make it into our bloodstream. “I find it difficult to understand how you could do an at-home test when we struggle with some of the most advanced instruments available to make the same measurements,” Thomas says.



Of the study suggesting people who had heart attacks also had higher levels of plastic, he said: “It is just as plausible that endogenous lipids in the blood are being misidentified as plastics. The headline could just as well read: ‘Patients who suffer heart attacks have more lipids in their blood’.” There are better ways to reduce our exposure to microplastics. Getty Images/iStockphoto This brings us to the third issue: even if it was possible to measure microplastics in our blood and our bodies, it doesn’t prove causation. For instance, the authors of the study linking microplastics with lung cancer acknowledged that diseased, inflamed lungs may be more likely to trap microplastics when we breathe them in. Studies connecting microplastics to health outcomes are interesting and worthy of further investigation, says Green.



Related Article Cardiovascular health This popular sweetener is linked to higher heart attack and stroke risk As microplastics are a physical particle, foreign to our bodies, they are likely to have an effect at some point and increase our inflammation markers at very least. “As to whether they cause specific diseases, that’s a different thing, and we need the methodology to be more accurate before we can ask those questions,” says Green. A better way to minimise exposure If researchers with access to the best equipment can’t confidently distinguish between fats and microplastics or quantify the effects, what value is an invalidated expensive finger-prick test?



Additionally, Jones questions what a person is meant to do with any results they do get. Unsurprisingly, some companies claim they can remove microplastics from your blood for a fee too. But there’s currently no proven way to completely remove microplastics from your blood, Jones says. He adds: “We have all these people selling microplastics tests or microplastic detoxes online and none of them remove anything except your money.” So what can people do? Start by maximising behaviours that support health such as getting enough exercise, a balanced diet, enough sleep and not drinking or smoking too much. We can also minimise our exposure to plastics. “There’s a lot we can do to reduce our exposure,” says Green. “And we can do that without blood tests.”



Where possible, don’t drink from plastic bottles, or store or heat food in plastic containers. Swap plastic cutting boards, utensils and containers for wood, glass or stainless steel; replace non-stick pans with stainless steel or cast iron; use a water filter; ditch cling wrap and single-use plastics; and wear less synthetic clothing. “The main one is to de-plastify your kitchen,” says Thomas. “The other one is regular vacuuming to keep your dust load in your house down. It’s not just the plastics that are there, but the chemicals associated with plastics. Keeping the dust load down has been shown to reduce your exposure to those chemicals as well.” Make the most of your health, relationships, fitness and nutrition with our Live Well newsletter. Get it in your inbox every Monday.

World.title: Path clears for next stage of $807m Royal Perth Hospital expansion
World.content:
NationalWAHealth Path clears for next stage of $807m Royal Perth Hospital expansion Indigo Lemay-Conway September 16, 2026 — 4:05pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Western Australia’s planning commission has approved an application for the next stage of works on a new emergency department at Royal Perth Hospital. The new works would see the construction of a nine-storey hospital building (S Block), a three-storey enclosed link structure between S Block and the existing R Block, emergency and vehicle access and public realm improvements. Artist impression of the new nine-storey emergency department building at Royal Perth Hospital. This is in addition to stage 1 of the $807.3 million expansion of the hospital, which began on June 19 and included the construction of the concrete slab, lift and stair cores, vehicle access ramps from Wellington Street and Moore Street. Deputy alliance manager for the Perth Pulse Alliance, Dion Di Crescenzo told the WAPC on Wednesday that the expansion is the largest redevelopment of the hospital site in recent history.



“Driven out of the urgent need for an upgraded emergency department, the project is now the catalyst for expanded hospital capacity and the future redevelopment works within the hospital and the wider precinct,” he said. Related Article Planning and development Green light for $10 million Fast Eddys replacement, with hopes for a Reuben on the menu “The project is highly complex with an accelerated delivery timeframe, and this is one of the reasons that the alliance delivery model has been chosen by the government to deliver the project. “It gives us the ability to work collaboratively and efficiently with a wide array of stakeholders.” Di Crescenzo said things have been moving well on site and foundation works are well underway.



In November 2025, the State Government committed to a staged redevelopment of the RPH precinct to address operational constraints within the existing emergency department and respond to forecast growth in demand. The application is made by the Department of Housing and Works on behalf of the Perth Pulse Alliance (the Alliance) and the Office of Major Infrastructure Delivery. Artist impression of the new emergency department expansion at Royal Perth Hospital. The new emergency department will be located on the north-western end of the hospital campus on Wellington Street in the Perth CBD, about 500 metres from the site’s current ED. Level one of the nine-storey building will include Priority 2 ambulance access from Moore Street, 10 ambulance parking bays, approximately 34 staff car parking bays, ambulance amenities, storerooms, staff end-of-trip facilities, switch and control rooms, and a commercial tenancy space.



The main emergency department will be on Level 2 and will include public entry, reception and triage, Priority 1 ambulance access from Wellington Street, six ambulance holding bays, resuscitation, imaging, fast-track area, and general acute/sub-acute clinical spaces. An ambulatory care unit, home hospital unit, emergency Department administration, mental health short-stay unit, emergency Department short-stay unit, and courtyard will be on Level 3 while Level 4 contains the cardiac investigation unit and coronary care unit. Level 5 will be a dedicated plant floor and Level 6 will be the general surgical inpatient unit and cardiology inpatient unit. Two acute medical inpatient units will be on Level 7, a roof plant will be on Level 8 and Level 9 will be the lift overrun. The three-storey enclosed link between the new building and the existing R Block will provide staff, patient and public circulation on Levels 2, 3 and 4.



There are also 23 short-term parking bays included in the application for emergency department patients and visitors. Health Infrastructure Minister John Carey said at the commencement of stage 1 works that the project is expected to be finished by 2028. WAPC commissioner Bianca Sandri threw her support behind the new application. “I think this is a much-needed piece of infrastructure that’s required at RPH, and certainly, I think a lot of work’s gone through design review on the application,” she said. Similarly, commissioner Paul Lakey described the project as a “major milestone in the life of the hospital.”



“I think we sat here a while ago and approved stage one, and the process that has happened with the proponent and the government and the agencies and the department has been very, very collaborative, and I’m so pleased to see all agencies working together,” he said. The application was carried unanimously.

World.title: Thousands of Queensland cops join Palmer-backed vaccine lawsuit
World.content:
NationalQueenslandCoronavirus pandemic Thousands of Queensland cops join Palmer-backed vaccine lawsuit Cameron Atfield September 16, 2026 — 4:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

More than 3100 law enforcement personnel and staff have signed on to a Clive Palmer-funded class action against the Queensland Police Service over a COVID-era vaccination mandate, with the law firm behind the action making a final appeal for others to join. Sibley Lawyers director Justin Sibley, whose firm represented current and former QPS employees, said there were potentially thousands more who could come forward before the Friday deadline. “At the time the vaccination mandate was introduced in September 2021, there were around 18,000 QPS employees, meaning a significant number of people may potentially be eligible to participate in this class action,” he said. Queensland police during the COVID pandemic. Chris Hyde/Getty Images “Given our experience protecting frontline workers since mandates began, I’m not surprised by the number of police and staff vaccinated under duress. Hopefully everyone who is eligible will come forward, and those that haven’t still have time.”



Palmer, through his mining company Mineralogy, was funding the class action. The mandates were a contentious requirement during the pandemic, but health authorities declared them to be scientifically justified. Unlike many in the community, police officers were considered essential workers and, as such, were able to move more freely during the COVID lockdowns. Then-police commissioner Katarina Carroll introduced the mandate, which was to last five months, in September 2021. “The dynamic nature of policing means frontline officers interact with large volumes of people and move around to all corners of the state,” she said at the time.



“It is important the Queensland community has confidence and feel safe when interacting with their police. “While we respect individual choice and we will engage closely with our members as we implement the directive, our overwhelming obligation is to ensure we have safe workplaces and a safe community.” Former Queensland Police Service commissioner Katarina Carroll introduced the mandate in 2021. Matt Dennien Officers and staff who did not comply faced suspension without pay and, potentially, the loss of their jobs. Other government employees, such as teachers, faced similar mandates. However, when the Palaszczuk government lifted those mandates in June 2022, the QPS mandate remained in place as it was a commissioner’s directive, not a government mandate.



The QPS directive was revoked that December. In February 2024, Supreme Court Justice Glenn Martin found the QPS directive was unlawful under the Human Rights Act. Rather than ruling that workplace vaccination requirements themselves were inherently illegal, Martin found the directive unlawful because Carroll failed to properly consider human rights advice during the decision-making process. Sibley said the episode had turned police “against each other” and had damaged the QPS’s strong cultural bond. “Many police and staff complied with the directions because the alternative was to be suspended without pay and then terminated,” he said.



“Police and staff, many with years of experience and exemplary service records, had their pay cut off just before Christmas of 2021. Those who had held out briefly could see that the threat of suspension without pay was real. “The reality was that many employees who had legitimate medical advice not to be vaccinated were refused applications for exemptions.” Sibley said the majority of class action participants nominated that they were in the “vaccine coercion group” – officers and staff employed between September 7, 2021, and December 12, 2022, who received jabs after the relevant directions were issued, but would not otherwise have received those doses. Almost 200 had nominated the “vaccine refusal group”, which included those who refused vaccinations altogether and were liable to disciplinary action. Sibley said others had nominated for the “refused medical exemption group”, whose applications for medical exemptions were refused.



“The class action is now at an important stage, with a September 18 deadline for people to either opt in or opt out of the class action,” he said. A QPS spokeswoman said the service would be unable to provide comment “due to pending proceedings”. World.title: ‘An attack on me’: Brisbane agent fights to keep licence
World.content:
A prominent Brisbane real estate agent convicted of an overseas assault is fighting in court to get his licence reinstated, claiming his business is suffering as others stand to gain financially from his downfall. Last year Tony O’Doherty, formerly the principal at McGrath Bulimba, pleaded guilty and received a two-year fully suspended sentence for a 2013 one-punch assault on a man outside a nightclub in Ireland. The victim suffered a fractured skull and a bleed to his brain. Tony O’Doherty speaking outside court. Cloe Read O’Doherty’s legal team are appealing against a decision by the Office of Fair Trading to cancel his licence.



Under the Property Occupations Act 2014, a person is considered unsuitable to hold a real estate licence if they were convicted within the previous five years, regardless of when the conduct occurred. Justice Soraya Ryan on Wednesday heard arguments from O’Doherty’s barrister, Rob Anderson KC, who said there was urgency in the case, given the agent’s livelihood had been curtailed by the automatic termination of his licence. Anderson put forward arguments around the interpretation of the law, including whether a foreign offence should be included under Queensland law. He told the court there was no option in the Irish criminal justice system to not record convictions, whereas under Queensland law, a judge would consider aspects of a defendant’s life, such as their occupation. He said the impact on O’Doherty’s real estate licence was not considered by the Irish judge.



Barrister Angus Scott KC, representing the Department of Justice, said the law was in place to protect the community and consumers. “The ultimate point we make throughout this legislation is it is concerned with the protection of the community,” he said, adding that the criteria under the law considered whether the offence involved violence. Speaking outside court, O’Doherty said the loss of his licence had had a detrimental impact on his business, and the McGrath team were hopeful it would be short term. “It is an incredible attack on the business, and I’m going to go against my legal advice and say that this is an attack on me,” he said. “It is an attack. Let’s just say other people stand to gain commercially and financially by my downfall, and they have not been silent.”



O’Doherty said he took full responsibility for what happened more than a decade ago, saying he made a poor decision. He said there had been an altercation, and he wished it never happened. “I think a lot of the media’s coverage hasn’t been in its entirety, and it never is,” he said. “The night in question was by no means a brutal attack, which is what the headlines have been. I’m not condoning my behaviour.” He questioned how many other people with criminal convictions were operating in the real estate industry after cases the media had not covered. The Limerick Post reported that O’Doherty was at the Club Mission nightclub in Newcastle West when the victim, James Fitzgerald, threw a glass over his shoulder, which smashed near O’Doherty and splashed a drink on him.



Fitzgerald, who was severely drunk at the time, was removed from the nightclub by security. O’Doherty ran after Fitzgerald and confronted him, hitting him in the jaw. He was sent backwards and banged his head into a door, according to the Limerick Post. Ryan reserved her decision for a later date. Get alerts on significant breaking news as happens.

World.title: A Looney Tunes live action long in the making, plus other new movies to watch this week
World.content:
(PG) 103 minutes

It all began in 1990 with an inspired piece of comic writing in the Shouts and Murmurs section of The New Yorker.

Humorist Ian Frazier dreamed up a court case starring Looney Tunes’ Wile E. Coyote as the plaintiff in a suit against Acme, the fictional manufacturer of the many specialised products the hapless predator had tried in his eternal pursuit of the Road Runner. The list included “itching powder, giant kites, Burmese tiger traps, anvils and two hundred-foot rubber bands” and the injuries to Mr Coyote caused by these dubious purchases had been serious enough to be “a major impediment” to his social life.

Will Forte as lawyer Kevin Avery and Wile E. Coyote, voiced by Eric Bauza, in Coyote vs Acme. Ketchup Entertainment via AP

This sparked strong interest from Looney Tunes’ studio, Warner Bros, and shooting eventually began on a film that mixed animation with live action in the manner of the 1988 hit Who Framed Roger Rabbit. The studio’s animation division struck hard times before the film could be released and management decided it should join Batgirl, among other animated films it was shelving at the time as tax write-offs.
